`CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(plugify-port LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)
endif()

# Shared SDK: plg headers (plugify-module-cpp, API v3), generated s2sdk bindings, plugin_export.h, nlohmann/json
add_library(plugify_sdk INTERFACE)
target_include_directories(plugify_sdk INTERFACE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include")

# s2sdk binding globals (__s2sdk_*), compiled into every plugin that links s2sdk_bindings
add_library(s2sdk_bindings OBJECT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include/s2sdk/s2sdk.cpp")
target_link_libraries(s2sdk_bindings PUBLIC plugify_sdk)
target_compile_definitions(s2sdk_bindings PUBLIC _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1)

# permissions (official plugify-plugin-permissions 1.3.1) binding globals (__permissions_*)
add_library(permissions_bindings OBJECT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include/permissions/permissions.cpp")
target_link_libraries(permissions_bindings PUBLIC plugify_sdk)
target_compile_definitions(permissions_bindings PUBLIC _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1)

# polyhook (official plugify-plugin-polyhook 2.5.6) binding globals (__polyhook_*)
add_library(polyhook_bindings OBJECT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include/polyhook/polyhook.cpp")
target_link_libraries(polyhook_bindings PUBLIC plugify_sdk)
target_compile_definitions(polyhook_bindings PUBLIC _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1)

# hudmenu (plugins/hudmenu) binding globals (__hudmenu_*). pisexcompat resolves every displayed
# menu type through these; it PUBLIC-links this object library, so every pisexcompat consumer
# (plugins/admin_system, plugins/as_*, the tests) gets the globals automatically - the plugin
# .so then exports them (version script "__hudmenu_*") and its manifest declares the optional
# hudmenu dependency, which is what makes the plugify module fill them.
add_library(hudmenu_bindings OBJECT "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include/hudmenu/hudmenu.cpp")
target_link_libraries(hudmenu_bindings PUBLIC plugify_sdk)
target_compile_definitions(hudmenu_bindings PUBLIC _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1)

add_subdirectory(libs/plgdb)
add_subdirectory(libs/pisexcompat)


# Every plugin directory with a CMakeLists.txt is built (plugins/<name>). A plugin may add test
# executables named *_tests with RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/tests" (run by test.sh).
file(GLOB _plugin_dirs LIST_DIRECTORIES true "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/plugins/*")
list(SORT _plugin_dirs)
foreach(_d ${_plugin_dirs})
    if(EXISTS "${_d}/CMakeLists.txt")
        add_subdirectory(${_d})
    endif()
endforeach()

option(PLUGIFY_PORT_TESTS "Build tests" ON)
if(PLUGIFY_PORT_TESTS)
    if(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests")
        add_subdirectory(tests)
    endif()
endif()

```

`README.md`:

```md
# cs2ac (Plugify)

CS2AC fork v11 (Metamod CS2AC 1.0.14 + packages v3-v11) - server-side anti-cheat for Counter-Strike 2 by karola3vax, ported from its Metamod:Source plugin to Plugify/s2sdk. Watches the usercmds, movement, aim, shot, input-history and settings data players send to the server and reports and punishes 18 detection categories (aimbot, aimlock, antiaim, autostrafe, bhop, dll injection, desubticking, doubletap, hyperscroll, inhuman accuracy, invalid cvar, invalid input, irregular behavior, namechanger, nulls, silentaim, subtick spam, triggerbot) plus the fork's report-only BACKTRACK, TICK MANIPULATION, INTERP BACKTRACK, MOUSE MISMATCH, TRIGGER PATTERN and RCS telemetry. Usercmd and movement data come from polyhook detours on the gamedata-resolved libserver.so functions, everything else from s2sdk (events, net messages, client cvars, schema). Bans are queued through the optional admin_system API (falling back to the configured command); kicks use the configured kick command. Configuration and translations are the fork's cs2ac.cfg and translations/<lang>.txt. Administrator commands: cs2ac_status, cs2ac_help, cs2ac_reload, cs2ac_check_config, cs2ac_test_announcement, cs2ac_webhook_test, cs2ac_config_loaded, plus the diagnostics cs2ac_hooks and cs2ac_usercmd_dump. Reports go to the server console, chat, center screen, a configurable admin-plugin ban/kick command, the JSONL detection log and an optional Discord webhook. Known port limitations (see PORT_PLAN.md and FORK_SYNC.md): the auto-updater is not ported, the DLL Injection detector stays off unless its vtable index is verified in gamedata, and the usercmd protobuf reader reports through cs2ac_usercmd_dump so it can be confirmed on a live server.

Plugify port (fork) of **CS2AC** by karola3vax (Metamod (C++)).
Original: https://github.com/karola3vax/CS2AC
The code was rewritten for Plugify / s2sdk; behaviour follows the original.

## Requirements
- [Plugify](https://github.com/untrustedmodders/plugify) with [s2sdk](https://github.com/untrustedmodders/plugify-plugin-s2sdk)
- Plugify dependencies: s2sdk, polyhook, admin_system (optional)

## Installation
Download `cs2ac-1.1.0.zip` from Releases and extract it into `game/csgo/`.

## Building
Requires Docker. `./build.sh` builds in the Steam Runtime 3 (sniper) SDK image; the package
is written to `build/package/cs2ac`.

`plugins/admin_system` carry only the API headers of the plugins this one uses.

## License
AGPL-3.0 (as the original), see LICENSE.


```

`build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Builds the plugin in the Steam Runtime 3 (sniper) SDK image and packages it into build/package.
# Usage: ./build.sh
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
docker build -q -t plugify-plugin-builder "$ROOT/docker" >/dev/null
docker run --rm -u "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$ROOT":/src -w /src --entrypoint bash plugify-plugin-builder -c '
set -e
cmake -S /src -B /src/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=gcc-14 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=g++-14 \
      -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DPLUGIFY_PORT_TESTS=OFF >/dev/null
ninja -C /src/build'
for p in "$ROOT"/plugins/*/package.sh; do bash "$p"; done

```

`docker/Dockerfile`:

```
FROM registry.gitlab.steamos.cloud/steamrt/sniper/sdk:latest
RUN apt-get update -qq && V=1:10.5.23-0+deb11u1 \
 && apt-get install -y -qq --allow-downgrades mariadb-common=$V libmariadb3=$V libmariadb-dev=$V ninja-build >/dev/null \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

```

`libs/pisexcompat/CMakeLists.txt`:

```txt
# pisexcompat — re-creates the subset of the Pisex "utils" (IUtilsApi), "menus" (IMenusApi) and
# "players" (IPlayersApi) APIs that the cs2-admin_system core its modules use, on top of s2sdk.
#
# Static library: linked into each ported plugin together with the s2sdk binding globals, so the
# plugin itself only has to link `pisexcompat`.
#
# See README.md for the inventory table (which Pisex method is used how often) and for the list of
# behaviours that are intentionally different from the Metamod originals.

file(GLOB PISEXCOMPAT_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp")
add_library(pisexcompat STATIC ${PISEXCOMPAT_SOURCES})

target_include_directories(pisexcompat PUBLIC "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include")
# hudmenu_bindings: the library resolves each displayed menu's s2sdk type name through
# __hudmenu_GetClientMenuType when the hudmenu plugin is installed; PUBLIC so every consumer
# (and the tests) gets the globals exactly like s2sdk_bindings.
target_link_libraries(pisexcompat PUBLIC plugify_sdk s2sdk_bindings hudmenu_bindings)
target_compile_definitions(pisexcompat PUBLIC _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1)
# The generated plg/s2sdk headers are not ours to fix; keep their warnings out of -Werror.
target_include_directories(pisexcompat SYSTEM PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include")
target_compile_options(pisexcompat PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow -Werror -fvisibility=hidden)

# Timer-registry test: installs fake s2sdk timer bindings (the globals are only null until a fake
# is assigned) and drives the real Create/Remove/Process/OnFire code - the paths whose bugs made
# the server watchdog-fatal (a repeat timer with delay 0 loops forever inside one RunFrame
# call) or leaked/use-after-freed timers. Lives under build/tests so ./test.sh picks it up.
add_executable(pisexcompat_timers_tests test/timers_engine_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(pisexcompat_timers_tests PRIVATE pisexcompat s2sdk_bindings -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc)
target_include_directories(pisexcompat_timers_tests SYSTEM PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include")
target_compile_options(pisexcompat_timers_tests PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Werror)
set_target_properties(pisexcompat_timers_tests PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/tests")

# Player-wrapper test: fake client bindings + the map lifecycle gate. Covers the crash cases
# (SetClientName on a clientless slot, any client query during the map shutdown) and asserts that
# a slot without a client/controller never reaches s2sdk. Runs from ../test.sh.
add_executable(pisexcompat_players_tests test/players_engine_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(pisexcompat_players_tests PRIVATE pisexcompat s2sdk_bindings -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc)
target_include_directories(pisexcompat_players_tests SYSTEM PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include")
target_compile_options(pisexcompat_players_tests PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Werror)
set_target_properties(pisexcompat_players_tests PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/tests")

# Command-registration test: fake s2sdk command manager, drives the real CommandTrampoline.
# Covers RegServerCommand (no ClientCanExecute, no caller slot reaches the handler, server-only
# wins over a duplicate RegCommand) and that RegCommand keeps its client-executable flags.
# Runs from ../test.sh.
add_executable(pisexcompat_commands_tests test/commands_engine_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(pisexcompat_commands_tests PRIVATE pisexcompat s2sdk_bindings -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc)
target_include_directories(pisexcompat_commands_tests SYSTEM PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include")
target_compile_options(pisexcompat_commands_tests PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Werror)
set_target_properties(pisexcompat_commands_tests PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/tests")

# Menu test: fake s2sdk menu manager, counts CreateMenu/DestroyMenu. Covers the documented rule
# "always destroy your menus from the handler's End case" (deferred out of the handler, exactly
# once, never while another client still shows the menu). Runs from ../test.sh.
add_executable(pisexcompat_menu_tests test/menu_engine_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(pisexcompat_menu_tests PRIVATE pisexcompat s2sdk_bindings -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc)
target_include_directories(pisexcompat_menu_tests SYSTEM PRIVATE "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/sdk/include")
target_compile_options(pisexcompat_menu_tests PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Werror)
set_target_properties(pisexcompat_menu_tests PROPERTIES RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/tests")

# Integration check: build one real plugin .so against the library, so ./build.sh's ABI report
# covers a consumer of pisexcompat (GLIBC <= 2.31, no libstdc++/libmariadb NEEDED). It is not part
# of any package - the file name makes that obvious.
option(PISEXCOMPAT_SMOKE_PLUGIN "Build the pisexcompat link/ABI smoke plugin" ON)
if(PISEXCOMPAT_SMOKE_PLUGIN)
    add_library(pisexcompat_smoke_plugin SHARED test/smoke_plugin.cpp)
    target_link_libraries(pisexcompat_smoke_plugin PRIVATE pisexcompat -static-libstdc++ -static-libgcc)
    target_compile_options(pisexcompat_smoke_plugin PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Werror)
    # Same definitions a real plugin sets (see plugins/perm_connector/CMakeLists.txt).
    target_compile_definitions(pisexcompat_smoke_plugin PRIVATE
        _GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1 PLUGIFY_MODULE="pisexcompat_smoke" PLUGIFY_IS_DEBUG=0 PLUGIFY_IS_RELEASE=1)
    set_target_properties(pisexcompat_smoke_plugin PROPERTIES OUTPUT_NAME pisexcompat_smoke)
endif()

```

`libs/pisexcompat/README.md`:

```md
# pisexcompat — the Pisex utils/menus/players API on top of s2sdk

A static library that re-creates the parts of the Pisex "utils" (`IUtilsApi`), "menus"
(`IMenusApi`) and "players" (`IPlayersApi`) APIs that the Pisex admin core and its 17
modules actually call, so that porting one of them is a near-mechanical edit:

```cpp
#include <pisex/pisex.hpp>
using namespace pisex;                 // g_pUtils / g_pMenus / g_pPlayers

plg::PluginResult OnPluginStart() {
    pisex::Init("admin_system");       // dirs + s2sdk listeners; never fails hard
    g_pUtils->StartupServer(StartupServer);   // runs on the first update with a map
    return plg::PluginResult::Success; // never Failed: that stops every plugify plugin
}
plg::PluginResult OnPluginUpdate(std::chrono::milliseconds) { pisex::Poll(); return plg::PluginResult::Continue; }
plg::PluginResult OnPluginEnd() { pisex::Shutdown(); return plg::PluginResult::Success; }
```

Everything runs on the game thread. No exception escapes into s2sdk callbacks (all of them are
wrapped), and nothing touches a client before a map exists — see *Safety* below.

Files: `src/*.cpp`, `include/pisex/*.hpp`. Tests: `tests/pisexcompat_tests.cpp` (`./test.sh`).

---

## 1. Inventory: which Pisex methods are used, and how often

Counted over the Pisex admin core and its modules (`g_pUtils*`,
`g_pMenus*`, `g_pPlayers*`, including the `…Api` aliases the modules use). "Status" says what
pisexcompat does with it.

### IUtilsApi (`g_pUtils->`)

| Calls | Method | Status in pisexcompat |
|---:|---|---|
| 118 | `PrintToChat(slot, fmt, ...)` | `pisex::PrintToChat` — colour tags, HUD_PRINTTALK |
| 70 | `PrintToConsole(slot, fmt, ...)` | `pisex::PrintToConsole` — negative slot → server console |
| 63 | `ErrorLog(fmt, ...)` | `pisex::ErrorLog` — plugify log + `<logs>/error_MM-DD-YYYY.txt` |
| 56 | `PrintToChatAll(fmt, ...)` | `pisex::PrintToChatAll` |
| 38 | `RegCommand(console, chat, cb)` | `pisex::RegCommand` (plugin id dropped) |
| 18 | `GetCGlobalVars()` | `GetCGlobalVars()` — snapshot struct, refreshed every `Poll()` |
| 18 | `GetCGameEntitySystem()` | returns `nullptr` (no engine layout in s2sdk) — use `pisex/schema.hpp` |
| 18 | `GetCEntitySystem()` | returns `nullptr` (same) |
| 17 | `StartupServer(fn)` | deferred to the first `Poll()` (map up) |
| 14 | `CreateTimer(fl, fn)` | `CreateTimer` over s2sdk timers, return value = next delay |
| 7 | `SetStateChanged(ent, cls, field)` | `pisex::SetStateChanged` (schema network update) |
| 4 | `HookEvent(name, cb)` | `pisex::HookEvent` (s2sdk pre hook) |
| 3 | `TeleportEntity(ent, …)` | not covered — entity work, use s2sdk `TeleportClient`/entity functions |
| 3 | `RemoveEntity(ent)` | not covered — use s2sdk `RemoveEntity` |
| 2 | `PrintToCenter(slot, fmt, …)` | `pisex::PrintToCenter` |
| 2 | `AddChatListenerPre(cb)` | `pisex::AddChatListenerPre` (see the chat caveat in §4) |
| 1 | `PrintToCenterAll`, `PrintToAlert`, `NextFrame`, `LoadTranslations`, `GetLanguage` | all covered |
| 1 | `HookIsHearingClient(cb)` | not covered (voice hook, polyhook territory) |
| 1 | `DispatchSpawn`, `CreateEntityByName`, `AcceptEntityInput` | not covered — s2sdk entity functions |

Modelled but unused by the admin core (kept because cs2-menus exposes them and modules may grow):
`PrintToConsoleAll`, `PrintToCenterHtml{All}`, `PrintToAlertAll`, `LogToFile`, `MapStartHook`,
`MapEndHook`, `RemoveTimer`, `GetVersion`.

### IMenusApi (`g_pMenus->`)

| Calls | Method | Status |
|---:|---|---|
| 133 | `AddItemMenu(menu, back, text, iType)` | `pisex::AddItemMenu` (ITEM_HIDE dropped, ITEM_DISABLED → s2sdk Disabled) |
| 40 | `SetTitleMenu` | covered |
| 40 | `SetExitMenu` | covered → s2sdk exit button (digit 0 / cancel reason Exit) |
| 40 | `DisplayPlayerMenu(menu, slot[, bClose[, bReset]])` | covered (both overloads) |
| 38 | `SetCallback(menu, fn)` | covered — `std::function` kept on our side, keyed per slot |
| 36 | `SetBackMenu` | covered → s2sdk exit-back button (cancel reason ExitBack) |
| 11 | `ClosePlayerMenu(slot)` | covered (no callback, like Pisex) |
| 5 | `escapeString(str)` | covered — byte-identical to cs2-menus |

Not covered (Panorama-only in Pisex): `AddToggleMenu`, `AddSelectMenu`, `AddSelectOption`,
`SetToggleState`/`GetToggleState`, `SetSelectedOption`, `AddSelectMenu` item refs, `ItemKind`
rendering, `SetDescriptionMenu` (stored, never rendered), `AddRawItemMenu` (covered).

**Menu type selection** (`GetMenuType`/`SetMenuType`): each displayed menu resolves its s2sdk
type through `pisex::ResolveS2sdkMenuTypeName` — an explicit `SetMenuType(slot, ...)` override
wins; otherwise, when the hudmenu plugin is installed, its exported `GetClientMenuType(slot)`
(the player's own `!menu` choice from the permissions cookie `Utils.MenuType`, Pisex numbering)
decides; without hudmenu the slot's Pisex `MenuType` is mapped: `HUD_LAYOUT` → `hud` and
`CENTER_WASD` → `wasd` when the matching hudmenu backend is registered, else `button` (or
`chat`/`centerhtml` for the digit types). `SetDefaultMenuType` resets every slot (and clears the
overrides, like the Pisex original that replaced the whole table); `IsMenuTypeForced(slot)`
reports whether a slot carries an override.

`pisex::Init(name)` sets `<configs>/<name>` (and `<configs>/<name>/translations`) as the base
dirs; the resolvers also strip the Metamod spellings (`addons/configs/<x>/…`,
`addons/translations/…`, `addons/data/…`), so ported loaders keep their old paths.

One-line-per-function reference of the free functions (the `*Api` methods are thin forwarders):
see the header comments — every declaration carries a doc comment explaining the Pisex semantics
it preserves.

## 3. How the s2sdk side is wired (verified against `libplugify-plugin-s2sdk.so`)

* **Chat commands** — `ConCommandManager::DispatchConCommand` special-cases `say`/`say_team`: a
  first argument starting with a trigger from the s2sdk settings (`PublicChatTrigger` `"!"`,
  `SilentChatTrigger` `"/"`) is stripped, the rest tokenised and dispatched as a *command* with
  `ConCommandContext::Chat`; a silent-trigger message (or one whose handler returns
  `Handled`/`Stop`) is then not broadcast. `args[0]` is the command name, `caller` is `-1` for the
  server console.
  `RegCommand` therefore strips the trigger from the chat names and registers the bare name via
  `AddConsoleCommand`; a console name is only dispatched for console input and a chat name only
  for chat input (like Pisex). `RegServerCommand` registers a console name the same way but
  without `ClientCanExecute` (the Metamod `CON_COMMAND_F(..., FCVAR_NONE)` behaviour): a call from
  any caller slot is swallowed before the callback runs. The callback receives the
  **registered spelling** as `arg[0]`
  (`"!ban 3 60"`, `"mm_admin"`) plus the arguments, space-joined — so ported handlers that
  `Tokenize()` the content and compare `arg[0]` keep working unchanged.
* **Menus** — `MenuHandlerCallback` is a plain function pointer called as
  `(MenuId, MenuAction, playerSlot, param)`: `Select` passes the 0-based item index, `Cancel`
  passes the `MenuCancelReason`, then `End` follows. pisexcompat keeps the `std::function`
  callback and the item list on its side, keyed by the slot, and translates:
  `Select` → Pisex item number `index - GetClientMenuOffset(slot) + 1` (1..5, page size set to 5
  with `SetMenuPagination`), `Cancel(Exit)` → `("exit","exit",9)`, `Cancel(ExitBack)` →
  `("back","back",7)`; timeouts/disconnects drop the menu without calling back (Pisex's own
  behaviour). s2sdk's page turn (digits 8/9) is handled by its backend and does **not** call the
  Pisex callback (Pisex notified `("next","next",8)`/`("back","back",7)` for those).
  **Destroying the menu is our job**: the menus guide ("always destroy your menus … call
  `DestroyMenu(id)` from your handler's `End` case — otherwise every menu you display leaks for
  the lifetime of the plugin") and s2sdk's `EndClientMenu()` (which only clears the client state)
  make a display that ends on its own — exit button, timeout (default 60 s), disconnect — leak its
  `MenuData` for the process lifetime unless we destroy it. Since `DestroyMenu` from inside the handler
  would re-enter the handler (Cancel + End for every viewer while the outer call is still on the
  stack), `Cancel`/`End` only *queue* the id (`QueueMenuDestroy`); `Poll()` →
  `ProcessMenuRequests()` calls `s2sdk::DestroyMenu` outside the lock, exactly once per session
  (Cancel and End both report the same end and are deduped), and only when no other client still
  displays that id (s2sdk menus are shared objects — such an id stays queued and is re-checked, it
  is not dropped). A display that s2sdk refused, and a menu created before an exception, are
  destroyed on the spot. `CloseAllMenus()` (map end / `Shutdown()`) destroys the open *and* the
  queued ids, so `plg reload` leaves neither `MenuData` nor handlers pointing into unloaded code.
  In the map-change window it ends a displayed session through `CancelClientMenu(slot, Disconnect)`
  instead of `DestroyMenu(id)`: destroy cancels the viewer through the menu type backend
  (`PrintHtmlCentre`, hudmenu's `HideForSlot`) - a client/entity call that window forbids - while
  s2sdk's disconnect path skips the backend close, clears the manager state and runs our handler,
  which only queues the (then viewerless) destroy.
* **Timers** — created with `TimerFlag::Repeat`, delayed/rescheduled from `Poll()`. The engine's
  `TimerSystem::RunFrame` invokes the callback while holding its own lock and is not re-entrant,
  so the callback only *records* the delay the Pisex function returned; `Poll()` then calls
  `RescheduleTimer` (or `KillsTimer` for a negative return). A timer that is waiting for that
  reschedule ignores further fires, so a callback never runs twice in one frame.
  **Every delay handed to s2sdk is floored at one server tick** (`pisex::kMinTimerDelay`, 1/64 s,
  see `ClampTimerDelay` in `pisex/timers.hpp`) — at creation *and* on every reschedule. The s2sdk
  backend re-inserts a repeating timer at `universalTime + stored delay` inside a `while` loop, so
  a stored 0 makes it run the callback forever within a single frame ("Server took too long to
  process" FATAL); Pisex's "return 0 = next frame" therefore
  becomes one tick. s2sdk's timer ids start at 0, and id 0 is tracked/killed like any other (the
  "id != 0" guard the old code had broke the first timer of the process). A callback that returns
  a negative value stops the timer: `Poll()` kills the engine timer, so no engine-side zombie
  remains. `RemoveTimer()` is legal from inside the timer's own callback — the object is freed
  after the callback returns, not while it is on the stack. **While no map is up the callback is
  not called at all**: the fire is marked postponed, further engine fires are ignored, and the
  timer is re-armed with one tick on the first ready frame (so the callback runs as early as the
  engine can again, but with a live map). The delay the callback returns then governs the
  following runs, exactly like Pisex's semantics.
  *Map end, checked in cs2-menus:* there is no map-end timer cleanup there at all (the plugin
  clears its menu state per slot, the `g_timers` vector keeps running across map changes) —
  and the admin core's one-second timer that expires punishments/admins relies on that. So
  pisexcompat also leaves timers running across maps (s2sdk's `TimerFlag::NoMapChange` is
  deliberately **not** set) and only `Shutdown()` kills them. `RemoveTimer` on an already-dead
  handle is a safe no-op (Pisex freed the object, so ported cleanup code calls it on dead handles).
* **Events** — `HookEvent(..., HookMode::Pre)` (the engine's pre-fire point, which is where
  cs2-menus' `FireEvent` SourceHook called the plugins). One trampoline fans out by event name.
* **Chat listeners** — `AddCommandListener("say"/"say_team", …, Pre)`.
* **NextFrame** — drained by `Poll()` instead of `QueueTaskForNextFrame`, and only while a map is
  up (a "next frame" during a map change would be a ready frame, like the postponed timers): the
  callback is a
  `std::function` that cannot cross the `plg::vector<plg::any>` boundary of an s2sdk task, and
  the plugin already has one per-frame pump (`OnPluginUpdate`) where its deferred work runs in a
  predictable order (next-frame callbacks first, then timer reschedules, then queued menu
  changes). The practical timing is the same as Pisex's own queue (`Menus::GameFrame`).
* **Map lifecycle** — `OnMapStart`/`OnMapEnd` s2sdk listeners drive `IsGameReady()`. It is false
  from the map end until the **next map start** (`Poll()` alone is not enough: the host can pump
  updates throughout a changelevel), so the whole [map end, next map start] window answers
  defaults. Map-start callbacks run from the first ready `Poll()` after the map starts (so client
  queries inside them are safe); map end only drops our own state and ends open menu sessions
  through s2sdk's menu manager (no s2sdk client/entity call from a map-end callback). A plugin
  that was loaded into an already running map (no map end seen yet) becomes ready on its first
  update - the host pumps `OnPluginUpdate` from `ServerPostSimulate`, which only runs with a map
  up. While not ready: timers and `NextFrame`
  callbacks are **postponed** to the first ready frame (see below), events are still delivered
  (data only) but every client/entity lookup they make answers a default.

## 4. Safety rules this library enforces

* **No client query before a map (or during a map change)** — `pisex::IsGameReady()` is false
  until the first ready `Poll()` and again from every `OnMapEnd` until the next `OnMapStart`.
  Every player wrapper and every printer checks it, so a plugin that calls
  `g_pPlayers->GetSteamID64(i)` in `OnPluginStart` gets `0` instead of a dead server, and a timer
  that fires during a map change cannot touch a stale slot. `StartupServer`/`MapStartHook`
  callbacks are deferred for the same reason. s2sdk's client list is *gone* in that window:
  `utils::GetClientBySlot` reads the half-destroyed server and segfaults at address 0 (a crash seen
  in a ported plugin's MapEnd handler), and `Player::SetName` (SetClientName) dereferences a null
  client and a null controller (a crash seen right after a map start), so pisexcompat makes no
  s2sdk client call at all then - the menu layer ends its sessions through the manager and never
  lets `DestroyMenu` cancel a viewer in that window (§3).
* **Every player wrapper validates the slot** — beyond the map gate they use
  `pisex::IsClientReady(slot)` (public helper): slot in range, `IsClientConnected`, and the
  controller entity exists. `SetPlayerName`/`GetPlayerName` require the controller (the crash
  above); `GetIpAddress` additionally refuses fake clients (`Player::GetIpAddress` dereferences a
  net channel that bots do not have); `GetSteamID64`/`GetSteamID` answer `0`/`""` for a slot
  without a client instead of s2sdk's stale `m_unauthenticatedSteamID`; the pawn/controller
  accessors (`GetPlayerHealth`, `GetPlayerTeam`, `Teleport`, `ChangeTeam`, …) are only called for
  a slot that passes the guard, which also removes their "invalid player slot" log spam. s2sdk's
  `"<unknown>"` name placeholder becomes an empty string, like the Pisex API returned.
* **No entity query before a map either** — every `pisex/schema.hpp` accessor (and
  `FindEntityByClassname`, `DisplayPlayerMenu`) checks `IsGameReady()` as well. s2sdk's entity
  exports dereference `g_pGameEntitySystem` (and the menu path `gpGlobals`) without a null check;
  s2sdk only fills them in on server start, so a pre-map call is a null dereference, i.e. a dead
  server. Before the first map there are no entities to query, so the wrappers return their
  defaults.
* **Schema access stays off the map-start path** (porting rule, not enforced): s2sdk's *typed*
  schema calls can dereference an invalid `CSchemaType*` (-1) for a class whose schema table the
  engine built around a map load; the first typed access of that class, one frame after the map
  load, crashes. Use `pisex::SchemaOffset()` + s2sdk's raw
  `GetEntData2`/`SetEntData2` with the field's real width (as `plugins/fortnite_emotes` does) for
  anything on that path. `pisex::SchemaChainOffset()` normalises "no chainer"/"no binding" to -1
  (never 0, which s2sdk would read as a real chain offset).
* **No exceptions across the boundary** — every s2sdk callback (`CommandTrampoline`,
  `ChatTrampoline`, `MenuHandlerTrampoline`, `EventTrampoline`, timer/next-frame/map/startup/
  callback paths) catches everything and logs through `ErrorLog`.
* **No blocking work on the game thread** — the library never opens a network connection; the
  only I/O is config/phrase reads (which the plugins do at startup) and log appends.
* **Missing bindings degrade to no-ops** — every entry point checks the `__s2sdk_*` pointer
  before calling it, so a server without the s2sdk plugin (or an older one) logs once and keeps
  running.

## 5. Deliberate differences from the Metamod originals (porting notes)

1. **`PluginId` parameters are gone** (`RegCommand`, `StartupServer`, `HookEvent`, …); the
   library owns every registration and drops them all in `Shutdown()`.
2. **Item texts are not escaped.** cs2-menus escapes item text because its Panorama layout is
   XML/printf-formatted; the s2sdk backends take plain text. Porting note: drop
   `g_pMenus->escapeString(...)` around item texts, or the client sees `&lt;` and `%%`.
3. **Page turns don't notify the callback** (see §3); `("back"/"next"/…)` notifications with
   `iItem == 8` are gone, `7` (exit-back) and `9` (exit) remain.
4. **Chat listeners** see every `say`/`say_team` message *except* the ones s2sdk consumes: a
   silent-trigger message, or a chat command whose handler returned `true` (handled). Pisex's
   listeners saw those too. `AddChatListenerPost` does not exist (it needs cs2-menus' own mute
   flag).
5. **`GetCGameEntitySystem()`/`GetCEntitySystem()` return `nullptr`** — s2sdk has no engine
   entity-system object; use `pisex/schema.hpp` / the s2sdk entity functions.
6. **`GetCGlobalVars()` returns a snapshot** refreshed at the start of every `Poll()` (up to one
   frame old) instead of a live engine pointer.
7. **Timers**: same semantics (return value = next delay, negative = stop) but rescheduling
   happens in `Poll()` (≤ one frame later, no double-run), and s2sdk's `TimerFlag::NoMapChange`
   is deliberately not set so timers behave like the Pisex ones across map changes.
8. **`GetTranslation`-style fallback**: `LoadPhrasesFile` resolves each key for the selected
   language, then `"en"`, then any language present. Pisex read `GetString(language)` with no
   fallback (an untranslated key printed an empty line).
9. **Language codes**: the s2sdk server language (`GetServerLanguage`) is normalised
   (`russian`→`ru`, `portuguese`→`pt-BR`, …); override with `pisex::SetPhrasesLanguage("ru")` if
   the server is configured differently.
10. **`KeyValues::LoadFromFile` takes one argument** (the engine filesystem is gone) and the path
    is resolved as described in §2. The parser is KV1 only (no `.kv3`, no `#include` expansion —
    `#base`/`#include`/`#define` lines are skipped).
11. **`RemoveTimer` on a dead handle is safe** (see §3); `CTimer` objects are freed when the
    timer stops.
12. **`escapeString` keeps its Pisex behaviour** (it is still used for Panorama leftovers), but
    `AddItemMenu` no longer calls it (difference 2).
13. **`%llu` must become `%lu` for steam ids.** Metamod's `uint64` is `unsigned long long`; on
    Linux/glibc `uint64_t` is `unsigned long`, so a ported `PrintToChat(slot, "%llu", steamid64)`
    is a format/argument-size mismatch — undefined behaviour in the engine's printf, and a
    `-Wformat` error with the attributes the printers carry. Use `%lu` (or cast to
    `unsigned long long` and keep `%llu`). Same for `std::to_string`.
14. **`CCommand` is gone**: the handlers that split the callback content use `pisex::CommandArgs`
    (`Tokenize`/`ArgC`/`Arg`/`ArgS`/`operator[]`, same behaviour for the admin core's usage).
15. **Menu changes made from inside a menu callback are applied one frame later** (the engine calls
    handlers while holding the menu manager's lock, so `DisplayPlayerMenu`/`ClosePlayerMenu` from a
    callback are queued and run from `Poll()`); global menu state (`IsMenuOpen`, the new menu's
    contents) therefore updates on the next frame, not inside the callback. The item number is
    derived from the item index modulo the page size (5), so it matches Pisex's 1..5 without any
    engine query inside the handler.
16. **Player values for slots without a client are the API defaults, never s2sdk's stale ones**:
    `GetPlayerName` is `""` (s2sdk says `"<unknown>"`), `GetSteamID64`/`GetSteamID` are `0`/`""`
    (s2sdk would answer the *previous* occupant's unauthenticated id), `GetIpAddress` is `""` for
    bots (s2sdk has no net channel for them). Metamod's originals could answer for a connecting
    client as well; the difference only shows in that transient state.
17. **The map-change window is a "no client/entity code" gap**: from `OnMapEnd` until the next
    `OnMapStart` (plus the update that follows it) `IsGameReady()` is false, timers/`NextFrame` are
    postponed to the first ready frame, and events keep being delivered (data only) with every
    client/entity lookup they make answering defaults. Plugins that cache a slot/entity across the
    gap must re-validate (see `IsClientReady`/`IsValidEntity`); the Pisex originals had no such
    window because Metamod kept its client objects alive through a changelevel.

## 6. Not covered at all (port these to s2sdk directly)

Entity work (`CreateEntityByName`, `DispatchSpawn`, `AcceptEntityInput`, `TeleportEntity`,
`RemoveEntity`, `SetEntityModel`), `SetTransmitState`, damage/voice/CanAcquire hooks
(`HookOnTakeDamage*`, `HookIsHearingClient`, `AddCanAcquire*`), Panorama/HUD-layout menus
(toggles, selects, `SetDescriptionMenu` rendering), notifications (`ShowNotify*`), settings menu
hooks, `TerminateRound`, `AddPrecache`, `AddServerListener`/`AddEntityListener`,
`ShowAdminLastCategoryMenu`-style APIs from other Pisex plugins (VIP/LR/Shop APIs are different
libraries, not part of this one), players' `SetConVar*`/sound/`RayTrace`/`TakeDamage`,
`AddListener` listener objects, and the schema-typed entity accessors of `SchemaEntity`.
Everything in that list is a normal s2sdk call or a small helper on top of s2sdk; nothing here
needs Metamod.

## 7. Integration check

`test/smoke_plugin.cpp` is built as a real plugin `.so` (`libpisexcompat_smoke.so`) by
`./build.sh`: it uses Init/Poll/Shutdown, a command with `CommandArgs`, an event hook and a timer
exactly like a ported plugin. It is not packaged; it exists so that the normal build gates cover a
*consumer* of the library — the ABI report shows `max GLIBC_2.25`, `NEEDED: libc, ld-linux` (no
libstdc++/libmariadb), and all 1062 `__s2sdk_*` binding globals plus `Plugify_PluginInit` are
exported from the plugin as the plugify module expects.

## 8. Tests

`tests/pisexcompat_tests.cpp` (run by `./test.sh`) covers the engine-free parts, 210 checks:
KeyValues parsing of the real admin-system `.ini` config files (including the
`flags`/`times_reasons`/`default_permissions` shapes and the malformed-input rejection), phrase
loading with language fallback, the colour table byte-for-byte against cs2-menus, menu builder
bookkeeping (ITEM_HIDE dropped, callback/title/flags/clear, no crash without an engine), path
resolution (incl. the Metamod spellings), `FormatString` and the timer-delay clamp
(`ClampTimerDelay`: 0/negative/sub-tick/NaN all floor to `kMinTimerDelay`).

`libs/pisexcompat/test/timers_engine_test.cpp` (built as `build/tests/pisexcompat_timers_tests`)
drives the *real* timer registry with fake s2sdk timer bindings: the fake s2sdk
`CreateTimer`/`RescheduleTimer`/`KillsTimer` record what the library does, and the test fires the
recorded callback exactly like `TimerSystem::RunFrame()` would. It covers that crash and the
bookkeeping bugs: creation and reschedule delays are always ≥ one tick, a returned `0` is clamped,
s2sdk id 0 is a valid, killable timer, a stopped one-shot kills its engine timer, a callback may
remove its own timer (or another one), `Shutdown()` from inside a callback, a callback never runs
twice in one frame, a recycled `CTimer` address is not mistaken for a dead handle, and a timer
(and `NextFrame`) whose fire falls into a map change is postponed and re-armed with one tick on
the first ready frame.

`libs/pisexcompat/test/players_engine_test.cpp` (built as `build/tests/pisexcompat_players_tests`)
does the same for the player wrappers with fake client bindings. It asserts the two crash
fixes by *call counting*: while no map is up not a single s2sdk client call is made, and
`SetClientName` is never reached for a slot without a client or without a controller yet - while
the happy path (human and bot) still works, `"<unknown>"` becomes
`""`, a bot has no IP, and a disconnected slot answers steamid `0` instead of the previous
occupant's id.

`libs/pisexcompat/test/menu_engine_test.cpp` (built as `build/tests/pisexcompat_menu_tests`) drives
the menu layer with a fake s2sdk menu manager that counts `CreateMenu`/`DestroyMenu` and mimics the
handler dispatch (Cancel then End) and `DestroyMenu`'s own end-of-session callbacks. It proves the
documented destroy rule: a timed-out / exited / disconnected display destroys its menu exactly
once and only from `Poll()` (never inside the handler, where the manager's lock is held), an
explicit close or a refused display destroys immediately without a second destroy later, an id
another client still displays stays alive until that session ends, and map end / `Shutdown()`
destroys everything open or queued — with the map-end destroy never running over a client that
still displays the menu (`DestroyMenu`'s viewer cancel is the client call that window forbids).

Everything else that touches s2sdk (events, chat triggers) needs a running server — the bindings
are null pointers in the test process.

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/api.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — the Pisex-shaped API objects.
//
// A ported plugin keeps the exact call sites it had with Metamod:
//
//   #include <pisex/pisex.hpp>
//   using namespace pisex;               // makes g_pUtils/g_pMenus/g_pPlayers visible
//   ...
//   g_pUtils->PrintToChat(iSlot, phrase, name);
//   g_pMenus->AddItemMenu(hMenu, "kick", display);
//   g_pPlayers->GetSteamID64(iSlot);
//
// The three objects forward to the free functions of the headers next to this one (same names,
// same behaviour). Nothing else about the Pisex interfaces is emulated: a plugin that needs a
// functionality s2sdk does not have keeps failing loudly at compile time instead of silently at
// runtime. The unused ones are listed in README.md under "not covered".

#pragma once

#include <chrono>
#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <pisex/commands.hpp>
#include <pisex/compat.hpp>
#include <pisex/events.hpp>
#include <pisex/menu.hpp>
#include <pisex/output.hpp>
#include <pisex/phrases.hpp>
#include <pisex/players.hpp>
#include <pisex/timers.hpp>

namespace pisex {

// Deferred "the server started" callback (Pisex's IUtilsApi::StartupServer, whose listener fires
// once per server start). pisexcompat runs it on the first Poll(), i.e. with a map loaded, because
// the Pisex startup handlers load configs and open databases.
using StartupCallback = std::function<void()>;
using MapStartCallback = std::function<void(const char* szMap)>;

class UtilsApi {
public:
	// --- messages ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
	void PrintToChat(int iSlot, const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
	void PrintToChatAll(const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
	void PrintToConsole(int iSlot, const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
	void PrintToConsoleAll(const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
	void PrintToCenter(int iSlot, const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
	void PrintToCenterAll(const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
	void PrintToCenterHtml(int iSlot, int iDuration, const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 4, 5)));
	void PrintToCenterHtmlAll(int iDuration, const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
	void PrintToAlert(int iSlot, const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
	void PrintToAlertAll(const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
	void ErrorLog(const char* msg, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
	void LogToFile(const char* szFile, const char* szText, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));

	// --- commands / events -------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Pisex's PluginId parameter is gone: the library owns every registration and drops them all
	// in pisex::Shutdown().
	void RegCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& console, const std::vector<std::string>& chat,
					const CommandCallback& callback);
	// Console names only, ignored for every caller slot (see pisex::RegServerCommand).
	void RegServerCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& console, const CommandCallback& callback);
	void AddChatListenerPre(const CommandCallbackPre& callback);
	void HookEvent(const char* sName, const EventCallback& callback);

	// --- timers ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	CTimer* CreateTimer(float flInterval, std::function<float()> func);
	void RemoveTimer(CTimer* timer);
	void NextFrame(std::function<void()> fn);

	// --- lifecycle / info --------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Runs fn once, on the first update with a map loaded (Pisex: on server startup).
	void StartupServer(StartupCallback fn);
	void MapStartHook(MapStartCallback fn);
	void MapEndHook(StartupCallback fn);
	// Loads <translations dir>/<file>.txt into pisex::g_translations (Pisex's IUtilsApi method).
	void LoadTranslations(const char* file);
	const char* GetLanguage();
	const char* GetVersion();

	// --- engine ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	GlobalVars* GetCGlobalVars();
	// s2sdk has no entity-system pointer with an engine-defined layout: these return nullptr.
	// Use pisex/schema.hpp (or the s2sdk entity functions) instead of iterating the entity system.
	void* GetCGameEntitySystem();
	void* GetCEntitySystem();

	// --- helpers (not part of IUtilsApi) ------------------------------------------------------
	std::string Colorize(const std::string& text);
};

class MenusApi {
public:
	void AddItemMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* sBack, const char* sText, int iType = ITEM_DEFAULT);
	void AddRawItemMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* sBack, const char* sText, int iType = ITEM_DEFAULT);
	void SetTitleMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* szTitle);
	void SetExitMenu(Menu& hMenu, bool bExit);
	void SetBackMenu(Menu& hMenu, bool bBack);
	void SetCallback(Menu& hMenu, MenuCallbackFunc func);
	void SetDescriptionMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* szDescription);
	void DisplayPlayerMenu(Menu& hMenu, int iSlot, bool bClose = true);
	void DisplayPlayerMenu(Menu& hMenu, int iSlot, bool bClose, bool bReset);
	void ClosePlayerMenu(int iSlot);
	bool IsMenuOpen(int iSlot);
	std::string escapeString(const std::string& input);
	MenuType GetMenuType(int iSlot);
	void SetMenuType(int iSlot, MenuType type);
	void SetMenuTimeout(int iSeconds);
};

class PlayersApi {
public:
	bool IsFakeClient(int iSlot);
	bool IsConnected(int iSlot);
	bool IsInGame(int iSlot);
	bool IsAuthenticated(int iSlot);
	bool IsAlive(int iSlot);
	void HookOnClientAuthorized(const OnClientAuthorizedCallback& callback);
	uint64_t GetSteamID64(int iSlot);
	const char* GetSteamID(int iSlot);
	const char* GetIpAddress(int iSlot);
	const char* GetPlayerName(int iSlot);
	void SetPlayerName(int iSlot, const char* szName);
	const char* GetClientLanguage(int iSlot);
	int FindPlayer(uint64_t iSteamID64);
	int FindPlayer(const char* szName);
	int GetHealth(int iSlot);
	int GetArmor(int iSlot);
	int GetMoney(int iSlot);
	int GetTeam(int iSlot);
	void ChangeTeam(int iSlot, int iNewTeam);
	void SwitchTeam(int iSlot, int iNewTeam);
	void Respawn(int iSlot);
	void CommitSuicide(int iSlot, bool bExplode, bool bForce);
	void SetMoveType(int iSlot, int moveType);
	void RemoveWeapons(int iSlot);
};

// The Pisex globals. They are non-null from program start, so a plugin may use them in any
// callback as long as pisex::Init() has run before the call site (the printers themselves are
// no-ops before a map exists).
extern UtilsApi* const g_pUtils;
extern MenusApi* const g_pMenus;
extern PlayersApi* const g_pPlayers;

// The instances behind the pointers.
UtilsApi& Utils();
MenusApi& Menus();
PlayersApi& Players();

} // namespace pisex

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/commands.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — RegCommand / chat listeners over s2sdk.
//
// Pisex registers console names and chat names separately:
//
//   g_pUtils->RegCommand(g_PLID, {"mm_admin", "css_admin"}, {"!admin"}, OnAdminMenu);
//
// and the callback gets the raw argument string, so the ported handlers keep parsing it with
// CCommand::Tokenize and comparing arg[0] against the registered spelling ("!admin", "mm_admin").
// pisexcompat preserves that: the command name is handed back exactly as it was registered,
// followed by the arguments (space-joined), no matter which trigger the player used.
//
// How the s2sdk side works (verified against libplugify-plugin-s2sdk.so):
//   * ConCommandManager::DispatchConCommand() special-cases "say"/"say_team": when the first
//     argument starts with a trigger from the s2sdk settings (PublicChatTrigger "!", silent "/"),
//     it strips the trigger, tokenizes the rest and dispatches it as a *command* with
//     ConCommandContext::Chat - a silent-trigger message (or one whose command returns
//     Handled/Stop) is then not broadcast at all.
//   * Every command (registered or existing) reaches a callback registered with
//     AddConsoleCommand/AddCommandListener; args[0] is the command name, caller is -1 for the
//     server console.
//   * The chat commands therefore share the console command namespace: chat names are registered
//     with their trigger stripped ("!ban" -> "ban"), and a chat name is dispatched only for chat
//     input while a console name is dispatched only for console input (like Pisex).
//
// Callback contract (unchanged from Pisex):
//   CommandCallback    -> return true  = handled, the engine must not process the command/chat
//                                      message any further (Pisex's MRES_SUPERCEDE)
//                         return false = let the engine continue
//   CommandCallbackPre -> return true  = allow the chat message
//                         return false = block it (Pisex's SendChatListenerPreCallback)

#pragma once

#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {

using CommandCallback = std::function<bool(int iSlot, const char* szContent)>;
using CommandCallbackPre = std::function<bool(int iSlot, const char* szContent, bool bTeam)>;

// A stand-in for the engine's CCommand, which the Pisex command handlers use to split the content
// they get handed:
//
//   g_pUtils->RegCommand(..., [](int iSlot, const char* szContent) {
//       CommandArgs arg;
//       arg.Tokenize(szContent);
//       if (strcmp(arg[0], "!ban") == 0 && arg.ArgC() > 3) { ... atoi(arg.Arg(3)) ... }
//       return true;
//   });
//
// Same API as the subset of CCommand the admin core uses: ArgC(), Arg(i), ArgS(), operator[].
// Whitespace separated, double quotes group a token and are removed (the content built by
// RegCommand joins the engine tokens with single spaces, so quoting round-trips).
class CommandArgs {
public:
	CommandArgs() = default;
	explicit CommandArgs(const char* text) { Tokenize(text); }

	// Keeps the raw text (ArgS()) and the parsed tokens.
	void Tokenize(const char* text);
	void Tokenize(std::string_view text) { Tokenize(std::string(text).c_str()); }

	int ArgC() const { return static_cast<int>(args_.size()); }
	// nullptr when the index is out of range (CCommand would read past the end).
	const char* Arg(int index) const;
	const char* operator[](int index) const { return Arg(index); }
	// The whole (unparsed) string, as it was passed to Tokenize().
	const char* ArgS() const { return text_.c_str(); }
	void Reset();

private:
	std::string text_;
	std::vector<std::string> args_;
};

// Registers the console and chat names. Empty vectors are fine; a name may be registered twice
// (the most recently registered handler wins, like Pisex's std::map overwrite). A name that is
// also registered with RegServerCommand stays server-only.
void RegCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& console, const std::vector<std::string>& chat,
				const CommandCallback& callback);
// Convenience overloads for the one-name cases.
void RegCommand(const char* consoleName, const CommandCallback& callback);
void RegCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& console, const CommandCallback& callback);

// Server-console-only variant: registers console names without ClientCanExecute and ignores every
// call from a slot (client console or chat), like the Metamod CON_COMMAND_F(..., FCVAR_NONE)
// commands it replaces.
void RegServerCommand(const std::vector<std::string>& console, const CommandCallback& callback);
void RegServerCommand(const char* consoleName, const CommandCallback& callback);

// Called for every chat message the engine lets through (see README for the three cases s2sdk
// consumes before this point). Pisex's "post" variant cannot be implemented: it needs the mute
// flag of cs2-menus' own chat hook, which s2sdk does not expose.
void AddChatListenerPre(const CommandCallbackPre& callback);

// Extra trigger characters recognised when a chat name is registered ("!" and "/" are built in).
void AddChatTrigger(char trigger);
// Looks up the s2sdk settings (PublicChatTrigger / SilentChatTrigger) by parsing
// envs/plugins/s2sdk/settings.jsonc when it can be found; falls back to the built-in set.
void RefreshChatTriggers();
bool IsChatTrigger(char c);

// Drops every registration (Shutdown() calls this). s2sdk commands are removed with RemoveCommand.
void RemoveAllCommands();
// Internal: retries listeners for engine commands that did not exist yet (called by Poll()).
void PollCommandRegistrations();

// True when at least one command or chat listener is registered (used by IsChatListenerActive).
bool HasChatListeners();
bool HasCommands();

} // namespace pisex

```

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/compat.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — the single entry point a ported Pisex plugin uses.
//
//   plg::PluginResult OnPluginStart() {
//       pisex::Init("admin_system");            // names the plugin (config/translations dirs)
//       pisex::g_pUtils->StartupServer([] { ... }); // deferred to the first update with a map
//       return plg::PluginResult::Success;      // never Failed: that stops every Plugify plugin
//   }
//   plg::PluginResult OnPluginUpdate(std::chrono::milliseconds) {
//       pisex::Poll();                          // timers, next-frame queue, deferred startup
//       return plg::PluginResult::Continue;
//   }
//   plg::PluginResult OnPluginEnd() { pisex::Shutdown(); return plg::PluginResult::Success; }
//
// Why the trio exists:
//   * s2sdk client queries (IsClientConnected & friends) crash when they run before a map exists,
//     so everything that touches clients waits for the first Poll() (OnPluginUpdate is pumped from
//     ServerPostSimulate, i.e. only with a live map). pisex::IsGameReady() exposes that state to
//     the ported plugin, and every player wrapper in <pisex/players.hpp> checks it first.
//   * timers and the next-frame queue need a game-thread pump that is ours, not the engine's
//     (see <pisex/timers.hpp> for why s2sdk timers are rescheduled from Poll()).
//
// The s2sdk listeners are registered defensively: if the s2sdk plugin (or a single binding) is
// missing, Init() logs and returns false instead of throwing - a plugin that returns Failed from
// OnPluginStart stops every Plugify plugin on the server.

#pragma once

#include <chrono>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string_view>

namespace pisex {

// Sets the plugin name (config/translations/data dirs) and registers the s2sdk listeners used by
// this library (map start/end, say, ...). Safe to call before a map exists; no client query is
// made here. Returns false when the s2sdk bindings are unavailable.
bool Init(std::string_view pluginName);
// Same, with explicit dirs (empty = derive from the plugify dirs + plugin name).
bool Init(std::string_view pluginName, std::string_view configDir, std::string_view translationsDir);
// Unregisters everything this library registered, removes the remaining timers and drops the
// registries (commands, menus, events, chat listeners, next-frame queue).
void Shutdown();
// Must be called from OnPluginUpdate (game thread, once per frame): pumps the next-frame queue and
// reschedules/kills s2sdk timers. Also marks the game as ready and fires the deferred
// StartupServer callbacks on the first call.
void Poll();

// True once a map is running (from the first Poll or from the engine's map-start callback).
// Every wrapper that could reach a client query checks it.
bool IsGameReady();
// Current map name (empty when no map is running).
std::string_view CurrentMap();

// Set by the plugin when it wants the library to know about map changes (optional; Init already
// registers the s2sdk listeners when they are available).
void OnMapStartNotify();
void OnMapEndNotify();

// --- engine globals ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// The Pisex modules keep `gpGlobals = g_pUtils->GetCGlobalVars()` and read gpGlobals->curtime /
// ->maxClients. s2sdk exposes the same values as functions, so GetCGlobalVars() hands out a
// snapshot struct that is refreshed at the start of every Poll(). Values are therefore up to one
// frame old, which is what the Metamod pointers effectively were as well (they were read between
// engine updates).
struct GlobalVars {
	float curtime = 0.0f;			  // GetGameTime()
	float frametime = 0.0f;			  // GetGameFrameTime()
	float intervalPerTick = 0.0f;	  // GetTickInterval()
	int maxClients = 64;			  // GetMaxClients()
	int tickcount = 0;				  // GetGameTickCount()
	double realtime = 0.0;			  // GetEngineTime()
	float absoluteFrameTime = 0.0f;	  // GetGameFrameTime()
};
GlobalVars* GetCGlobalVars();
// Refreshes the snapshot (called by Poll(); call manually if you read it outside of a frame).
void RefreshGlobalVars();

// --- deferred server-start / map callbacks ----------------------------------------------------
// Registering here rather than running immediately is what makes them safe: every callback fires
// from Poll(), i.e. with a live map and on the game thread.
void RegisterStartupCallback(std::function<void()> callback);
void RegisterMapStartCallback(std::function<void(const char* map)> callback);
void RegisterMapEndCallback(std::function<void()> callback);

} // namespace pisex

```

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/events.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — game event hooks over s2sdk.
//
//   g_pUtils->HookEvent("player_death", [](const char* szName, IGameEvent* pEvent, bool bDontBroadcast) {
//       const int victim = pEvent->GetInt("userid");
//   });
//
// Pisex's HookEvent is a *pre* hook: cs2-menus installs a SourceHook on IGameEventManager2::FireEvent
// and calls the plugin callbacks before the engine processes the event, with the event pointer and
// the current broadcast flag. s2sdk::HookEvent(..., HookMode::Pre) is the same point, so the ported
// callbacks keep their signature and their behaviour (they may read and even change values; the
// engine honours the changes made in a pre hook).
//
// The value accessors mirror the IGameEvent getters the Pisex modules use. GetString() stores the
// engine string in a per-handle cache, so the returned pointer stays valid as long as the event
// does (IGameEvent::GetString() had the same guarantee for the event's lifetime).
//
// Event hooks survive map changes (like the Pisex ones) and are removed by Shutdown().

#pragma once

#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {

// Thin wrapper around the s2sdk event pointer (IGameEvent* in the Metamod code).
class IGameEvent {
public:
	IGameEvent() = default;
	explicit IGameEvent(void* event) : event_(event) {}

	bool IsValid() const { return event_ != nullptr; }
	void* Native() const { return event_; }

	const char* GetName() const;

	bool GetBool(const char* key, bool def = false) const;
	float GetFloat(const char* key, float def = 0.0f) const;
	int GetInt(const char* key, int def = 0) const;
	unsigned long long GetUInt64(const char* key, unsigned long long def = 0) const;
	const char* GetString(const char* key, const char* def = "") const;
	// Player slot of a "userid"/"attacker"/... key (-1 when the key holds no valid player).
	int GetPlayerSlot(const char* key) const;

	void SetBool(const char* key, bool value) const;
	void SetFloat(const char* key, float value) const;
	void SetInt(const char* key, int value) const;
	void SetUInt64(const char* key, unsigned long long value) const;
	void SetString(const char* key, const char* value) const;
	void SetPlayerSlot(const char* key, int slot) const;

private:
	// GetString() hands out a pointer into this cache (map nodes are stable across insertions).
	mutable std::map<std::string, std::string> strings_;
	void* event_ = nullptr;
};

using EventHandle = IGameEvent;

// Pisex's EventCallback: szName, the event, and whether it is broadcast to clients.
using EventCallback = std::function<void(const char* szName, IGameEvent* pEvent, bool bDontBroadcast)>;

// Registers a pre hook for the event (multiple callbacks per event are fine).
void HookEvent(const char* name, const EventCallback& callback);
void UnhookEvent(const char* name);
// Drops every hook (Shutdown()).
void RemoveAllEvents();

} // namespace pisex

```

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/keyvalues.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — Valve KeyValues (KV1) text parser.
//
// The Pisex plugins read their .ini / .cfg / .phrases.txt files with hl2sdk's KeyValues
// (LoadFromFile -> FindKey -> GetString/GetInt/... and FOR_EACH_SUBKEY/FOR_EACH_VALUE loops).
// This is the same thing without the engine: a small, dependency-free KV1 reader whose API covers
// the subset that Pisex actually uses (see README.md), so porting a config loader is a matter of
// replacing `new KeyValues("X")`/`kv->LoadFromFile(g_pFullFileSystem, path)` with
// `pisex::KeyValues` / `kv.LoadFromFile(path)`.
//
// Supported syntax (everything the real Pisex configs contain):
//   * quoted ("key" "value") and unquoted (key value) tokens,
//   * nested blocks: "key" { ... },
//   * // line comments (and /* */ block comments), trailing comments after a value,
//   * escape sequences inside quoted strings: \" \\ \n \r \t,
//   * the #base/#include/#define directives are parsed and dropped (no file inclusion),
//   * a key may carry both a value and a block, like Valve's KV1.
//
// Deliberate differences from hl2sdk's KeyValues:
//   * memory is owned by std::unique_ptr (no refcount, no leak on early return),
//   * no .kv3/.kv binary formats, no #include expansion, no localized tokens (the $ prefix),
//   * FindKey is case-insensitive (like Valve's), GetName keeps the original spelling.

#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {

class KeyValues {
public:
	// RAII wrapper so `KeyValues::AutoDelete kv("Phrases"); kv->LoadFromFile(...)` (the Pisex
	// spelling) keeps compiling.
	class AutoDelete {
	public:
		explicit AutoDelete(std::string_view name) : ptr_(std::make_unique<KeyValues>(name)) {}
		AutoDelete(const AutoDelete&) = delete;
		AutoDelete& operator=(const AutoDelete&) = delete;

		KeyValues* operator->() const { return ptr_.get(); }
		KeyValues& operator*() const { return *ptr_; }
		KeyValues* get() const { return ptr_.get(); }

	private:
		std::unique_ptr<KeyValues> ptr_;
	};

	explicit KeyValues(std::string_view name);
	KeyValues(const KeyValues&) = delete;
	KeyValues& operator=(const KeyValues&) = delete;
	~KeyValues();

	// --- loading -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Path resolution is delegated to pisex::ResolvePath (config/translations dirs, see compat.hpp).
	// Returns false when the file is missing or malformed; the tree is then left empty.
	bool LoadFromFile(std::string_view path);
	// Same parser over an in-memory buffer (used by the unit tests).
	bool LoadFromBuffer(std::string_view text);

	// --- identity ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
	const char* GetName() const { return name_.c_str(); }
	void SetName(std::string_view name) { name_ = std::string(name); }
	bool IsEmpty(std::string_view key) const;

	// --- lookup ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// Returns the first child with that name (case-insensitive). bCreate adds an empty child when
	// the key is missing, exactly like Valve's KeyValues.
	KeyValues* FindKey(const char* key, bool bCreate = false);
	const KeyValues* FindKey(const char* key) const;
	// Same, but only matches children that have a value (Valve's FindKey + GetFirstValue chain).
	KeyValues* FindKeyWithValue(const char* key);

	// --- values ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
	// A null/empty key reads the node's own value. All getters return the default when the key is
	// missing or the stored text cannot be converted.
	std::string_view GetStringValue(const char* key = nullptr, std::string_view def = {}) const;
	const char* GetString(const char* key = nullptr, const char* def = "") const;
	int GetInt(const char* key = nullptr, int def = 0) const;
	float GetFloat(const char* key = nullptr, float def = 0.0f) const;
	bool GetBool(const char* key = nullptr, bool def = false) const;

	void SetString(std::string_view key, std::string_view value);
	void SetInt(std::string_view key, int value);

	// True when this node is a block (has children). Pisex's FOR_EACH_SUBKEY loops need this.
	bool HasChildren() const { return !children_.empty(); }
	bool HasValue() const { return hasValue_; }
	std::size_t GetSubKeyCount() const { return children_.size(); }

	KeyValues* AddSubKey(std::string_view name);
	// Insertion-ordered child access (used by the tests and by callers that index by position).
	KeyValues* GetSubKey(std::size_t index);
	const KeyValues* GetSubKey(std::size_t index) const;

	// --- iteration (Valve's naming; loop with the FOR_EACH_* macros below) --------------------
	KeyValues* GetFirstSubKey();
	const KeyValues* GetFirstSubKey() const;
	KeyValues* GetNextKey();
	const KeyValues* GetNextKey() const;

	KeyValues* GetFirstTrueSubKey();
	const KeyValues* GetFirstTrueSubKey() const;
	KeyValues* GetNextTrueSubKey();
	const KeyValues* GetNextTrueSubKey() const;

	KeyValues* GetFirstValue();
	const KeyValues* GetFirstValue() const;
	KeyValues* GetNextValue();
	const KeyValues* GetNextValue() const;

	std::vector<KeyValues*> GetSubKeyList();
	// Drops every child and the own value (Pisex calls KeyValues::deleteAllSubkeys on reload).
	void Clear();

private:
	// A child is a "true sub key" when it is a block, and a "value" when it carries a scalar.
	bool IsValueNode() const;
	bool IsBlockNode() const;

	std::string name_;
	std::string value_;
	bool hasValue_ = false;
	KeyValues* parent_ = nullptr;
	std::vector<std::unique_ptr<KeyValues>> children_;
};

// Pisex (hl2sdk) iteration macros, kept verbatim so ported loops compile unchanged.
#define FOR_EACH_SUBKEY(kvParent, kvName) \
	for (pisex::KeyValues* kvName = (kvParent)->GetFirstTrueSubKey(); kvName; kvName = kvName->GetNextTrueSubKey())

#define FOR_EACH_VALUE(kvParent, kvName) \
	for (pisex::KeyValues* kvName = (kvParent)->GetFirstValue(); kvName; kvName = kvName->GetNextValue())

} // namespace pisex

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/menu.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — the Pisex menu builder over s2sdk menus.
//
// The ported code keeps its shape:
//
//   Menu hMenu;
//   g_pMenus->SetTitleMenu(hMenu, phrase);
//   g_pMenus->AddItemMenu(hMenu, "kick", display);
//   g_pMenus->SetExitMenu(hMenu, true);
//   g_pMenus->SetCallback(hMenu, [](const char* back, const char* front, int iItem, int iSlot) {
//       if (iItem < 7) { /* item "back" was chosen */ }
//       else if (iItem == 7) { /* exit-back */ }
//   });
//   g_pMenus->DisplayPlayerMenu(hMenu, iSlot);
//
// Item numbers are the Pisex ones: 1..5 for the items of the current page, 7 = exit-back ("back"),
// 9 = exit ("exit"). s2sdk's built-in backends use their own digits (1-7 items, 8 previous page,
// 9 next page, 0 exit) - the trampoline translates the actions back into Pisex numbers, so ported
// callbacks keep working unchanged. Paging itself is handled by the s2sdk backend and does *not*
// call the callback (Pisex called it with ("next","next",8) / ("back","back",7) for page turns).
//
// ITEM_HIDE items are dropped when the menu is created (like Pisex: AddItemMenu ignores iType 0),
// ITEM_DISABLED items are added as s2sdk "Disabled" items and are not selectable.
//
// Which s2sdk menu type a displayed menu gets (ResolveS2sdkMenuTypeName):
//   1. an explicit per-slot SetMenuType(slot, ...) wins (the plugin forced it);
//   2. otherwise the player's own choice is used when the hudmenu plugin is installed - its
//      exported GetClientMenuType(slot) returns "hud"/"wasd"/"button"/"centerhtml"/"chat" from
//      the permissions cookie "Utils.MenuType" (Pisex's "!menu" choice), so every plugin's
//      menus follow what the player picked;
//   3. without hudmenu, the slot's Pisex MenuType is mapped (HUD_LAYOUT -> "hud" and
//      CENTER_WASD -> "wasd" when the matching backend is registered, else "button").
//
// Only the s2sdk menu features are offered: the HUD_LAYOUT/Panorama extras of cs2-menus
// (SetDescriptionMenu, toggles, selects) exist as no-ops or throw-away state - see README.

#pragma once

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {

// cs2-menus item types.
inline constexpr int ITEM_HIDE = 0;
inline constexpr int ITEM_DEFAULT = 1;
inline constexpr int ITEM_DISABLED = 2;

struct Items {
	int iType = ITEM_DEFAULT;
	std::string sBack;
	std::string sText;
};

// cs2-menus MenuType.
enum class MenuType : int {
	CHAT = 0,
	CENTER = 1,
	CENTER_WASD = 2,
	HUD_LAYOUT = 3,
};

// Pisex's MenuCallbackFunc: (back value, front text, item number, slot).
using MenuCallbackFunc = std::function<void(const char* szBack, const char* szFront, int iItem, int iSlot)>;

struct Menu {
	std::string szTitle;
	std::vector<Items> hItems;
	bool bBack = false;
	bool bExit = false;
	MenuCallbackFunc hFunc;
	// HUD_LAYOUT only in Pisex; kept so SetDescriptionMenu() has somewhere to store it.
	std::string szDescription;

	void clear() {
		szTitle.clear();
		hItems.clear();
		bBack = false;
		bExit = false;
		hFunc = nullptr;
		szDescription.clear();
	}
};

// Adds an item (iType ITEM_DEFAULT/ITEM_DISABLED; ITEM_HIDE is ignored, exactly like Pisex).
void AddItemMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* sBack, const char* sText, int iType = ITEM_DEFAULT);
// Same without the escaping Pisex applies to the display text (for pre-formatted text).
void AddRawItemMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* sBack, const char* sText, int iType = ITEM_DEFAULT);
void SetTitleMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* szTitle);
void SetExitMenu(Menu& hMenu, bool bExit);
void SetBackMenu(Menu& hMenu, bool bBack);
void SetCallback(Menu& hMenu, MenuCallbackFunc func);
void SetDescriptionMenu(Menu& hMenu, const char* szDescription);

// Shows the menu to the client. bClose/bReset exist for Pisex compatibility: the s2sdk menu of
// that slot is always replaced (Pisex's "keep the old state" path was only used for page turns,
// which s2sdk does itself).
void DisplayPlayerMenu(Menu& hMenu, int iSlot, bool bClose = true);
void DisplayPlayerMenu(Menu& hMenu, int iSlot, bool bClose, bool bReset);
// Closes whatever menu the client has, without calling the callback (Pisex behaviour).
void ClosePlayerMenu(int iSlot);
// Internal (called by Init): reserves s2sdk menu id 0, see menu.cpp.
void BurnMenuIdZero();
// Closes every open menu of this library (map end / plugin end).
void CloseAllMenus();
bool IsMenuOpen(int iSlot);

// Pisex's escapeString(): % -> %%, \ " \n \r \t and < > escaped for the Panorama layout.
std::string escapeString(const std::string& input);

MenuType GetMenuType(int iSlot);
// Forces this slot's s2sdk menu type: ResolveS2sdkMenuTypeName then ignores the player's own
// "!menu" choice for the slot (Pisex's SetMenuType semantics, kept for module overrides).
void SetMenuType(int iSlot, MenuType type);
// Resets the default for every slot (and clears all per-slot overrides, like the Pisex original
// which overwrote the whole table). Slots without an override follow the players' own choice.
void SetDefaultMenuType(MenuType type);
// True while this slot carries an explicit SetMenuType() override (diagnostics/tests).
bool IsMenuTypeForced(int iSlot);

// Pure part of the type selection, exposed for the tests:
//   forced                 - the slot has an explicit SetMenuType() override
//   type                   - the slot's Pisex MenuType (the default when not forced)
//   playerTypeChoice       - hudmenu's GetClientMenuType() answer, empty when hudmenu is not
//                            installed; must be "hud", "wasd", "button", "centerhtml" or "chat"
//   hudTypeRegistered      - the "hud" s2sdk menu type is registered
//   wasdTypeRegistered     - the "wasd" s2sdk menu type is registered
// Returns one of the registered s2sdk type names (the returned view is a literal or points
// into playerTypeChoice).
std::string_view ResolveS2sdkMenuTypeName(bool forced, MenuType type, std::string_view playerTypeChoice,
										  bool hudTypeRegistered, bool wasdTypeRegistered);
// Seconds before an open menu closes by itself (cs2-menus core.ini "MenuTime", default 60).
void SetMenuTimeout(int seconds);
int MenuTimeout();

// Applies the menu changes a callback asked for (pisex::Poll() calls this). A menu handler runs
// inside s2sdk's menu manager (under its recursive mutex, so no deadlock); the hazard is
// re-entrancy: DestroyMenu ends the menu for every viewer and calls the handler's Cancel and End
// again while the outer handler is still on the stack (s2sdk's DestroyMenu/EndClientMenu). So
// DisplayPlayerMenu() and ClosePlayerMenu() *from inside a
// callback* queue the request and it is executed here, one frame later. Calls from anywhere else (commands, timers, event handlers) are applied immediately.
void ProcessMenuRequests();

} // namespace pisex

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/output.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — chat / console / centre output and logging (IUtilsApi's print family).
//
// All printers take a printf-style format (Pisex passes a format plus arguments) and go through
// s2sdk's HUD destinations, which use the same CUserMessageTextMsg the Metamod plugin used, so
// the colour bytes produced by pisex::Colorize() arrive untouched:
//
//   PrintToChat(slot, "%s joined", name)      -> HUD_PRINTTALK   (coloured, 1 client)
//   PrintToChatAll(...)                       -> HUD_PRINTTALK   (all real players)
//   PrintToConsole(slot, ...)                 -> HUD_PRINTCONSOLE (a negative slot prints to the
//                                                server console, like Pisex's META_CONPRINT)
//   PrintToCenter / PrintToAlert              -> HUD_PRINTCENTER / HUD_PRINTALERT
//   PrintToCenterHtml(slot, duration, ...)    -> HTML centre message (s2sdk's PrintCentreHtml)
//
// Every printer is a no-op while no map is running (pisex::IsGameReady() == false), because the
// s2sdk print helpers reach for client state; they are called from plugin start in Pisex and must
// not crash there. Use "%s" style formats only - Pisex's own format strings (%i, %llu) work.

#pragma once

#include <string>
#include <string_view>

namespace pisex {

void PrintToChat(int iSlot, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
void PrintToChatAll(const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));
void PrintToChatRaw(int iSlot, std::string_view message);

void PrintToConsole(int iSlot, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
void PrintToConsoleAll(const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));

void PrintToCenter(int iSlot, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
void PrintToCenterAll(const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));

void PrintToCenterHtml(int iSlot, int iDuration, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)));
void PrintToCenterHtmlAll(int iDuration, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));

void PrintToAlert(int iSlot, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
void PrintToAlertAll(const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));

// Timestamped line to the server console + <logs dir>/<file>.txt (Pisex: addons/logs/<file>.txt).
void LogToFile(const char* file, const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 2, 3)));
// Red "[Error] ..." line on the server console + <logs dir>/error_MM-DD-YYYY.txt.
void ErrorLog(const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));

// printf into a std::string (the shared formatter behind the printers).
std::string FormatString(const char* format, ...) __attribute__((format(printf, 1, 2)));

} // namespace pisex

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/paths.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — path resolution for configs / translations / data files.
//
// The Pisex plugins hard-code Metamod paths ("addons/configs/admin_system/core.ini",
// "addons/translations/admin_system.phrases.txt", "addons/data/..."). Plugify gives each plugin
// its own config and data directory instead, so pisexcompat resolves relative paths through a
// small candidate list, which keeps the ported loaders free of layout knowledge:
//
//   file.txt                          -> cwd, then <configs>/<plugin>/file.txt, then <configs>/file.txt
//   addons/configs/<x>/file.txt       -> the "addons/configs/<x>/" prefix is stripped
//   addons/translations/file.txt      -> resolved in the translations dir
//   addons/data/file.txt              -> resolved in the data dir
//
// Any path that already exists as given (absolute or relative to the server working directory)
// wins, so a ported plugin can also be pointed at a hand-written file.

#pragma once

#include <string>
#include <string_view>

namespace pisex {

// Names the ported plugin; sets <GetConfigsDir()>/<name> and <GetDataDir()>/<name> as base dirs.
// Called by pisex::Init(), or directly before loading a config outside of a plugin.
void SetPluginName(std::string_view name);
const std::string& PluginName();

// Explicit overrides (empty string = derive from the plugify dirs / plugin name).
void SetConfigDir(std::string_view dir);
void SetTranslationsDir(std::string_view dir);

const std::string& ConfigDir();       // <GetConfigsDir()>/<plugin>
const std::string& TranslationsDir(); // <ConfigDir()>/translations
const std::string& DataDir();         // <GetDataDir()>/<plugin>

std::string JoinPath(std::string_view a, std::string_view b);
bool FileExists(std::string_view path);
// Reads a whole file; returns an empty string and sets *ok=false when it cannot be opened.
std::string ReadFile(std::string_view path, bool* ok = nullptr);

// Candidate search described above; returns the first existing path, or "" when nothing matched.
std::string ResolvePath(std::string_view path);
// Same, but always resolved against the translations dir first (phrases files).
std::string ResolveTranslationsPath(std::string_view path);
// Same, resolved against the data dir first.
std::string ResolveDataPath(std::string_view path);

} // namespace pisex

```

`libs/pisexcompat/include/pisex/phrases.hpp`:

```hpp
// pisexcompat — chat colour tags and the Pisex phrase (translation) store.
//
// Colour tags: cs2-menus/utils.h owns the table the whole Pisex family uses
// ({DEFAULT} {WHITE} {RED} {LIGHTPURPLE} {GREEN} {LIME} {LIGHTGREEN} {DARKRED} {GRAY} {LIGHTOLIVE}
//  {OLIVE} {LIGHTBLUE} {BLUE} {PURPLE} {LIGHTRED} {GRAYBLUE} {\n}); pisex::Colorize() replaces the
// tags with exactly the same bytes (0x01..0x10 and the U+2029 line separator for "\n") so chat
// output is byte-identical to the Metamod server.
//
// Phrases: LoadPhrasesFile() reads a *.phrases.txt (KeyValues: "Key" { "ru" "..." "en" "..." })
// and resolves every key for the selected language with an "en" fallback, which is what
// cs2-menus/admin_system do (they read GetString(GetLanguage()) with no fallback at all).
// The result lands in the caller's map or in the shared pisex::g_translations.

#pragma once

#include <map>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>

namespace pisex {

using PhraseMap = std::map<std::string, std::string>;

// Shared store filled by UtilsApi::LoadTranslations() / pisex::LoadPhrases("name.phrases").
extern PhraseMap g_translations;

// Replaces {TAG} colour tags with the cs2-menus chat colour bytes.
std::string Colorize(std::string_view text);
// The same tags removed (and "\\n" turned into a real newline): for the server console, which
// shows the chat colour bytes as garbage and the tags as literal text.
std::string StripColorTags(std::string_view text);

// Language used when a phrase has no entry for the selected language.
inline constexpr std::string_view kFallbackLanguage = "en";

// Loads <translations dir>/<file> (".txt" is appended when missing) into `out`.
// When `language` is null the current language (pisex::PhrasesLanguage) is used.
// Returns false when the file cannot be read; `out` is left untouched then.
bool LoadPhrasesFile(const char* file, PhraseMap& out, const char* language = nullptr);

// Same, into the shared store (adds to it; Pisex's LoadTranslations has the same additive
// behaviour - the admin core clears its map itself on reload).
bool LoadPhrases(const char* file, const char* language = nullptr);

// Current language ("ru", "en", ...). Defaults to the server language reported by s2sdk,
// normalized to the codes used by the Pisex phrase files, with "en" as the fallback.
void SetPhrasesLanguage(std::string_view language);
const std::string& PhrasesLanguage();

// Maps a Source language name ("russian", "portuguese", ...) to the phrase-file code ("ru",
// "pt-BR", ...). Unknown names are returned unchanged.
std::string NormalizeLanguage(std::string_view name);

// Phrase lookup in the shared store; returns the key itself when it is missing, which is what
// IAdminApi::GetTranslation() does (so missing phrases are visible instead of printing nothing).
const std::string& GetPhrase(const char* key);
const char* GetPhraseCStr(const char* key);

} // namespace pisex
