`libs/pisexcompat/src/paths.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <pisex/paths.hpp>

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstdio>
#include <fstream>
#include <sstream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {
namespace {

std::string g_pluginName;
std::string g_configDirOverride;
std::string g_translationsDirOverride;
std::string g_configDir;       // cache, valid while the overrides do not change
std::string g_translationsDir;
std::string g_dataDir;
bool g_dirsCached = false;

std::string CfgRoot() {
	return plg::GetConfigsDir ? std::string(plg::GetConfigsDir()) : std::string();
}

std::string DataRoot() {
	return plg::GetDataDir ? std::string(plg::GetDataDir()) : std::string();
}

void InvalidateCaches() {
	g_dirsCached = false;
	g_configDir.clear();
	g_translationsDir.clear();
	g_dataDir.clear();
}

bool StartsWith(std::string_view text, std::string_view prefix) {
	return text.size() >= prefix.size() && text.compare(0, prefix.size(), prefix) == 0;
}

std::string_view StripPrefix(std::string_view text, std::string_view prefix) {
	return StartsWith(text, prefix) ? text.substr(prefix.size()) : std::string_view{};
}

// Tries the candidates in order and returns the first one that exists on disk.
std::string FirstExisting(const std::vector<std::string>& candidates) {
	for (const std::string& candidate : candidates) {
		if (!candidate.empty() && FileExists(candidate)) {
			return candidate;
		}
	}
	return {};
}

std::vector<std::string> Candidates(std::string_view path, const std::string& preferredDir) {
	std::vector<std::string> out;
	if (path.empty()) {
		return out;
	}
	const std::string raw(path);
	const bool absolute = !raw.empty() && raw.front() == '/';
	out.push_back(raw); // as given (absolute, or relative to the server working directory)

	if (absolute) {
		return out;
	}

	// "addons/configs/<plugin>/x.ini" / "addons/translations/x.phrases.txt" / "addons/data/x"
	// are the Metamod spellings; strip the fixed prefix and treat the rest as a relative path.
	std::string_view relative = path;
	bool fromTranslations = false;
	bool fromData = false;
	if (auto rest = StripPrefix(path, "addons/configs/"); !rest.empty()) {
		relative = rest;
		// "admin_system/core.ini" -> "core.ini" when it is our own config dir.
		if (!g_pluginName.empty() && StartsWith(rest, g_pluginName + "/")) {
			relative = rest.substr(g_pluginName.size() + 1);
		}
	} else if (auto rest2 = StripPrefix(path, "addons/translations/"); !rest2.empty()) {
		relative = rest2;
		fromTranslations = true;
	} else if (auto rest3 = StripPrefix(path, "addons/data/"); !rest3.empty()) {
		relative = rest3;
		fromData = true;
	} else if (auto rest4 = StripPrefix(path, "addons/"); !rest4.empty()) {
		relative = rest4;
	}

	const std::string rel(relative);
	const std::string& configDir = preferredDir.empty() ? ConfigDir() : preferredDir;
	const std::string& translations = preferredDir.empty() ? TranslationsDir() : preferredDir;

	if (fromTranslations) {
		out.push_back(JoinPath(translations, rel));
	} else if (fromData) {
		out.push_back(JoinPath(DataDir(), rel));
	} else {
		out.push_back(JoinPath(configDir, rel));
		out.push_back(JoinPath(translations, rel));
		out.push_back(JoinPath(DataDir(), rel));
	}
	return out;
}

} // namespace

void SetPluginName(std::string_view name) {
	g_pluginName.assign(name);
	InvalidateCaches();
}

const std::string& PluginName() {
	return g_pluginName;
}

void SetConfigDir(std::string_view dir) {
	g_configDirOverride.assign(dir);
	InvalidateCaches();
}

void SetTranslationsDir(std::string_view dir) {
	g_translationsDirOverride.assign(dir);
	InvalidateCaches();
}

const std::string& ConfigDir() {
	if (!g_dirsCached) {
		g_configDir = !g_configDirOverride.empty()
						  ? g_configDirOverride
						  : (g_pluginName.empty() ? CfgRoot() : JoinPath(CfgRoot(), g_pluginName));
		g_translationsDir = !g_translationsDirOverride.empty()
								? g_translationsDirOverride
								: JoinPath(g_configDir, "translations");
		g_dataDir = g_pluginName.empty() ? DataRoot() : JoinPath(DataRoot(), g_pluginName);
		g_dirsCached = true;
	}
	return g_configDir;
}

const std::string& TranslationsDir() {
	(void)ConfigDir(); // fills every cache
	return g_translationsDir;
}

const std::string& DataDir() {
	(void)ConfigDir();
	return g_dataDir;
}

std::string JoinPath(std::string_view a, std::string_view b) {
	if (a.empty()) {
		return std::string(b);
	}
	if (b.empty()) {
		return std::string(a);
	}
	std::string out(a);
	if (out.back() != '/') {
		out.push_back('/');
	}
	if (b.front() == '/') {
		b.remove_prefix(1);
	}
	out.append(b);
	return out;
}

bool FileExists(std::string_view path) {
	if (path.empty()) {
		return false;
	}
	std::ifstream file(std::string(path), std::ios::binary);
	return file.good();
}

std::string ReadFile(std::string_view path, bool* ok) {
	std::string content;
	std::ifstream file(std::string(path), std::ios::binary);
	if (!file) {
		if (ok) {
			*ok = false;
		}
		return content;
	}
	std::ostringstream buffer;
	buffer << file.rdbuf();
	content = buffer.str();
	if (ok) {
		*ok = true;
	}
	return content;
}

std::string ResolvePath(std::string_view path) {
	if (path.empty()) {
		return {};
	}
	std::string resolved = FirstExisting(Candidates(path, {}));
	if (resolved.empty()) {
		// Nothing on disk: hand back the most likely location so callers can log a useful path.
		const auto candidates = Candidates(path, {});
		if (!candidates.empty()) {
			resolved = candidates.size() > 1 ? candidates[1] : candidates.front();
		}
	}
	return resolved;
}

std::string ResolveTranslationsPath(std::string_view path) {
	if (path.empty()) {
		return {};
	}
	std::string file(path);
	if (file.size() < 4 || file.compare(file.size() - 4, 4, ".txt") != 0) {
		file += ".txt"; // Pisex's LoadTranslations() takes "menus.phrases" and appends ".txt"
	}
	const std::string direct = FirstExisting({file, JoinPath(TranslationsDir(), file), JoinPath(ConfigDir(), file)});
	if (!direct.empty()) {
		return direct;
	}
	// "addons/translations/admin_system.phrases.txt" and friends.
	std::string_view relative = file;
	if (auto rest = StripPrefix(file, "addons/translations/"); !rest.empty()) {
		relative = rest;
	}
	const std::string candidate = JoinPath(TranslationsDir(), relative);
	if (FileExists(candidate)) {
		return candidate;
	}
	return candidate;
}

std::string ResolveDataPath(std::string_view path) {
	if (path.empty()) {
		return {};
	}
	std::string file(path);
	if (auto rest = StripPrefix(file, "addons/data/"); !rest.empty()) {
		file = std::string(rest);
	}
	const std::string candidate = JoinPath(DataDir(), file);
	return FileExists(candidate) ? candidate : candidate;
}

} // namespace pisex
```

`libs/pisexcompat/src/phrases.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <pisex/phrases.hpp>

#include <pisex/compat.hpp>
#include <pisex/keyvalues.hpp>
#include <pisex/paths.hpp>

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>
#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <string>
#include <utility>

namespace pisex {

PhraseMap g_translations;

namespace {

// cs2-menus/utils.h: colors_text[] / colors_hex[], same order, same bytes. The last entry is the
// chat line break: "\n" -> U+2029 (e2 80 a9), which the CS2 chat renderer shows as a new line.
struct ColorTag {
	std::string_view tag;
	std::string_view bytes;
};

constexpr std::array<ColorTag, 17> kColorTags = {{{"{DEFAULT}", "\x01"},
												  {"{WHITE}", "\x01"},
												  {"{RED}", "\x02"},
												  {"{LIGHTPURPLE}", "\x03"},
												  {"{GREEN}", "\x04"},
												  {"{LIME}", "\x05"},
												  {"{LIGHTGREEN}", "\x06"},
												  {"{DARKRED}", "\x07"},
												  {"{GRAY}", "\x08"},
												  {"{LIGHTOLIVE}", "\x09"},
												  {"{OLIVE}", "\x10"},
												  {"{LIGHTBLUE}", "\x0B"},
												  {"{BLUE}", "\x0C"},
												  {"{PURPLE}", "\x0E"},
												  {"{LIGHTRED}", "\x0F"},
												  {"{GRAYBLUE}", "\x0A"},
												  {"\\n", "\xe2\x80\xa9"}}};

std::string g_language;
bool g_languageDetected = false;

// The Pisex server language: cs2-menus read "ServerLang" from addons/configs/core.cfg.
// The Plugify equivalent of that shared file is <configs>/core.cfg; empty when there is none.
std::string CoreConfigLanguage() {
	if (!plg::GetConfigsDir) {
		return {};
	}
	std::string path(plg::GetConfigsDir());
	if (path.empty()) {
		return {};
	}
	if (path.back() != '/') {
		path.push_back('/');
	}
	path += "core.cfg";
	KeyValues core("Core");
	if (!FileExists(path) || !core.LoadFromFile(path.c_str())) {
		return {};
	}
	const char* language = core.GetString("ServerLang", "");
	return language != nullptr ? std::string(language) : std::string();
}

// One language for every phrase of the plugin, like Pisex: core.cfg "ServerLang" first, then
// s2sdk's ServerLanguage (envs/plugins/s2sdk/settings.jsonc). Both are plain config reads, so
// this works at plugin start (the phrases are loaded there) - no map is needed.
std::string DetectLanguage() {
	if (const std::string core = CoreConfigLanguage(); !core.empty()) {
		return NormalizeLanguage(core);
	}
	if (!__s2sdk_GetServerLanguage) {
		return std::string(kFallbackLanguage);
	}
	try {
		const plg::string serverLanguage = s2sdk::GetServerLanguage();
		if (serverLanguage.empty()) {
			return std::string(kFallbackLanguage);
		}
		return NormalizeLanguage(std::string_view(serverLanguage));
	} catch (...) {
		return std::string(kFallbackLanguage);
	}
}

} // namespace

std::string StripColorTags(std::string_view text) {
	std::string out(text);
	for (const ColorTag& color : kColorTags) {
		const std::string_view replacement = color.tag == "\\n" ? std::string_view("\n") : std::string_view();
		std::size_t pos = 0;
		while ((pos = out.find(color.tag, pos)) != std::string::npos) {
			out.replace(pos, color.tag.size(), replacement);
			pos += replacement.size();
		}
	}
	return out;
}

std::string Colorize(std::string_view text) {
	std::string out(text);
	for (const ColorTag& color : kColorTags) {
		std::size_t pos = 0;
		while ((pos = out.find(color.tag, pos)) != std::string::npos) {
			out.replace(pos, color.tag.size(), color.bytes);
			pos += color.bytes.size();
		}
	}
	return out;
}

std::string NormalizeLanguage(std::string_view name) {
	std::string lower;
	lower.reserve(name.size());
	for (const char c : name) {
		lower.push_back(static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c))));
	}
	// Source language names -> the codes used by the Pisex phrase files.
	if (lower == "russian" || lower == "ru") return "ru";
	if (lower == "english" || lower == "en") return "en";
	if (lower == "ukrainian" || lower == "ua" || lower == "uk") return "ua";
	if (lower == "portuguese" || lower == "pt-br" || lower == "brazilian") return "pt-BR";
	if (lower == "spanish" || lower == "es") return "es";
	if (lower == "german" || lower == "de") return "de";
	if (lower == "french" || lower == "fr") return "fr";
	if (lower == "polish" || lower == "pl") return "pl";
	if (lower == "turkish" || lower == "tr") return "tr";
	if (lower == "schinese" || lower == "zh-cn") return "zh-CN";
	return std::string(name);
}

bool LoadPhrasesFile(const char* file, PhraseMap& out, const char* language) {
	if (!file || !*file) {
		return false;
	}
	KeyValues root("Phrases");
	if (!root.LoadFromFile(ResolveTranslationsPath(file))) {
		return false;
	}

	if (!language || !*language) {
		language = PhrasesLanguage().c_str();
	}
	const std::string fallback(kFallbackLanguage);

	for (KeyValues* key = root.GetFirstTrueSubKey(); key; key = key->GetNextTrueSubKey()) {
		std::string text;
		if (const KeyValues* localized = key->FindKey(language); localized && localized->HasValue()) {
			text = std::string(localized->GetStringValue());
		}
		if (text.empty() && std::string_view(language) != fallback) {
			if (const KeyValues* english = key->FindKey(fallback.data()); english && english->HasValue()) {
				text = std::string(english->GetStringValue());
			}
		}
		if (text.empty()) {
			// Last resort: any language the file has, so a partially translated file still shows
			// something instead of an empty chat line.
			for (KeyValues* candidate = key->GetFirstValue(); candidate; candidate = candidate->GetNextValue()) {
				if (candidate->HasValue()) {
					text = std::string(candidate->GetStringValue());
					break;
				}
			}
		}
		out[key->GetName()] = std::move(text);
	}
	return true;
}

bool LoadPhrases(const char* file, const char* language) {
	return LoadPhrasesFile(file, g_translations, language);
}

void SetPhrasesLanguage(std::string_view language) {
	g_language.assign(language);
	g_languageDetected = true;
}

const std::string& PhrasesLanguage() {
	if (!g_languageDetected) {
		g_language = DetectLanguage();
	}
	return g_language;
}

const std::string& GetPhrase(const char* key) {
	static const std::string empty;
	if (!key) {
		return empty;
	}
	const auto found = g_translations.find(key);
	return found == g_translations.end() ? empty : found->second;
}

const char* GetPhraseCStr(const char* key) {
	if (!key) {
		return "";
	}
	const auto found = g_translations.find(key);
	return found == g_translations.end() ? key : found->second.c_str();
}

} // namespace pisex
```

`libs/pisexcompat/src/players.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <pisex/players.hpp>
#include <pisex/schema.hpp>

#include <pisex/compat.hpp>
#include <pisex/output.hpp>

#include <plg/numerics.hpp>
#include <plg/string.hpp>
#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <array>
#include <cctype>
#include <cstdint>
#include <exception>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {
namespace {

std::vector<OnClientAuthorizedCallback> g_authorizedHooks;
bool g_authorizedListenerRegistered = false;

// s2sdk OnClientAuthenticated listener; must not throw into the engine.
void OnClientAuthorizedListener(int32_t playerSlot, uint64_t steamid64) {
	try {
		const std::vector<OnClientAuthorizedCallback> callbacks = g_authorizedHooks;
		for (const OnClientAuthorizedCallback& callback : callbacks) {
			if (callback) {
				callback(playerSlot, steamid64);
			}
		}
	} catch (const std::exception& ex) {
		ErrorLog("pisexcompat: OnClientAuthorized callback threw: %s", ex.what());
	} catch (...) {
		ErrorLog("pisexcompat: OnClientAuthorized callback threw an unknown exception");
	}
}

// Pisex returned engine-owned strings, so a pointer stayed valid. The wrappers keep one string per
// slot: GetPlayerName(a) and GetPlayerName(b) in the same expression both stay valid, which would
// not hold with a single scratch buffer.
constexpr int kSlots = 64;
std::array<std::string, kSlots> g_nameCache;
std::array<std::string, kSlots> g_ipCache;
std::array<std::string, kSlots> g_authCache;
std::array<std::string, kSlots> g_languageCache;

bool Ready(int slot) {
	return IsGameReady() && slot >= 0 && slot < kSlots;
}

// Layer 1 of the client guard: the slot has a client object and the client is connected.
// s2sdk's Player::GetClient() -> utils::GetClientBySlot() needs the server's client list, which
// only exists with a map up (hence Ready()), and answers nullptr - never a crash - for a slot
// whose controller entity does not exist yet (a client that is still connecting). Bots are real
// connected clients and pass. Used by every wrapper whose s2sdk export touches the client object.
bool ClientExists(int slot) {
	return Ready(slot) && __s2sdk_IsClientConnected && s2sdk::IsClientConnected(slot);
}

// Layer 2: the slot also has a controller entity. Player::SetName (SetClientName) dereferences
// the client *and* the controller without any check - a crash seen right after a map start while
// the bots were being created (Player::SetName -> client->GetPlayerSlot() with a null client).
// Everything that reaches the controller/pawn goes through this.
bool ControllerExists(int slot) {
	return ClientExists(slot) && pisex::GetControllerEntity(slot) != 0;
}

// Layer 3: the controller also has a current pawn. The s2sdk exports implemented with
// helpers::GetController2 (GetClientHealth, GetClientArmor, GetClientTeam, RespawnClient,
// ForcePlayerSuicide, SetClientMoveType, TeleportClient, GetClientAbsOrigin, ...) print
// "Cannot execute '...' on invalid player pawn: N" to the console for a controller without one
// (typically a client that is still connecting) and answer nothing. GetClientPawn
// only needs the controller, so it checks silently.
bool PawnExists(int slot) {
	if (!ControllerExists(slot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientPawn) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::GetClientPawn(slot) != nullptr;
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

std::string ToLower(std::string_view text) {
	std::string out(text);
	for (char& c : out) {
		c = static_cast<char>(std::tolower(static_cast<unsigned char>(c)));
	}
	return out;
}

void Assign(plg::string value, std::string& out) {
	out.assign(value.data(), value.size());
}

} // namespace

void HookOnClientAuthorized(const OnClientAuthorizedCallback& callback) {
	if (!callback || !__s2sdk_OnClientAuthenticated_Register) {
		return;
	}
	g_authorizedHooks.push_back(callback);
	if (!g_authorizedListenerRegistered) {
		s2sdk::OnClientAuthenticated_Register(&OnClientAuthorizedListener);
		g_authorizedListenerRegistered = true;
	}
}

void RemoveAllPlayerHooks() {
	if (g_authorizedListenerRegistered && __s2sdk_OnClientAuthenticated_Unregister) {
		s2sdk::OnClientAuthenticated_Unregister(&OnClientAuthorizedListener);
		g_authorizedListenerRegistered = false;
	}
	g_authorizedHooks.clear();
}

bool IsFakeClient(int iSlot) {
	if (!Ready(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_IsFakeClient) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::IsFakeClient(iSlot);
	} catch (...) {
		return true; // treat as unavailable rather than as a real player
	}
}

bool IsConnected(int iSlot) {
	if (!Ready(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_IsClientConnected) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::IsClientConnected(iSlot);
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

bool IsInGame(int iSlot) {
	if (!Ready(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_IsClientInGame) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::IsClientInGame(iSlot);
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

bool IsAuthenticated(int iSlot) {
	if (!Ready(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_IsClientAuthorized) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::IsClientAuthorized(iSlot);
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

bool IsAlive(int iSlot) {
	if (!Ready(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_IsClientAlive) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::IsClientAlive(iSlot);
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

uint64_t GetSteamID64(int iSlot) {
	// The s2sdk call itself is null-safe, but for a slot that is not connected it answers from
	// Player::m_unauthenticatedSteamID - which keeps the *previous* occupant's id after a
	// disconnect. Pisex/Metamod returned 0 for a slot without a client; so do we.
	if (!ClientExists(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientSteamID64) {
		return 0;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::GetClientSteamID64(iSlot);
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

const char* GetSteamID(int iSlot) {
	if (!ClientExists(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientAuthId) {
		return "";
	}
	try {
		Assign(s2sdk::GetClientAuthId(iSlot), g_authCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)]);
	} catch (...) {
		g_authCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].clear();
	}
	return g_authCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].c_str();
}

const char* GetPlayerName(int iSlot) {
	if (!ControllerExists(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientName) {
		return "";
	}
	try {
		std::string& cached = g_nameCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)];
		Assign(s2sdk::GetClientName(iSlot), cached);
		// s2sdk answers "<unknown>" when it cannot resolve the client (Player::GetName); the
		// Pisex API returned an empty string there, and callers treat "" as "no name".
		if (cached == "<unknown>") {
			cached.clear();
		}
	} catch (...) {
		g_nameCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].clear();
	}
	return g_nameCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].c_str();
}

void SetPlayerName(int iSlot, const char* szName) {
	// Player::SetName crashes for a slot without a client or without a controller (both are
	// dereferenced unchecked) - never call SetClientName unless the slot is fully in place.
	if (!ControllerExists(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_SetClientName) {
		return;
	}
	try {
		s2sdk::SetClientName(iSlot, plg::string(szName ? szName : ""));
	} catch (...) {
	}
}

const char* GetIpAddress(int iSlot) {
	// Player::GetIpAddress reads the client's net channel, which is null for bots (and only
	// exists once the client is connected): return "" instead of crashing.
	if (!ClientExists(iSlot) || IsFakeClient(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientIp) {
		return "";
	}
	try {
		Assign(s2sdk::GetClientIp(iSlot), g_ipCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)]);
	} catch (...) {
		g_ipCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].clear();
	}
	return g_ipCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].c_str();
}

const char* GetClientLanguage(int iSlot) {
	// Player::GetLanguage returns a cached member (no client dereference), so the plain map-level
	// gate is enough - and it keeps the language s2sdk already knows for a client that is still
	// connecting.
	if (!Ready(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientLanguage) {
		return "";
	}
	try {
		Assign(s2sdk::GetClientLanguage(iSlot), g_languageCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)]);
	} catch (...) {
		g_languageCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].clear();
	}
	return g_languageCache[static_cast<std::size_t>(iSlot)].c_str();
}

int FindPlayer(uint64_t iSteamID64) {
	if (!IsGameReady() || iSteamID64 == 0) {
		return -1;
	}
	const int maxPlayers = GetMaxPlayers();
	for (int slot = 0; slot < maxPlayers; ++slot) {
		if (!IsConnected(slot) || IsFakeClient(slot)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (GetSteamID64(slot) == iSteamID64) {
			return slot;
		}
	}
	return -1;
}

int FindPlayer(const char* szName) {
	if (!IsGameReady() || !szName || !*szName) {
		return -1;
	}
	const std::string wanted = ToLower(szName);
	if (wanted.empty()) {
		return -1;
	}
	const int maxPlayers = GetMaxPlayers();
	// Exact (case-insensitive) match first - cs2-menus compares the name for equality.
	for (int slot = 0; slot < maxPlayers; ++slot) {
		if (!IsConnected(slot) || IsFakeClient(slot)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (ToLower(GetPlayerName(slot)) == wanted) {
			return slot;
		}
	}
	// Substring match as a convenience (the admin core's "find by name" menu uses prefixes).
	for (int slot = 0; slot < maxPlayers; ++slot) {
		if (!IsConnected(slot) || IsFakeClient(slot)) {
			continue;
		}
		if (ToLower(GetPlayerName(slot)).find(wanted) != std::string::npos) {
			return slot;
		}
	}
	return -1;
}

int GetPlayerTeam(int iSlot) {
	// The team lives on the controller (CBaseEntity::m_iTeamNum, what Pisex read). s2sdk's
	// GetClientTeam goes through the pawn: it answered 0 - and printed a console warning - for every
	// client without a current pawn, so read the controller's field at the cached offset instead.
	if (!ControllerExists(iSlot)) {
		return 0;
	}
	static int s_teamOffset = -1;
	if (s_teamOffset < 0 && __s2sdk_GetEntData2 && __s2sdk_PlayerSlotToEntPointer) {
		s_teamOffset = SchemaOffset("CBaseEntity", "m_iTeamNum");
	}
	try {
		if (s_teamOffset >= 0) {
			void* controller = s2sdk::PlayerSlotToEntPointer(iSlot);
			return controller ? static_cast<int>(s2sdk::GetEntData2(controller, s_teamOffset, 1) & 0xFF) : 0;
		}
		// No offset/binding: the pawn-based export, asked only when a pawn exists (silent otherwise).
		return PawnExists(iSlot) && __s2sdk_GetClientTeam ? static_cast<int>(s2sdk::GetClientTeam(iSlot)) : 0;
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

	} catch (...) {

int GetOwnerSlot(int iEntity) {
	if (!IsGameReady() || !__s2sdk_GetEntityOwner || !__s2sdk_ClientPtrToPlayerSlot || !__s2sdk_EntIndexToEntPointer) {
		return -1;
	}
	try {
		const int handle = EntIndexToEntHandle(iEntity); // s2sdk wants/returns handles, not indices
		if (handle == -1) {
			return -1;
		}
		const int owner = EntHandleToEntIndex(s2sdk::GetEntityOwner(handle));
		if (owner <= 0) {
			return -1;
		}
		void* pointer = s2sdk::EntIndexToEntPointer(owner);
		return pointer ? s2sdk::ClientPtrToPlayerSlot(pointer) : -1;
	} catch (...) {
		return -1;
	}
}

bool IsClientReady(int iSlot) {
	return ControllerExists(iSlot);
}

int GetMaxPlayers() {
	if (!__s2sdk_GetMaxClients) {
		return kSlots;
	}
	try {
		const int maxClients = s2sdk::GetMaxClients();
		return maxClients > 0 && maxClients <= kSlots ? maxClients : kSlots;
	} catch (...) {
		return kSlots;
	}
}
```

```cpp
#include <pisex/schema.hpp>

#include <stdexcept>

#include <pisex/compat.hpp>
#include <pisex/output.hpp>
#include <pisex/players.hpp>

#include <plg/string.hpp>
#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <utility>

namespace pisex {
namespace {

std::unordered_map<std::string, int> g_offsetCache;
std::string g_stringCache; // GetEntString() return value, refreshed per call

const char* Safe(const char* text) {
	return text ? text : "";
}

bool ValidEntity(int entity) {
	// Every s2sdk entity export dereferences g_pGameEntitySystem without a null check - it is only
	// assigned in s2sdk's ServerStartup, so an entity query before the first map (or on a server
	// that never started one) is a null dereference, i.e. a dead server. s2sdk's own
	// timer/listener paths never guard this; pisexcompat refuses the call until the first Poll()
	// with a map instead.
	// No entities exist before that point, so every wrapper returns its default.
	return IsGameReady() && entity > 0 && entity < 1 << 15;
}

// s2sdk takes and returns CEntityHandle ints (entry index | serial << 15), NOT entity indices.
// The pisex API keeps Pisex's "int = entity index" convention, so every s2sdk call converts.
// Throws when the entity does not exist: callers' try/catch turn that into the default value
// (and s2sdk never logs "invalid entity handle" for it).
int32_t HandleOf(int iEntity) {
	if (!ValidEntity(iEntity) || !__s2sdk_EntIndexToEntHandle) {
		throw std::runtime_error("pisexcompat: invalid entity index");
	}
	const int32_t handle = s2sdk::EntIndexToEntHandle(iEntity);
	if (handle == -1) {
		throw std::runtime_error("pisexcompat: entity index has no live entity");
	}
	return handle;
}

int IndexOf(int32_t iHandle) {
	if (iHandle == -1 || iHandle == 0 || !__s2sdk_EntHandleToEntIndex) {
		return 0;
	}
	const int index = s2sdk::EntHandleToEntIndex(iHandle);
	return index > 0 ? index : 0;
}

// Builds the cache key in a reused buffer: a by-value key allocated on every lookup (cache hits
// included - "CCSPlayerPawn" + "m_hController" is past the SSO limit), and the typed schema helpers
// are called from per-event and per-slot code. Valid until the next call on the same thread.
const std::string& CacheKey(std::string_view cls, std::string_view field) {
	thread_local std::string key;
	key.clear();
	key.append(cls);
	key.push_back('\0');
	key.append(field);
	return key;
}

// Schema field that links a CCSPlayerPawn back to its controller.
constexpr const char* kPawnClass = "CCSPlayerPawn";

} // namespace

int SchemaOffset(const char* className, const char* fieldName) {
	if (!className || !fieldName || !*className || !*fieldName) {
		return -1;
	}
	const std::string& key = CacheKey(className, fieldName);
	const auto cached = g_offsetCache.find(key);
	if (cached != g_offsetCache.end()) {
		return cached->second;
	}
	int offset = -1;
	if (__s2sdk_GetSchemaOffset) {
		try {
			offset = s2sdk::GetSchemaOffset(plg::string(className), plg::string(fieldName));
		} catch (...) {
			offset = -1;
		}
	}
	if (offset >= 0) {
		// Only successful lookups are cached: before the schema system is initialised (no map yet)
		// every lookup fails, and a cached -1 would poison the field for the rest of the session.
		g_offsetCache.emplace(key, offset);
	}
	return offset;
}

int SchemaChainOffset(const char* className) {
	// s2sdk's SafeNetworkStateChanged() reads a chain offset >= 0 as "the object's
	// __m_pChainEntity sits at object + offset": answering 0 for "no chainer" (or for a missing
	// binding) would make it treat the object's vtable as a chainer. -1 is the "the object itself
	// is the entity" sentinel, so an absent or non-positive offset is normalised to -1.
	if (!className || !__s2sdk_GetSchemaChainOffset) {
		return -1;
	}
	try {
		const int offset = s2sdk::GetSchemaChainOffset(plg::string(className));
		return offset > 0 ? offset : -1;
	} catch (...) {
		return -1;
	}
}

bool IsSchemaFieldNetworked(const char* className, const char* fieldName) {
	if (!className || !fieldName || !__s2sdk_IsSchemaFieldNetworked) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::IsSchemaFieldNetworked(plg::string(className), plg::string(fieldName));
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

bool IsValidEntity(int iEntity) {
	if (!ValidEntity(iEntity) || !__s2sdk_EntIndexToEntPointer) {
		return false;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::EntIndexToEntPointer(iEntity) != nullptr;
	} catch (...) {
		return false;
	}
}

void* EntIndexToEntPointer(int iEntity) {
	if (!ValidEntity(iEntity) || !__s2sdk_EntIndexToEntPointer) {
		return nullptr;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::EntIndexToEntPointer(iEntity);
	} catch (...) {
		return nullptr;
	}
}

	if (!pointer || !__s2sdk_EntPointerToEntIndex) {
		return 0;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::EntPointerToEntIndex(pointer);
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

int EntIndexToEntHandle(int iEntity) {
	if (!ValidEntity(iEntity) || !__s2sdk_EntIndexToEntHandle) {
		return -1;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::EntIndexToEntHandle(iEntity);
	} catch (...) {
		return -1;
	}
}

int EntHandleToEntIndex(int iHandle) {
	// A handle is index | serial << 15 in 32 bits: once the game's serial counter passes 65535 a
	// valid handle is a negative int. Only INVALID_EHANDLE_INDEX (-1) is invalid; 0 (the world) is
	// never an entity a plugin asks about and keeps meaning "none".
	if (iHandle == -1 || iHandle == 0 || !__s2sdk_EntHandleToEntIndex) {
		return 0;
	}
	try {
		return s2sdk::EntHandleToEntIndex(iHandle);
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

		return {};

		return {};
	}
}

int FindEntityByClassname(int iStart, const char* className) {
	// IsGameReady() is required, not just for the entity system pointer: the export dereferences it
	// before it even looks at the arguments. EntIndexToEntHandle is called for the start index, so
	// its binding is required as well.
	if (!IsGameReady() || !className || !*className || !__s2sdk_FindEntityByClassname ||
		(iStart > 0 && !__s2sdk_EntIndexToEntHandle)) {
		return 0;
	}
	try {
		const int32_t start = iStart > 0 ? s2sdk::EntIndexToEntHandle(iStart) : -1;
		return IndexOf(s2sdk::FindEntityByClassname(start, plg::string(className)));
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

int GetPlayerPawn(int iSlot) {
	// GetClientPawn logs "invalid player slot" (helpers::GetController) for an empty slot; the
	// client guard keeps loops over all 64 slots silent and matches s2sdk's own result (0).
	if (!IsClientReady(iSlot) || !__s2sdk_GetClientPawn) {
		return 0;
	}
	try {
		void* pawn = s2sdk::GetClientPawn(iSlot);
		return pawn ? EntPointerToEntIndex(pawn) : 0;
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

int GetPlayerController(int iSlot) {
	if (!IsGameReady() || iSlot < 0 || iSlot >= GetMaxPlayers() || !__s2sdk_PlayerSlotToEntPointer) {
		return 0;
	}
	try {
		void* controller = s2sdk::PlayerSlotToEntPointer(iSlot);
		return controller ? EntPointerToEntIndex(controller) : 0;
	} catch (...) {
		return 0;
	}
}

int GetPawnController(int iPawn) {
	const int controller = GetEntEntity(iPawn, kPawnClass, "m_hController");
	if (controller != 0) {
		return controller;
	}
	// Some maps/versions keep the link only as a raw entity component; the schema name is stable
	// across the CS2 builds we target, so an empty result simply means "no controller".
	return 0;
}
```

`libs/pisexcompat/src/timers.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <pisex/timers.hpp>

#include <pisex/compat.hpp> // IsGameReady(): callbacks must not run while no map is up
#include <pisex/output.hpp>

#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <cstddef>
#include <deque>
#include <exception>
#include <memory>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <unordered_set>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace pisex {
namespace {

// How many dead handles are remembered so that RemoveTimer() on an already dead timer stays a
// no-op. One entry is a pointer, so the cap costs ~160 KB at the very most; a plugin that keeps a
// handle across thousands of other timer lifetimes is buggy anyway (Pisex would have crashed).
constexpr std::size_t kMaxDeadHandles = 4096;

// Owns the CTimer objects. The plugin only ever holds raw CTimer* handles (Pisex's CreateTimer
// returns a raw pointer) and Pisex frees a timer the moment it stops, so ported cleanup code
// routinely calls RemoveTimer() on a dead handle - stopped handles are remembered for that reason.
//
// One thread (the game thread) touches this class, but at two different points of the frame:
//   * from TimerSystem::RunFrame() -> Trampoline() -> OnFire() - the engine is inside its own
//     callback loop here, so OnFire() makes no s2sdk timer call at all: it only records what the
//     callback wants. (A callback that removes its own timer does call KillsTimer through
//     Remove(); the engine defers the erase for a timer that is executing, so that is safe. What
//     is *not* safe is touching the CTimer after the callback returned, or freeing it while the
//     callback is on the stack - both are handled by Firing_/pendingReap_.)
//   * from pisex::Poll() -> Process(), which does the killing/rescheduling after the engine loop,
//   * from plugin code (game thread as well) -> Create()/Remove().
class TimerRegistry {
public:
	TimerRegistry() = default;
	TimerRegistry(const TimerRegistry&) = delete;
	TimerRegistry& operator=(const TimerRegistry&) = delete;

	CTimer* Create(float interval, std::function<float()> fn) {
		if (!__s2sdk_CreateTimer || fn == nullptr) {
			return nullptr;
		}
		auto timer = std::make_unique<CTimer>();
		TimerAccess::Interval(*timer) = interval;
		TimerAccess::Fn(*timer) = std::move(fn);

		// The delay handed to s2sdk is floored at one server tick (see ClampTimerDelay: the
		// backend re-inserts a repeating timer at universalTime + the *stored* delay, so a 0 would
		// loop forever inside one RunFrame()). The CTimer keeps the value the plugin asked for, so
		// GetInterval()/SetInterval() stay Pisex-shaped.
		// Repeat: the timer stays alive until we kill it. Deliberately *without* NoMapChange -
		// the Pisex timers keep running across map changes (the admin core's punishment-expiry
		// timer relies on that).
		const s2sdk::TimerId id =
			s2sdk::CreateTimer(ClampTimerDelay(static_cast<double>(interval)), &TimerRegistry::Trampoline,
							   s2sdk::TimerFlag::Repeat, plg::vector<plg::any>{});
		// s2sdk's ids start at 0 (TimerSystem::m_nextId{}), so id 0 is a real timer - only the
		// documented -1 means "could not create". Treating 0 as failure broke the process's first
		// timer (the plugin got nullptr) and leaked its untracked engine timer.
		if (id == static_cast<s2sdk::TimerId>(-1)) {
			return nullptr;
		}

		CTimer* raw = timer.release();
		// The dead-handle bookkeeping (dead_) matches raw pointer *values*, and CTimer objects are
		// recycled by the allocator: a fresh timer can be allocated at the address of one that was
		// removed earlier. Forget any stale entry for that address, or the new timer would be
		// treated as dead by the first RemoveTimer() call (silently not stopping it) and by OnFire()
		// (which would free the live object after its first callback - a use-after-free).
		dead_.erase(raw);
		TimerAccess::Id(*raw) = id;
		byId_[id] = raw;
		live_.insert(raw);
		return raw;
	}

	void Remove(CTimer* timer) {
		if (!timer || Gone(timer) || live_.count(timer) == 0) {
			return; // unknown, already dead, or stopped and waiting for Process() to reap it
		}
		Kill(timer);
		MarkDead(timer);
		// Both registries must forget the object before it goes away: a leftover byId_ entry would
		// be dereferenced by the engine's next fire (use-after-free - and for id 0, the engine
		// timer was never even killed), a leftover live_ entry would be written to and freed a
		// second time by Clear() during Shutdown().
		byId_.erase(TimerAccess::Id(*timer));
		live_.erase(timer);
		if (TimerAccess::Firing(*timer)) {
			// Called from inside this timer's own callback: the callback still owns the object -
			// OnFire() reads it once more when the callback returns - and fn_ is executing right
			// now, so neither the object nor fn_ may be touched here. OnFire() frees the object as
			// soon as the callback has returned (the registries no longer know it, so the handle
			// is dead and the engine timer is gone).
			return;
		}
		TimerAccess::Fn(*timer) = nullptr;
		delete timer;
	}

	// Game thread, once per frame (pisex::Poll).
	void Process() {
		const std::vector<CTimer*> reschedule = std::move(pendingReschedule_);
		pendingReschedule_.clear();
		for (CTimer* timer : reschedule) {
			if (Gone(timer) || live_.count(timer) == 0 || !TimerAccess::Alive(*timer)) {
				continue;
			}
			if (!IsGameReady()) {
				// No map (or a map change in progress): callbacks must not run, so the timer
				// stays parked - Pending is still set, which makes OnFire() ignore the engine's
				// repeated fires. Keep it queued and re-arm it on the first ready Poll.
				pendingReschedule_.push_back(timer);
				continue;
			}
			const bool postponed = TimerAccess::Postponed(*timer);
			TimerAccess::Postponed(*timer) = false;
			TimerAccess::Pending(*timer) = false;
			if (__s2sdk_RescheduleTimer) {
				try {
					// Same clamp as Create(): the value the callback returned (Pisex's "0 = next
					// frame" included) must never reach the backend below one tick, or the
					// engine's RunFrame() re-fires this repeating timer inside the same frame.
					// A fire that was postponed over the map change is re-armed with one tick so
					// the callback runs as soon as the engine can again (the delay the callback
					// returns then governs the following runs).
					s2sdk::RescheduleTimer(TimerAccess::Id(*timer),
										   postponed ? kMinTimerDelay
													 : ClampTimerDelay(static_cast<double>(TimerAccess::Interval(*timer))));
				} catch (...) {
					Kill(timer);
					MarkDead(timer);
					byId_.erase(TimerAccess::Id(*timer));
					live_.erase(timer);
					TimerAccess::Fn(*timer) = nullptr;
					stragglers_.erase(timer);
					delete timer;
				}
			}
		}

		const std::vector<CTimer*> reap = std::move(pendingReap_);
		pendingReap_.clear();
		for (CTimer* timer : reap) {
			// Queued exactly once: Remove()/OnFire() only queue an object they also just erased
			// from live_/byId_ (a second RemoveTimer() call on it is a no-op), and the object is
			// still allocated here. The kill is what stops the engine timer of a one-shot whose
			// callback returned a negative delay - OnFire() itself makes no s2sdk call. Killing an
			// id Remove() already killed is a no-op.
			stragglers_.erase(timer);
			Kill(timer);
			delete timer;
		}
	}

	void Clear() {
		for (const auto& entry : byId_) {
			Kill(entry.second);
		}
		for (CTimer* timer : live_) {
			if (TimerAccess::Firing(*timer)) {
				// Shutdown() came from inside this timer's own callback: the callback still owns
				// the object and fn_ is on the stack. OnFire() frees the object once the callback
				// returned (the engine timer was killed above, so it never runs again); freeing or
				// clearing fn_ here would be a use-after-free.
				continue;
			}
			TimerAccess::Alive(*timer) = false;
			TimerAccess::Fn(*timer) = nullptr;
			delete timer;
		}
		for (CTimer* timer : stragglers_) { // stopped or removed, waiting for a Process()
			delete timer;
		}
		live_.clear();
		byId_.clear();
		dead_.clear();
		deadOrder_.clear();
		stragglers_.clear();
		pendingReschedule_.clear();
		pendingReap_.clear();
	}

	// Engine thread; must never throw.
	static void Trampoline(uint32_t id, const plg::vector<plg::any>& userData) {
		(void)userData;
		try {
			Instance().OnFire(id);
		} catch (...) {
		}
	}

	static TimerRegistry& Instance() {
		static TimerRegistry registry;
		return registry;
	}

private:
	// A pointer that was freed (or is about to be freed by Process) - never dereferenced.
	bool Gone(CTimer* timer) const { return dead_.count(timer) != 0; }

	void MarkDead(CTimer* timer) {
		dead_.insert(timer);
		deadOrder_.push_back(timer);
		while (deadOrder_.size() > kMaxDeadHandles) {
			dead_.erase(deadOrder_.front());
			deadOrder_.pop_front();
		}
	}

	// No s2sdk call here (see the class comment): only bookkeeping.
	void OnFire(uint32_t id) {
		const auto found = byId_.find(id);
		if (found == byId_.end()) {
			return; // timer destroyed on our side
		}
		CTimer* timer = found->second;
		if (!TimerAccess::Alive(*timer) || TimerAccess::Pending(*timer) || !TimerAccess::Fn(*timer)) {
			return; // already ran this frame, waiting for Process() - or postponed (see below)
		}

		if (!IsGameReady()) {
			// No map is up (map end -> next map start): ported callbacks query clients/entities,
			// which s2sdk cannot serve in that window (its client list is gone; a query segfaults
			// at address 0). Do not run the callback now; mark the fire as
			// postponed and let Process() re-arm the timer with one tick on the first ready frame.
			// Pending stays set, so every further engine fire in this window is ignored.
			TimerAccess::Postponed(*timer) = true;
			TimerAccess::Pending(*timer) = true;
			pendingReschedule_.push_back(timer);
			return;
		}

		// While the flag is set, Remove() must not free the object or touch fn_ (the callback is
		// executing it): it only records the removal, and the code below frees the object.
		TimerAccess::Firing(*timer) = true;
		float next = -1.0f;
		try {
			next = TimerAccess::Fn(*timer)();
		} catch (const std::exception& ex) {
			ErrorLog("pisexcompat: timer callback threw: %s", ex.what());
			next = -1.0f;
		} catch (...) {
			ErrorLog("pisexcompat: timer callback threw an unknown exception");
			next = -1.0f;
		}
		TimerAccess::Firing(*timer) = false;

		if (Gone(timer) || live_.count(timer) == 0) {
			// The callback removed its own timer (Pisex handles are raw pointers and ported code
			// does that), or Shutdown() ran inside the callback: Remove()/Clear() killed the
			// engine timer, erased the registries and deliberately left the object for us. The
			// callback has returned by now, so fn_ is no longer executing - free it now (waiting
			// for Process() would leak it whenever Shutdown() is not followed by another Poll()).
			stragglers_.erase(timer);
			delete timer;
			return;
		}

		if (next >= 0.0f) {
			TimerAccess::Alive(*timer) = true;
			TimerAccess::Interval(*timer) = next;
			TimerAccess::Pending(*timer) = true;
			pendingReschedule_.push_back(timer);
			return;
		}

		// The callback wants to stop. Keep the handle valid for the caller (IsAlive() is false,
		// RemoveTimer() on it is a no-op) and let Process() kill the engine timer and free it.
		TimerAccess::Alive(*timer) = false;
		TimerAccess::Fn(*timer) = nullptr;
		byId_.erase(id);
		live_.erase(timer);
		MarkDead(timer);
		stragglers_.insert(timer);
		pendingReap_.push_back(timer);
	}

	void Kill(CTimer* timer) {
		// id 0 is as valid as any other (s2sdk's ids start at 0) - killing it is what makes the
		// first timer of the process work.
		if (__s2sdk_KillsTimer) {
			try {
				s2sdk::KillsTimer(TimerAccess::Id(*timer));
			} catch (...) {
			}
		}
	}

	std::unordered_map<uint32_t, CTimer*> byId_;
	std::unordered_set<CTimer*> live_;
	std::unordered_set<CTimer*> dead_;
	std::deque<CTimer*> deadOrder_;
	std::unordered_set<CTimer*> stragglers_; // stopped timers not yet deleted by Process()
	std::vector<CTimer*> pendingReschedule_;
	std::vector<CTimer*> pendingReap_;
};

std::deque<std::function<void()>> g_nextFrame;

} // namespace

void CTimer::RemoveTimer() {
	pisex::RemoveTimer(this);
}

CTimer* CreateTimer(float flInterval, std::function<float()> fn) {
	try {
		return TimerRegistry::Instance().Create(flInterval, std::move(fn));
	} catch (const std::exception& ex) {
		ErrorLog("pisexcompat: CreateTimer failed: %s", ex.what());
	} catch (...) {
		ErrorLog("pisexcompat: CreateTimer failed with an unknown exception");
	}
	return nullptr;
}

void RemoveTimer(CTimer* timer) {
	try {
		TimerRegistry::Instance().Remove(timer);
	} catch (...) {
	}
}

void NextFrame(std::function<void()> fn) {
	if (fn == nullptr) {
		return;
	}
	g_nextFrame.push_back(std::move(fn));
}

void ProcessTimers() {
	// Next-frame callbacks first: they are the cheapest "later" work a plugin queues, and the
	// budget keeps a callback that queues another one from starving the frame.
	// While no map is up they stay queued ("next frame" cannot mean "during the map change"):
	// they run on the first ready frame, like the postponed timers, so they never see stale slots.
	if (IsGameReady()) {
		std::size_t budget = g_nextFrame.size();
		while (budget-- > 0 && !g_nextFrame.empty()) {
			std::function<void()> fn = std::move(g_nextFrame.front());
			g_nextFrame.pop_front();
			try {
				fn();
			} catch (const std::exception& ex) {
				ErrorLog("pisexcompat: NextFrame callback threw: %s", ex.what());
			} catch (...) {
				ErrorLog("pisexcompat: NextFrame callback threw an unknown exception");
			}
		}
	}
	TimerRegistry::Instance().Process();
}

void ClearTimers() {
	TimerRegistry::Instance().Clear();
	g_nextFrame.clear();
}

} // namespace pisex
```

`libs/pisexcompat/test/commands_engine_test.cpp`:

```cpp
// pisexcompat command-registration test — drives the real CommandTrampoline with a fake s2sdk
// command manager. The global binding __s2sdk_AddConsoleCommand is assigned a fake that records
// every registration (name, flags, callback), and the test then calls the recorded callback the
// way the engine does: caller -1 = the server console, caller >= 0 = a player (from the client
// console or from chat, see ConCommandContext). __s2sdk_AddCommandListener records the chat
// trampoline the same way, so the pre-chat fan-out can be driven too.
//
// The rules under test: RegServerCommand registers a console name without ClientCanExecute and no
// caller slot may reach its handler — a privileged command (vip_give, mm_lvl_reset, …) must only
// run from the server console, like the Metamod CON_COMMAND_F(..., FCVAR_NONE) originals; and the
// chat fan-out must survive a listener that unregisters everything while it runs.
// Run by ../test.sh.

#include <pisex/commands.hpp>
#include <pisex/compat.hpp>

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>

#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// A real plugin gets these from PLUGIFY_PLUGIN; the test leaves them null (no plugify module).
namespace plg {
GetBaseDirFn GetBaseDir{nullptr};
GetExtensionsDirFn GetExtensionsDir{nullptr};
GetConfigsDirFn GetConfigsDir{nullptr};
GetDataDirFn GetDataDir{nullptr};
GetLogsDirFn GetLogsDir{nullptr};
GetCacheDirFn GetCacheDir{nullptr};
IsLoadedFn IsLoaded{nullptr};
LogFn Log{nullptr};
BeginZoneFn BeginZone{nullptr};
EndZoneFn EndZone{nullptr};
} // namespace plg

namespace {

int g_checks = 0;
int g_failures = 0;

void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
	++g_checks;
	if (!condition) {
		++g_failures;
		std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
	}
}

// --- the fake engine ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct FakeCommand {
	std::string name;
	s2sdk::ConVarFlag flags = s2sdk::ConVarFlag::None;
	s2sdk::ConCommandCallback callback = nullptr;
};

std::vector<FakeCommand> g_registered;

bool FakeAddConsoleCommand(const plg::string& name, const plg::string& /*description*/, s2sdk::ConVarFlag flags,
						   s2sdk::ConCommandCallback callback, s2sdk::HookMode /*type*/) {
	g_registered.push_back(FakeCommand{std::string(name.data(), name.size()), flags, callback});
	return true;
}

// The callback s2sdk would invoke for `name` (the first registration wins: duplicate registrations
// only attach a listener to the existing command).
const FakeCommand* FindRegistered(const std::string& name) {
	for (const FakeCommand& command : g_registered) {
		if (command.name == name) {
			return &command;
		}
	}
	return nullptr;
}

s2sdk::ResultType Dispatch(const FakeCommand& command, int32_t caller, s2sdk::ConCommandContext context,
						   std::initializer_list<const char*> args) {
	plg::vector<plg::string> argv;
	for (const char* arg : args) {
		argv.push_back(plg::string(arg));
	}
	return command.callback(caller, context, argv);
}

bool HasFlag(s2sdk::ConVarFlag flags, s2sdk::ConVarFlag flag) {
	return (static_cast<int64_t>(flags) & static_cast<int64_t>(flag)) != 0;
}

// --- the fake listener registry (chat) ---------------------------------------------------------

struct FakeListener {
	std::string name;
	s2sdk::ConCommandCallback callback = nullptr;
};

std::vector<FakeListener> g_listeners;

bool FakeAddCommandListener(const plg::string& name, s2sdk::ConCommandCallback callback, s2sdk::HookMode /*type*/) {
	const std::string key(name.data(), name.size());
	for (FakeListener& listener : g_listeners) {
		if (listener.name == key) {
			listener.callback = callback; // re-registration: same trampoline, one entry per name
			return true;
		}
	}
	g_listeners.push_back(FakeListener{key, callback});
	return true;
}

s2sdk::ConCommandCallback FindListener(const std::string& name) {
	for (const FakeListener& listener : g_listeners) {
		if (listener.name == name) {
			return listener.callback;
		}
	}
	return nullptr;
}

// --- tests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

void TestFlags() {
	pisex::RegCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_client"}, std::vector<std::string>{},
					  [](int, const char*) { return true; });
	pisex::RegServerCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_server"}, [](int, const char*) { return true; });

	const FakeCommand* client = FindRegistered("pix_client");
	const FakeCommand* server = FindRegistered("pix_server");
	Check(client != nullptr && server != nullptr, "both registrations reach s2sdk");
	if (client == nullptr || server == nullptr) {
		return;
	}
	Check(HasFlag(client->flags, s2sdk::ConVarFlag::ClientCanExecute),
		  "RegCommand keeps ClientCanExecute (players may run it)");
	Check(HasFlag(client->flags, s2sdk::ConVarFlag::Release), "RegCommand keeps Release");
	Check(!HasFlag(server->flags, s2sdk::ConVarFlag::ClientCanExecute),
		  "RegServerCommand drops ClientCanExecute");
	Check(HasFlag(server->flags, s2sdk::ConVarFlag::Release), "RegServerCommand keeps Release");
}

void TestServerOnlyDispatch() {
	int serverCalls = 0;
	int clientCalls = 0;
	int lastSlot = -2;
	std::string serverContent;
	pisex::RegServerCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_give"}, [&](int slot, const char* content) {
		++serverCalls;
		lastSlot = slot;
		serverContent = content ? content : "";
		return true;
	});
	pisex::RegCommand({}, std::vector<std::string>{"!pix_vip"}, [&](int, const char*) {
		++clientCalls;
		return true;
	});

	const FakeCommand* command = FindRegistered("pix_give");
	Check(command != nullptr, "pix_give is registered");
	if (command == nullptr) {
		return;
	}

	// The server console (slot -1) runs the handler and sees the registered spelling + arguments.
	Check(Dispatch(*command, -1, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_give", "3", "60", "vip"}) ==
			  s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "the server console call is handled");
	Check(serverCalls == 1 && lastSlot == -1 && serverContent == "pix_give 3 60 vip",
		  "the server console runs the handler");

	// A player (client console) must not reach it; the call is swallowed, not run.
	serverCalls = 0;
	Check(Dispatch(*command, 3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_give", "3", "60", "vip"}) ==
			  s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "a client-console call is swallowed (Handled)");
	Check(serverCalls == 0, "a client-console call never runs the handler");

	// Chat cannot reach it either: the name has no chat registration, and the guard covers the
	// call even if a chat dispatch finds it.
	Check(Dispatch(*command, 3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Chat, {"pix_give"}) ==
			  s2sdk::ResultType::Continue,
		  "a chat call does not match the console-only name");
	Check(serverCalls == 0, "a chat call never runs the server-only handler");

	// Names are matched case-insensitively (the engine lowercases some inputs).
	Check(Dispatch(*command, -1, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"PIX_GIVE"}) ==
			  s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "the name matches case-insensitively");
	Check(serverCalls == 1, "the case-insensitive server-console call runs the handler");

	// The chat path itself still works for a normal chat command.
	const FakeCommand* chat = FindRegistered("pix_vip");
	Check(chat != nullptr, "the chat name is registered");
	if (chat != nullptr) {
		Check(Dispatch(*chat, 3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Chat, {"pix_vip"}) == s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
			  "a chat command is dispatched to its handler");
		Check(clientCalls == 1, "the chat handler ran");
	}
}

void TestServerOnlyWinsOverRegCommand() {
	int clientHandlerCalls = 0;
	int serverHandlerCalls = 0;
	// The same console name registered both ways: no matter the order, the server-only
	// registration must win for the console path.
	pisex::RegCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_dual"}, std::vector<std::string>{},
					  [&](int, const char*) { ++clientHandlerCalls; return true; });
	pisex::RegServerCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_dual"}, [&](int, const char*) {
		++serverHandlerCalls;
		return true;
	});
	// And the other order, under a second name.
	pisex::RegServerCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_dual2"}, [&](int, const char*) {
		++serverHandlerCalls;
		return true;
	});
	pisex::RegCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_dual2"}, std::vector<std::string>{},
					  [&](int, const char*) { ++clientHandlerCalls; return true; });

	const FakeCommand* dual = FindRegistered("pix_dual");
	const FakeCommand* dual2 = FindRegistered("pix_dual2");
	Check(dual != nullptr && dual2 != nullptr, "both dual registrations reach s2sdk");
	if (dual == nullptr || dual2 == nullptr) {
		return;
	}

	Check(Dispatch(*dual, 3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_dual"}) == s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "the client call on a dual name is swallowed");
	Check(Dispatch(*dual2, 3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_dual2"}) == s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "the client call is swallowed in either registration order");
	Check(clientHandlerCalls == 0, "no client handler ran for a dual name");
	Check(Dispatch(*dual, -1, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_dual"}) == s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "the server console call on a dual name is handled");
	Check(Dispatch(*dual2, -1, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_dual2"}) == s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "the server console call is handled in either order");
	Check(serverHandlerCalls == 2 && clientHandlerCalls == 0, "the server-only handler won both times");
}

void TestLastRegistrationWins() {
	int firstCalls = 0;
	int secondCalls = 0;
	pisex::RegCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_dup"}, std::vector<std::string>{},
					  [&](int, const char*) { ++firstCalls; return true; });
	pisex::RegCommand(std::vector<std::string>{"pix_dup"}, std::vector<std::string>{},
					  [&](int, const char*) { ++secondCalls; return true; });

	const FakeCommand* command = FindRegistered("pix_dup");
	Check(command != nullptr, "a duplicate name is registered with s2sdk once");
	if (command != nullptr) {
		Dispatch(*command, -1, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Console, {"pix_dup"});
	}
	Check(secondCalls == 1 && firstCalls == 0, "the most recently registered handler wins (Pisex map overwrite)");
}

// A chat pre-listener may unregister everything (a plugin reloading itself calls Shutdown) or add
// further listeners while it runs: the fan-out iterates a snapshot, so the remaining listeners of
// this message still run and nothing reads a cleared/reallocated vector.
void TestChatFanoutSurvivesReentrancy() {
	int firstCalls = 0;
	int secondCalls = 0;
	int thirdCalls = 0;
	pisex::AddChatListenerPre([&](int, const char*, bool) {
		++firstCalls;
		pisex::RemoveAllCommands(); // clears the listener list from inside its own fan-out
		pisex::AddChatListenerPre([&](int, const char*, bool) {
			++thirdCalls;
			return true;
		});
		return true;
	});
	pisex::AddChatListenerPre([&](int, const char*, bool) {
		++secondCalls;
		return true;
	});
	Check(pisex::HasChatListeners(), "chat listeners are registered");

	const s2sdk::ConCommandCallback say = FindListener("say");
	Check(say != nullptr, "the chat trampoline is hooked for say");
	if (say == nullptr) {
		return;
	}
	plg::vector<plg::string> argv;
	argv.push_back(plg::string("say"));
	argv.push_back(plg::string("hello"));
	Check(say(3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Chat, argv) == s2sdk::ResultType::Continue,
		  "both listeners allowed the message");
	Check(firstCalls == 1 && secondCalls == 1, "the listeners that were registered at entry all ran");
	Check(thirdCalls == 0, "a listener added during the fan-out waits for the next message");

	Check(say(3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Chat, argv) == s2sdk::ResultType::Continue,
		  "the next message is allowed again");
	Check(thirdCalls == 1 && firstCalls == 1 && secondCalls == 1,
		  "the next message runs the listeners registered since the reentrant call");

	// A listener that blocks the message: the engine must not broadcast it.
	pisex::RemoveAllCommands();
	pisex::AddChatListenerPre([](int, const char*, bool) { return false; });
	Check(say(3, s2sdk::ConCommandContext::Chat, argv) == s2sdk::ResultType::Handled,
		  "a blocking listener swallows the message");
}

} // namespace

int main() {
	__s2sdk_AddConsoleCommand = &FakeAddConsoleCommand;
	__s2sdk_AddCommandListener = &FakeAddCommandListener;

	TestFlags();
	TestServerOnlyDispatch();
	TestServerOnlyWinsOverRegCommand();
	TestLastRegistrationWins();
	TestChatFanoutSurvivesReentrancy();

	// Leave the process in the state the other objects of a test binary expect (no s2sdk binding),
	// and drop the registrations again.
	__s2sdk_AddConsoleCommand = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_AddCommandListener = nullptr;
	pisex::Shutdown();

	std::printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", g_checks, g_failures);
	return g_failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`libs/pisexcompat/test/menu_engine_test.cpp`:

```cpp
// pisexcompat menu test — drives the real menu layer with a fake s2sdk menu manager.
//
// The rule under test (s2sdk's menus guide: always destroy your menus - call DestroyMenu(id) from
// your handler's End case, otherwise every menu you display leaks for the lifetime of the
// plugin): s2sdk's EndClientMenu() only clears the client state, so a menu whose display ends on
// its own (exit button, timeout, disconnect) has to be destroyed by us — from outside the handler,
// which runs under the menu manager's recursive mutex and would otherwise re-enter the plugin.
//
// The fake mimics s2sdk closely enough to count: CreateMenu/DestroyMenu/AddMenuItem/DisplayMenu/
// GetClientMenu/CancelClientMenu, the handler dispatch order (Cancel then End, End always last)
// and DestroyMenu ending every client session that still shows the menu (counted separately: that
// viewer cancel is what makes DestroyMenu unsafe in the map-change window). Run by ../test.sh.

#include <pisex/compat.hpp> // Poll(): the deferred menu pump
#include <pisex/menu.hpp>

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>

#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <array>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

// A real plugin gets these from PLUGIFY_PLUGIN; the test leaves them null (no plugify module).
namespace plg {
GetBaseDirFn GetBaseDir{nullptr};
GetExtensionsDirFn GetExtensionsDir{nullptr};
GetConfigsDirFn GetConfigsDir{nullptr};
GetDataDirFn GetDataDir{nullptr};
GetLogsDirFn GetLogsDir{nullptr};
GetCacheDirFn GetCacheDir{nullptr};
IsLoadedFn IsLoaded{nullptr};
LogFn Log{nullptr};
BeginZoneFn BeginZone{nullptr};
EndZoneFn EndZone{nullptr};
} // namespace plg

namespace {

int g_checks = 0;
int g_failures = 0;

void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
	++g_checks;
	if (!condition) {
		++g_failures;
		std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
	}
}

// --- the fake s2sdk menu manager ---------------------------------------------------------------

constexpr int kSlots = 64;

struct FakeMenu {
	s2sdk::MenuId id = 0;
	s2sdk::MenuHandlerCallback handler = nullptr;
	std::vector<std::string> items;
};

std::vector<FakeMenu> g_menus;
std::array<s2sdk::MenuId, kSlots> g_displayed{};
s2sdk::MenuId g_nextMenuId = 1;
bool g_displaySucceeds = true;

int g_createCalls = 0;
int g_destroyCalls = 0;
int g_destroysInsideHandler = 0;
// DestroyMenu ending a client that still shows the menu (s2sdk then runs the menu type backend's
// close, which reaches the client/entity layer - forbidden in the map-change window).
int g_destroyViewerCancels = 0;
std::vector<s2sdk::MenuId> g_destroyedIds;
int g_handlerDepth = 0;

const FakeMenu* FindMenu(s2sdk::MenuId id) {
	for (const FakeMenu& menu : g_menus) {
		if (menu.id == id) {
			return &menu;
		}
	}
	return nullptr;
}

void CallHandler(s2sdk::MenuId id, s2sdk::MenuAction action, int32_t slot, int32_t param) {
	const FakeMenu* menu = FindMenu(id);
	if (!menu || !menu->handler) {
		return;
	}
	++g_handlerDepth;
	try {
		menu->handler(id, action, slot, param);
	} catch (...) {
	}
	--g_handlerDepth;
}

s2sdk::MenuId FakeCreateMenu(const plg::string& title, s2sdk::MenuHandlerCallback handler, const plg::string& type) {
	(void)title;
	(void)type;
	++g_createCalls;
	FakeMenu menu;
	menu.id = g_nextMenuId++;
	menu.handler = handler;
	g_menus.push_back(menu);
	return menu.id;
}

// Like s2sdk's DestroyMenu: ends every client session that shows the menu (Cancel + End handler
// calls), then drops the MenuData. Only a plugin ever calls it - nothing in s2sdk does.
bool FakeDestroyMenu(s2sdk::MenuId id) {
	++g_destroyCalls;
	if (g_handlerDepth > 0) {
		++g_destroysInsideHandler;
	}
	for (auto it = g_menus.begin(); it != g_menus.end(); ++it) {
		if (it->id != id) {
			continue;
		}
		for (int slot = 0; slot < kSlots; ++slot) {
			if (g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] == id) {
				++g_destroyViewerCancels;
				g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] = 0;
				CallHandler(id, s2sdk::MenuAction::Cancel, slot, static_cast<int32_t>(s2sdk::MenuCancelReason::Destroyed));
				CallHandler(id, s2sdk::MenuAction::End, slot, 0);
			}
		}
		g_menus.erase(it);
		g_destroyedIds.push_back(id);
		return true;
	}
	return false;
}

int32_t FakeAddMenuItem(s2sdk::MenuId id, const plg::string& info, const plg::string& display, s2sdk::MenuItemStyle style) {
	(void)style;
	for (FakeMenu& menu : g_menus) {
		if (menu.id == id) {
			menu.items.push_back(std::string(display.data(), display.size()));
			(void)info;
			return static_cast<int32_t>(menu.items.size()) - 1;
		}
	}
	return -1;
}

bool FakeDisplayMenu(s2sdk::MenuId id, int32_t slot, int32_t time) {
	(void)time;
	if (!g_displaySucceeds || !FindMenu(id) || slot < 0 || slot >= kSlots) {
		return false;
	}
	g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] = id;
	return true;
}

s2sdk::MenuId FakeGetClientMenu(int32_t slot) {
	return (slot >= 0 && slot < kSlots) ? g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] : 0;
}

// The engine ending a display on its own: timeout, disconnect or the exit button. s2sdk sends
// Cancel first, End last (its EndClientMenu).
bool FakeCancelClientMenu(int32_t slot, s2sdk::MenuCancelReason reason) {
	if (slot < 0 || slot >= kSlots) {
		return false;
	}
	const s2sdk::MenuId id = g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)];
	if (id == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] = 0;
	CallHandler(id, s2sdk::MenuAction::Cancel, slot, static_cast<int32_t>(reason));
	CallHandler(id, s2sdk::MenuAction::End, slot, 0);
	return true;
}

bool FakeSetMenuPagination(s2sdk::MenuId id, int32_t items) {
	(void)id;
	(void)items;
	return true;
}

bool FakeSetMenuBool(s2sdk::MenuId id, bool value) {
	(void)id;
	(void)value;
	return true;
}

bool FakeIsMenuTypeRegistered(const plg::string& name) {
	(void)name;
	return false; // no custom backends: everything maps to the built-in types
}

void InstallFakes() {
	__s2sdk_CreateMenu = &FakeCreateMenu;
	__s2sdk_DestroyMenu = &FakeDestroyMenu;
	__s2sdk_AddMenuItem = &FakeAddMenuItem;
	__s2sdk_DisplayMenu = &FakeDisplayMenu;
	__s2sdk_GetClientMenu = &FakeGetClientMenu;
	__s2sdk_CancelClientMenu = &FakeCancelClientMenu;
	__s2sdk_SetMenuPagination = &FakeSetMenuPagination;
	__s2sdk_SetMenuExitButton = &FakeSetMenuBool;
	__s2sdk_SetMenuExitBackButton = &FakeSetMenuBool;
	__s2sdk_SetMenuCloseOnSelect = &FakeSetMenuBool;
	__s2sdk_IsMenuTypeRegistered = &FakeIsMenuTypeRegistered;
}

void MakeReady() {
	pisex::OnMapEndNotify(); // normalise the map lifecycle state
	pisex::Poll();
	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
}

// Drives one display of a fresh menu and returns the fake's menu id.
s2sdk::MenuId DisplayMenu(int slot, const pisex::MenuCallbackFunc& callback = nullptr) {
	pisex::Menu menu;
	pisex::SetTitleMenu(menu, "Test menu");
	pisex::SetExitMenu(menu, true);
	pisex::AddItemMenu(menu, "one", "One", pisex::ITEM_DEFAULT);
	pisex::AddItemMenu(menu, "two", "Two", pisex::ITEM_DEFAULT);
	if (callback) {
		pisex::SetCallback(menu, callback);
	}
	pisex::DisplayPlayerMenu(menu, slot, true, true);
	return g_displayed[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)];
}

// --- tests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The audit item: a display that ends on its own (timeout / disconnect) must destroy the menu -
// deferred out of the handler, exactly once.
void TestEndedDisplayIsDestroyed() {
	g_menus.clear();
	g_displayed.fill(0);
	g_nextMenuId = 1;
	g_createCalls = g_destroyCalls = g_destroysInsideHandler = 0;
	g_destroyedIds.clear();

	const s2sdk::MenuId id = DisplayMenu(3);
	Check(id != 0, "the menu was created and displayed");
	Check(g_menus.size() == 1, "the fake holds the menu");
	Check(pisex::IsMenuOpen(3), "the library reports the menu as open");
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 0, "no destroy happened while displaying");

	// The display times out: s2sdk calls the handler (Cancel then End) and clears its client
	// state. Nothing may be destroyed from inside the handler.
	FakeCancelClientMenu(3, s2sdk::MenuCancelReason::Timeout);
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 0, "the menu is not destroyed inside the handler (deferred)");
	Check(g_destroysInsideHandler == 0, "no DestroyMenu call happens under the menu manager's lock");
	Check(!pisex::IsMenuOpen(3), "the ended display is no longer open");

	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "Poll() destroys the menu whose display ended");
	Check(g_destroyedIds.size() == 1 && g_destroyedIds.front() == id, "the destroyed id is the menu's");
	Check(g_menus.empty(), "no MenuData left in the fake manager");

	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "a second Poll must not destroy it again");
}

// The exit button: the plugin callback still gets Pisex's exit values, and the menu is freed once.
void TestExitDestroysOnceAndKeepsCallback() {
	g_createCalls = g_destroyCalls = g_destroysInsideHandler = 0;
	g_destroyedIds.clear();

	std::string back;
	std::string front;
	int item = -1;
	const s2sdk::MenuId id = DisplayMenu(4, [&](const char* szBack, const char* szFront, int iItem, int iSlot) {
		back = szBack ? szBack : "";
		front = szFront ? szFront : "";
		item = iItem;
		(void)iSlot;
	});
	Check(id != 0, "menu displayed for the exit test");

	FakeCancelClientMenu(4, s2sdk::MenuCancelReason::Exit);
	Check(back == "exit" && front == "exit" && item == 9, "the Pisex exit callback values");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "the exited menu is destroyed exactly once");
}

// An explicit close destroys immediately; the engine's later End must not destroy it a second time.
void TestExplicitCloseIsSingle() {
	g_createCalls = g_destroyCalls = g_destroysInsideHandler = 0;
	g_destroyedIds.clear();

	const s2sdk::MenuId id = DisplayMenu(5);
	Check(id != 0, "menu displayed for the close test");
	pisex::ClosePlayerMenu(5);
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "ClosePlayerMenu destroys the menu right away");
	Check(g_menus.empty(), "the menu is gone after the explicit close");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "the deferred End of that session does not destroy it again");
}

// A display that the backend refuses (no client, wrong state): the created menu must not leak.
void TestFailedDisplayIsDestroyed() {
	g_createCalls = g_destroyCalls = g_destroysInsideHandler = 0;
	g_destroyedIds.clear();
	g_displaySucceeds = false;

	DisplayMenu(6);
	Check(g_createCalls == 1, "the menu was created");
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "a menu that could not be displayed is destroyed immediately");
	Check(g_menus.empty(), "nothing is left in the fake manager");
	Check(!pisex::IsMenuOpen(6), "no menu is registered for the slot");
	g_displaySucceeds = true;
}

// pisexcompat creates one menu per display, but s2sdk menus are shared objects: if the same id is
// still displayed to another client, the destroy must wait for that session to end.
void TestMultiRecipientSafety() {
	g_createCalls = g_destroyCalls = g_destroysInsideHandler = 0;
	g_destroyedIds.clear();

	const s2sdk::MenuId id = DisplayMenu(7);
	Check(id != 0, "menu displayed for the multi-recipient test");
	g_displayed[8] = id; // as if the same menu had been shown to a second client

	FakeCancelClientMenu(7, s2sdk::MenuCancelReason::Timeout);
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 0, "a menu still displayed to another client is not destroyed");
	Check(FindMenu(id) != nullptr, "the menu still exists");
	Check(g_displayed[8] == id, "the other client still shows it");

	FakeCancelClientMenu(8, s2sdk::MenuCancelReason::Timeout);
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 1, "the last session's end destroys it exactly once");
	Check(g_menus.empty(), "nothing is left after the last session");
}

// Map end / plugin shutdown: everything open or queued is destroyed, so `plg reload` does not
// leave MenuData (and handlers into unloaded code) behind - and the map end never hands a
// still-displayed menu to DestroyMenu, whose viewer cancel is a client call.
void TestMapEndAndShutdownDestroyEverything() {
	g_createCalls = g_destroyCalls = g_destroysInsideHandler = g_destroyViewerCancels = 0;
	g_destroyedIds.clear();

	int pisexCallbacks = 0;
	const s2sdk::MenuId open = DisplayMenu(9, [&](const char*, const char*, int, int) { ++pisexCallbacks; });
	const s2sdk::MenuId ended = DisplayMenu(10);
	Check(open != 0 && ended != 0, "two menus displayed");
	Check(g_displayed[9] == open, "the fake still shows the open menu to its client");
	FakeCancelClientMenu(10, s2sdk::MenuCancelReason::Disconnect); // queued for destroy

	pisex::OnMapEndNotify(); // map end runs CloseAllMenus
	Check(g_destroyCalls == 2, "map end destroys the open and the queued menu");
	Check(g_menus.empty(), "no MenuData survives the map end");
	Check(g_destroysInsideHandler == 0, "no destroy ran inside a handler");
	Check(g_destroyViewerCancels == 0, "map end never lets DestroyMenu cancel a viewer");
	Check(g_displayed[9] == 0, "the open session is gone from the fake manager");
	Check(pisexCallbacks == 0, "map end fires no Pisex exit/back callback");

	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(DisplayMenu(11) != 0, "a menu works again on the new map");
	pisex::Shutdown();
	Check(g_menus.empty(), "Shutdown destroys everything too");
}

} // namespace

int main() {
	std::printf("pisexcompat menu engine tests (fake s2sdk menu manager)\n");

	InstallFakes();
	MakeReady();

	TestEndedDisplayIsDestroyed();
	TestExitDestroysOnceAndKeepsCallback();
	TestExplicitCloseIsSingle();
	TestFailedDisplayIsDestroyed();
	TestMultiRecipientSafety();
	TestMapEndAndShutdownDestroyEverything();

	std::printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", g_checks, g_failures);
	return g_failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

```cpp
// pisexcompat player-wrapper test — drives the real wrappers with fake s2sdk client bindings.
//
// Background (the crash cases this guards against):
//   * pisex::SetPlayerName -> SetClientName -> Player::SetName dereferences a *null client* (and a
//     null controller) -> SIGSEGV at address 0x48 right after a map start, while the bots were
//     being created.
//   * any client query during the map shutdown (MapEnd dispatch) -> utils::GetClientBySlot reads
//     the half-destroyed server's client list -> SIGSEGV at address 0.
//   * s2sdk's Player::GetIpAddress dereferences the net channel, which is null for bots.
// Nothing in this file touches the engine: the __s2sdk_* globals are plain variables, so the test
// installs fakes and counts every call the library makes. Run by ../test.sh.

#include <pisex/compat.hpp> // Poll()/OnMapEndNotify()/OnMapStartNotify(): the map lifecycle gate
#include <pisex/players.hpp>
#include <pisex/schema.hpp> // GetPlayerPawn()

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>

void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
	++g_checks;
	if (!condition) {
		++g_failures;
		std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
	}

// --- the fake client layer ---------------------------------------------------------------------

struct FakeClient {
	bool connected = false;
	bool fake = false;
	bool controller = false; // PlayerSlotToEntPointer() answers a non-null entity
	bool pawn = true;		 // with a controller: GetClientPawn() answers a non-null pawn
	std::string name;
	uint64_t steamid64 = 0;
	int health = 100;
};

std::vector<FakeClient> g_clients(64);
int g_clientCalls = 0; // every fake below counts into this
int g_setNameCalls = 0;
int g_getNameCalls = 0;
int g_getIpCalls = 0;
int g_getSteamIdCalls = 0;
int g_getHealthCalls = 0;

bool ValidSlot(int32_t slot) {
	return slot >= 0 && slot < static_cast<int32_t>(g_clients.size());
}

const FakeClient& Slot(int32_t slot) {
	static const FakeClient empty;
	return ValidSlot(slot) ? g_clients[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)] : empty;
}

void ResetClients() {
	g_clients.assign(64, FakeClient{});
	g_clientCalls = g_setNameCalls = g_getNameCalls = g_getIpCalls = g_getSteamIdCalls = g_getHealthCalls = 0;
}

bool FakeIsClientConnected(int32_t slot) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	return Slot(slot).connected;
}

bool FakeIsClientInGame(int32_t slot) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	return Slot(slot).connected;
}

bool FakeIsFakeClient(int32_t slot) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	return Slot(slot).fake;
}

plg::string FakeGetClientName(int32_t slot) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	++g_getNameCalls;
	// s2sdk answers "<unknown>" when it cannot resolve the client (Player::GetName).
	return plg::string(Slot(slot).name.empty() ? "<unknown>" : Slot(slot).name);
}

void FakeSetClientName(int32_t slot, const plg::string& name) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	++g_setNameCalls;
	if (ValidSlot(slot)) {
		g_clients[static_cast<std::size_t>(slot)].name = std::string(name.data(), name.size());
	}
}

	(void)slot;
	++g_clientCalls;
	++g_getIpCalls;
	return plg::string("1.2.3.4");
}

	++g_getSteamIdCalls;
	return Slot(slot).steamid64;

	++g_clientCalls;
	++g_getHealthCalls;
	return Slot(slot).health;
}

void* FakePlayerSlotToEntPointer(int32_t slot) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	// The controller entity index is slot + 1 (like the engine's).
	return Slot(slot).controller ? reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(0x1000 + slot + 1)) : nullptr;
}

void* FakeGetClientPawn(int32_t slot) {
	++g_clientCalls;
	const FakeClient& client = Slot(slot);
	return client.controller && client.pawn ? reinterpret_cast<void*>(static_cast<uintptr_t>(0x2000 + slot + 1)) : nullptr;
}

	++g_clientCalls;
	return pointer ? static_cast<int32_t>(reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(pointer) - 0x1000) : 0;
```
