```cpp
// --- tests -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The map lifecycle gate: from a map end until the *next* map start (not just the next update)
// no client query may reach s2sdk - its client list is torn down in that window.
void TestMapLifecycleGate() {
	pisex::OnMapEndNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "a map end disables the library until a new map start");
	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "the map start alone is not enough (the host pumps the updates)");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(pisex::IsGameReady(), "the first update after a map start is ready");

	// A map with players, then the map ends.
	ResetClients();
	g_clients[3] = FakeClient{.connected = true, .controller = true, .name = "Alice", .steamid64 = 76561198000000001ULL};
	const int before = g_clientCalls;

	pisex::OnMapEndNotify();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "the map end disables the library");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "a Poll during the map change does not re-enable it");

	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(3)).empty(), "GetPlayerName is empty while no map is up");
	Check(pisex::GetSteamID64(3) == 0, "GetSteamID64 is 0 while no map is up");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetIpAddress(3)).empty(), "GetIpAddress is empty while no map is up");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetClientLanguage(3)).empty(), "GetClientLanguage is empty while no map is up");
	Check(!pisex::IsConnected(3), "IsConnected is false while no map is up");
	Check(!pisex::IsInGame(3), "IsInGame is false while no map is up");
	Check(!pisex::IsAuthenticated(3), "IsAuthenticated is false while no map is up");
	Check(!pisex::IsAlive(3), "IsAlive is false while no map is up");
	Check(!pisex::IsFakeClient(3), "IsFakeClient is false while no map is up");
	Check(!pisex::IsClientReady(3), "IsClientReady is false while no map is up");
	Check(pisex::GetPlayerHealth(3) == 0, "health is 0 while no map is up");
	Check(pisex::GetPlayerPawn(3) == 0, "the pawn is 0 while no map is up");
	Check(pisex::GetPawnEntity(3) == 0, "the pawn entity is 0 while no map is up");
	Check(pisex::FindPlayer(76561198000000001ULL) == -1, "FindPlayer finds nobody while no map is up");
	pisex::SetPlayerName(3, "Bob");
	pisex::ChangeTeam(3, 2);
	pisex::Respawn(3);
	Check(g_clientCalls == before, "not one s2sdk client call is made while no map is up");

	// The new map is up: the same calls work again.
	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(pisex::IsGameReady(), "ready again after the new map start");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(3)) == "Alice", "the client is reachable again");
}

// A slot without a client (or without a controller yet) must never reach SetClientName (the
// crash above), and the read-only wrappers must answer their defaults silently.
void TestClientlessSlotGuards() {
	ResetClients();

	// No client at all.
	pisex::SetPlayerName(5, "x");
	Check(g_setNameCalls == 0, "SetClientName is not called for a slot without a client");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(5)).empty(), "a slot without a client has an empty name");
	Check(g_getNameCalls == 0, "GetClientName is not called without a client");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetIpAddress(5)).empty(), "a slot without a client has no IP");
	Check(g_getIpCalls == 0, "GetClientIp is not called without a client");
	Check(pisex::GetPlayerHealth(5) == 0, "health is 0 for a slot without a client");
	Check(g_getHealthCalls == 0, "GetClientHealth is not called without a client");

	// Connected, but the controller entity does not exist yet (a client that is still connecting -
	// exactly the state right after a map start, while the bots are being created).
	g_clients[5].connected = true;
	Check(!pisex::IsClientReady(5), "a connecting client is not client-ready");
	pisex::SetPlayerName(5, "x");
	Check(g_setNameCalls == 0, "SetClientName is not called while the controller does not exist yet");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(5)).empty(), "a connecting client has an empty name");

	// Fully in place: the writes and reads go through.
	g_clients[5].controller = true;
	Check(pisex::IsClientReady(5), "a connected client with a controller is client-ready");
	pisex::SetPlayerName(5, "Charlie");
	Check(g_setNameCalls == 1, "SetClientName is called once the client and controller exist");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(5)) == "Charlie", "the name round-trips");
	Check(pisex::GetSteamID64(5) == 0, "a slot without a steam id answers 0");

	// s2sdk's "<unknown>" placeholder becomes an empty name (the Pisex API never returned it).
	g_clients[5].name.clear();
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(5)).empty(), "s2sdk's \"<unknown>\" becomes an empty name");
	Check(g_getNameCalls == 2, "GetClientName was called (and its placeholder normalised)");

	// Bots: GetIpAddress would dereference a null net channel - never call it for a fake client.
	g_clients[5].name = "Bot";
	g_clients[5].fake = true;
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetIpAddress(5)).empty(), "a bot has no IP");
	Check(g_getIpCalls == 0, "GetClientIp is not called for a fake client");
	g_clients[5].fake = false;
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetIpAddress(5)) == "1.2.3.4", "a human's IP is returned");
	Check(g_getIpCalls == 1, "GetClientIp is called for a connected human");

	// Steam ids must not go stale: the s2sdk implementation keeps the previous occupant's
	// unauthenticated id, so a disconnected slot has to answer 0 (Pisex semantics).
	g_clients[5].steamid64 = 76561198000000009ULL;
	Check(pisex::GetSteamID64(5) == 76561198000000009ULL, "a connected client's steam id is returned");
	g_clients[5].connected = false;
	Check(pisex::GetSteamID64(5) == 0, "a disconnected slot answers 0, not the previous occupant's id");

	// Out-of-range slots.
	Check(!pisex::IsClientReady(-1) && !pisex::IsClientReady(64), "out-of-range slots are not client-ready");
	pisex::SetPlayerName(64, "x");
	Check(g_setNameCalls == 1, "an out-of-range slot never reaches SetClientName");
}

// The heap of guards must not break the happy path: a fully connected human and a bot both work.
void TestHappyPath() {
	ResetClients();
	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(pisex::IsGameReady(), "the test map is up");

	g_clients[2] = FakeClient{.connected = true, .controller = true, .name = "Dana", .steamid64 = 76561198000000002ULL,
							  .health = 77};
	g_clients[4] = FakeClient{.connected = true, .fake = true, .controller = true, .name = "BOT Rick"};

	Check(pisex::IsConnected(2) && pisex::IsClientReady(2), "a connected human is ready");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(2)) == "Dana", "the human's name");
	Check(pisex::GetSteamID64(2) == 76561198000000002ULL, "the human's steam id");
	Check(pisex::GetPlayerHealth(2) == 77, "the human's health");
	// A controller without a pawn (connecting, spectator before the first spawn): s2sdk's
	// GetClientHealth would print "invalid player pawn" - the wrapper answers 0 without calling it.
	g_clients[2].pawn = false;
	const int healthCallsBefore = g_getHealthCalls;
	Check(pisex::GetPlayerHealth(2) == 0 && g_getHealthCalls == healthCallsBefore,
		  "no pawn: health is 0 and GetClientHealth is not called");
	g_clients[2].pawn = true;
	Check(pisex::IsFakeClient(4) && pisex::IsClientReady(4), "a bot is a ready client");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(4)) == "BOT Rick", "the bot's name");
	Check(pisex::FindPlayer(76561198000000002ULL) == 2, "FindPlayer finds the human");
	Check(pisex::FindPlayer("dana") == 2, "FindPlayer by name is case-insensitive");
	Check(pisex::FindPlayer("rick") == -1, "FindPlayer skips bots");
	pisex::SetPlayerName(4, "BOT Morty");
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(4)) == "BOT Morty", "a bot's name can be set");
}

// The fake bindings are restored to the no-s2sdk state (the other checks rely on it).
void TestWithoutBindings() {
	ResetClients();
	__s2sdk_IsClientConnected = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_IsClientInGame = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_IsFakeClient = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_GetClientName = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_SetClientName = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_GetClientIp = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_GetClientSteamID64 = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_GetClientHealth = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_PlayerSlotToEntPointer = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_EntPointerToEntIndex = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_GetClientPawn = nullptr;

	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(std::string(pisex::GetPlayerName(0)).empty(), "no bindings: an empty name");
	Check(pisex::GetSteamID64(0) == 0, "no bindings: steam id 0");
	Check(!pisex::IsClientReady(0), "no bindings: nothing is client-ready");
	pisex::SetPlayerName(0, "x");
	Check(true, "no bindings: the wrappers stay no-ops");
}

// Handles are index | serial << 15: past serial 65535 a valid handle is a negative int (a real
// pawn handle was -921534371 = index 93, serial 102949). Only -1 is invalid; 0 means "none".
int g_lastIndexQuery = 0;
int32_t FakeEntHandleToEntIndex(int32_t handle) {
	g_lastIndexQuery = handle;
	return static_cast<int32_t>(static_cast<uint32_t>(handle) & 0x7FFFu);
}

void TestNegativeHandles() {
	__s2sdk_EntHandleToEntIndex = &FakeEntHandleToEntIndex;
	Check(pisex::EntHandleToEntIndex(-921534371) == 93, "a negative (high-serial) handle resolves to its index");
	Check(g_lastIndexQuery == -921534371, "the negative handle reaches s2sdk unchanged");
	g_lastIndexQuery = 12345;
	Check(pisex::EntHandleToEntIndex(-1) == 0, "INVALID_EHANDLE_INDEX (-1) is none");
	Check(pisex::EntHandleToEntIndex(0) == 0, "0 is none");
	Check(g_lastIndexQuery == 12345, "-1 and 0 never reach s2sdk");
	__s2sdk_EntHandleToEntIndex = nullptr;
}

} // namespace

int main() {
	std::printf("pisexcompat player-wrapper engine tests (fake s2sdk client bindings)\n");

	InstallFakes();
	pisex::Poll(); // first update: a plugin loaded into a running map becomes ready
	Check(pisex::IsGameReady(), "the first update with no map end seen is ready (mid-map load)");

	TestMapLifecycleGate();
	TestClientlessSlotGuards();
	TestHappyPath();
	TestWithoutBindings();
	TestNegativeHandles();

	std::printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", g_checks, g_failures);
	return g_failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`libs/pisexcompat/test/smoke_plugin.cpp`:

```cpp
// pisexcompat smoke plugin — a minimal Plugify plugin that uses pisexcompat the way a ported
// Pisex plugin does, built as a real shared object by ./build.sh so that the integration points
// are checked by the normal build gates:
//   * the static library links into a plugin (.so) and pulls in the s2sdk binding globals,
//   * PLUGIFY_PLUGIN (the plugin's own plg::* globals) and the library's references to them agree,
//   * the ABI report for a plugin that uses pisexcompat stays inside GLIBC 2.31 with no
//     libstdc++/libmariadb NEEDED entries.
//
// It is part of the build on purpose and is not meant to be installed (see
// libs/pisexcompat/CMakeLists.txt). The handler bodies are the porting template: Init in
// OnPluginStart, Poll in OnPluginUpdate, Shutdown in OnPluginEnd.

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>
#include <plg/string.hpp>
#include <plugin_export.h>

#include <pisex/pisex.hpp>

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>

namespace {

class SmokePlugin final : public plg::Plugin {
public:
	plg::PluginResult OnPluginStart() override {
		// Never returns Failed: that stops every plugify plugin on the server.
		pisex::Init("pisexcompat_smoke");
		pisex::g_pUtils->StartupServer([] { pisex::g_pUtils->PrintToConsole(-1, "startup"); });
		pisex::g_pUtils->RegCommand({"pix_smoke"}, {"!smoke"}, [](int iSlot, const char* content) {
			pisex::CommandArgs args;
			args.Tokenize(content);
			pisex::g_pUtils->PrintToChat(iSlot, "%s from %s", args.Arg(0) ? args.Arg(0) : "", "smoke");
			return true;
		});
		pisex::g_pUtils->HookEvent("player_death", [](const char* name, pisex::IGameEvent* event, bool broadcast) {
			(void)name;
			(void)broadcast;
			pisex::g_pUtils->PrintToConsole(event->GetPlayerSlot("userid"), "died");
		});
		pisex::g_pUtils->CreateTimer(5.0f, [] {
			return -1.0f; // stop after the first run
		});
		return plg::PluginResult{};
	}

	plg::PluginResult OnPluginUpdate(std::chrono::milliseconds) override {
		pisex::Poll();
		return plg::PluginResult{};
	}

	plg::PluginResult OnPluginEnd() override {
		pisex::Shutdown();
		return plg::PluginResult{};
	}
};

SmokePlugin g_smokePlugin;

} // namespace

PLUGIFY_PLUGIN(PLUGIN_API, &g_smokePlugin)
```

`libs/pisexcompat/test/timers_engine_test.cpp`:

```cpp
// pisexcompat timer-registry test — drives the *real* Create/Remove/Process/OnFire code with fake
// s2sdk timer bindings. This is the part of the library that crashed the server: a repeating
// s2sdk timer with a stored delay of 0 makes TimerSystem::RunFrame() re-run the callback forever
// inside one frame ("Server took too long to process" FATAL), and the registry's remove/kill
// bookkeeping had a use-after-free and leaked engine timers for every one-shot timer.
//
// The engine is simulated: the fake CreateTimer records the callback the library registered, and
// the test invokes it exactly like the engine's RunFrame() would (twice per "frame" where the
// engine would repeat a still-scheduled timer). Everything runs in-process and single threaded,
// like the game thread. Run by ../test.sh.

#include <pisex/compat.hpp> // Poll()/Shutdown(): the timer pump the plugin host calls
#include <pisex/timers.hpp>

#include <plg/plugin.hpp>

#include <s2sdk/s2sdk.hpp>

#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

// A real plugin gets these from PLUGIFY_PLUGIN; the test leaves them null (no plugify module),
// which is also the state the library has to survive.
namespace plg {
GetBaseDirFn GetBaseDir{nullptr};
GetExtensionsDirFn GetExtensionsDir{nullptr};
GetConfigsDirFn GetConfigsDir{nullptr};
GetDataDirFn GetDataDir{nullptr};
GetLogsDirFn GetLogsDir{nullptr};
GetCacheDirFn GetCacheDir{nullptr};
IsLoadedFn IsLoaded{nullptr};
LogFn Log{nullptr};
BeginZoneFn BeginZone{nullptr};
EndZoneFn EndZone{nullptr};
} // namespace plg

namespace {

int g_checks = 0;
int g_failures = 0;

void Check(bool condition, const std::string& what) {
	++g_checks;
	if (!condition) {
		++g_failures;
		std::printf("FAIL: %s\n", what.c_str());
	}
}

// --- the fake engine ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

struct EngineTimer {
	uint32_t id = 0;
	double delay = 0.0;
	s2sdk::TimerCallback callback = nullptr;
	bool repeat = false;
};

std::vector<EngineTimer> g_engineTimers;
std::vector<uint32_t> g_killed;
std::vector<std::pair<uint32_t, double>> g_rescheduled;
uint32_t g_nextId = 0;

const EngineTimer* FindEngineTimer(uint32_t id) {
	for (const EngineTimer& timer : g_engineTimers) {
		if (timer.id == id) {
			return &timer;
		}
	}
	return nullptr;
}

// Forgets every recorded engine state (so the next timer gets id 0 again) but keeps the fake
// bindings installed.
void ClearRecording() {
	g_engineTimers.clear();
	g_killed.clear();
	g_rescheduled.clear();
	g_nextId = 0;
}

// Removes the fake bindings again: the "no s2sdk plugin" state.
void ResetEngine() {
	ClearRecording();
	__s2sdk_CreateTimer = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_KillsTimer = nullptr;
	__s2sdk_RescheduleTimer = nullptr;
}

// Ids start at 0, like s2sdk's TimerSystem::m_nextId{} - the first timer of the process really has
// id 0, and the library must treat that as a valid id.
s2sdk::TimerId FakeCreateTimer(double delay, s2sdk::TimerCallback callback, s2sdk::TimerFlag flags,
							   const plg::vector<plg::any>& userData) {
	(void)userData;
	EngineTimer timer;
	timer.id = g_nextId++;
	timer.delay = delay;
	timer.callback = callback;
	timer.repeat = (static_cast<int32_t>(flags) & static_cast<int32_t>(s2sdk::TimerFlag::Repeat)) != 0;
	g_engineTimers.push_back(timer);
	return timer.id;
}

void FakeKillsTimer(s2sdk::TimerId id) {
	g_killed.push_back(id);
	for (auto it = g_engineTimers.begin(); it != g_engineTimers.end(); ++it) {
		if (it->id == id) {
			g_engineTimers.erase(it);
			return;
		}
	}
}

void FakeRescheduleTimer(s2sdk::TimerId id, double delay) {
	g_rescheduled.emplace_back(id, delay);
	if (const EngineTimer* timer = FindEngineTimer(id)) {
		const_cast<EngineTimer*>(timer)->delay = delay;
	}
}

void InstallEngine() {
	ResetEngine();
	__s2sdk_CreateTimer = &FakeCreateTimer;
	__s2sdk_KillsTimer = &FakeKillsTimer;
	__s2sdk_RescheduleTimer = &FakeRescheduleTimer;
}

// What TimerSystem::RunFrame() does to a timer that is still scheduled: call it. A Repeat timer is
// re-inserted and fires again on every RunFrame() pass, which is exactly what the test simulates by
// firing twice before the next Poll().
void FireEngineTimer(uint32_t id) {
	const EngineTimer* timer = FindEngineTimer(id);
	Check(timer != nullptr, "the engine still knows timer " + std::to_string(id));
	if (timer && timer->callback) {
		timer->callback(id, plg::vector<plg::any>{});
	}
}

int KillCount(uint32_t id) {
	int count = 0;
	for (const uint32_t killed : g_killed) {
		count += killed == id ? 1 : 0;
	}
	return count;
}

bool RescheduledWith(uint32_t id, double delay) {
	for (const auto& [rescheduledId, value] : g_rescheduled) {
		if (rescheduledId == id && value == delay) {
			return true;
		}
	}
	return false;
}

// --- the tests ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// The delay handed to s2sdk (both at creation and on reschedule) must never be below one tick.
void TestCreateAndRescheduleClamp() {
	InstallEngine();

	struct Case {
		float interval;
		double expectedDelay;
	};
	// 0 (and negative) is Pisex's "run again next frame" - the only safe encoding is one tick.
	const Case cases[] = {
		{0.0f, pisex::kMinTimerDelay},	 { -2.0f, pisex::kMinTimerDelay }, {0.001f, pisex::kMinTimerDelay},
		{0.0156249f, pisex::kMinTimerDelay}, {1.0f, 1.0},				{60.0f, 60.0},
	};

	for (const Case& testCase : cases) {
		ClearRecording(); // keep the bindings, restart the id counter
		pisex::CTimer* timer = pisex::CreateTimer(testCase.interval, [] { return -1.0f; });
		Check(timer != nullptr, "CreateTimer(" + std::to_string(testCase.interval) + ") works");
		const EngineTimer* created = g_engineTimers.empty() ? nullptr : &g_engineTimers.front();
		Check(created != nullptr && created->delay == testCase.expectedDelay,
			  "CreateTimer(" + std::to_string(testCase.interval) + ") hands s2sdk the clamped delay");
		Check(created != nullptr && created->repeat, "the s2sdk timer is a Repeat timer");
		pisex::RemoveTimer(timer);
	}

	// TimerSystem ids start at 0: the first timer of a process must not be rejected as "failure",
	// and it must be killable (the old code skipped KillsTimer for id 0 - the engine timer then
	// fired forever with its CTimer already freed).
	ClearRecording();
	pisex::CTimer* first = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [] { return -1.0f; });
	Check(first != nullptr, "a timer with s2sdk id 0 is accepted");
	Check(first != nullptr && first->Handle() == 0, "the id really is 0");
	pisex::RemoveTimer(first);
	Check(KillCount(0) == 1, "RemoveTimer kills the engine timer with id 0");
	pisex::RemoveTimer(first); // dead handle: must stay a no-op (this is Pisex cleanup code)
	Check(KillCount(0) == 1, "RemoveTimer on a dead handle does not kill twice");

	// The value the callback returned goes through RescheduleTimer - clamped as well (Pisex's
	// "return 0" is the common repeat-next-frame idiom that crashed the server).
	ClearRecording();
	pisex::CTimer* repeat = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [] { return 0.0f; });
	Check(repeat != nullptr, "a next-frame repeating timer is created");
	const uint32_t repeatId = repeat != nullptr ? repeat->Handle() : 0;
	const std::size_t killCountBefore = g_killed.size();
	FireEngineTimer(repeatId);
	Check(g_rescheduled.empty(), "firing a timer makes no s2sdk call from inside the callback");
	Check(g_killed.size() == killCountBefore, "firing a timer kills nothing from inside the callback");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(RescheduledWith(repeatId, pisex::kMinTimerDelay), "a returned 0 is clamped to one tick at reschedule");
	// The engine re-fires the same timer before the next Poll (it is still scheduled with the old
	// delay): the callback must not run twice per frame.
	FireEngineTimer(repeatId);
	FireEngineTimer(repeatId);
	Check(g_rescheduled.size() == 1, "a timer that is waiting for its reschedule ignores further fires");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(g_rescheduled.size() == 2, "after the reschedule the timer can fire again");
	pisex::RemoveTimer(repeat);

	ResetEngine();
}

// A callback that returns a negative value stops the timer: the engine timer must be killed (the
// old reap path skipped already-marked timers, so every one-shot leaked its CTimer and left a
// repeating s2sdk timer firing forever).
void TestOneShotIsKilled() {
	InstallEngine();

	pisex::CTimer* oneShot = pisex::CreateTimer(0.5f, [] { return -1.0f; });
	Check(oneShot != nullptr, "one-shot timer created");
	const uint32_t id = oneShot != nullptr ? oneShot->Handle() : 0;
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	Check(oneShot != nullptr && !oneShot->IsAlive(), "the handle reports the timer as stopped");
	Check(g_killed.empty(), "the kill happens in Poll(), not inside the callback");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(KillCount(id) == 1, "Process() kills the engine timer of a stopped one-shot");
	pisex::RemoveTimer(oneShot); // the handle is dead but must stay safe
	Check(KillCount(id) == 1, "the dead one-shot handle stays a no-op");

	ResetEngine();
}

// A callback removing its *own* timer is legal Pisex usage - the old code freed the CTimer while
// OnFire() was still using it (use-after-free, and a double free at Shutdown()).
void TestRemoveFromInsideCallback() {
	InstallEngine();

	pisex::CTimer* self = nullptr;
	int runs = 0;
	self = pisex::CreateTimer(0.5f, [&self, &runs] {
		++runs;
		self->RemoveTimer();
		return -1.0f;
	});
	Check(self != nullptr, "self-removing timer created");
	const uint32_t id = self != nullptr ? self->Handle() : 0;
	FireEngineTimer(id); // the callback runs RemoveTimer() on its own handle
	Check(runs == 1, "the self-removing callback ran exactly once");
	Check(KillCount(id) == 1, "self-removal killed the engine timer");
	pisex::RemoveTimer(self); // dangling-looking handle: must still be a safe no-op
	Check(KillCount(id) == 1, "the handle of a self-removed timer stays a no-op");
	pisex::Poll(); // frees the object; must not touch it again
	Check(true, "Poll() after a self-removal does not crash");

	// A callback may also remove a *different* timer (the admin core's cleanup does).
	InstallEngine();
	pisex::CTimer* other = pisex::CreateTimer(5.0f, [] { return -1.0f; });
	pisex::CTimer* remover = nullptr;
	remover = pisex::CreateTimer(0.5f, [&other] {
		pisex::RemoveTimer(other);
		other = nullptr;
		return -1.0f;
	});
	const uint32_t otherId = other != nullptr ? other->Handle() : 0;
	Check(other != nullptr && remover != nullptr, "two timers created");
	FireEngineTimer(remover->Handle());
	Check(KillCount(otherId) == 1, "removing another timer from inside a callback kills it");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(true, "Poll() after a cross-timer removal does not crash");

	ResetEngine();
}

// Shutdown() from inside a timer callback (a plugin unloading itself): Clear() must not free or
// clear the fn_ of the timer whose callback is on the stack.
void TestShutdownFromInsideCallback() {
	InstallEngine();

	pisex::CTimer* timer = nullptr;
	int runs = 0;
	timer = pisex::CreateTimer(0.5f, [&timer, &runs] {
		++runs;
		pisex::Shutdown();
		return -1.0f;
	});
	pisex::CTimer* other = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [] { return -1.0f; });
	Check(timer != nullptr && other != nullptr, "timers created before the in-callback Shutdown");
	const uint32_t id = timer->Handle();
	const uint32_t otherId = other->Handle();
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	Check(runs == 1, "the callback ran");
	Check(KillCount(id) == 1 && KillCount(otherId) == 1, "Shutdown() killed both engine timers");
	pisex::RemoveTimer(timer); // safe no-op on a dead handle
	pisex::RemoveTimer(other);
	Check(true, "handles stay safe after an in-callback Shutdown");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(true, "Poll() after an in-callback Shutdown does not crash");

	// The registry is usable again after Shutdown (a plugin may call Init/Poll once more).
	InstallEngine();
	pisex::CTimer* again = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [] { return 1.0f; });
	Check(again != nullptr, "timers can be created again after Shutdown");
	if (again) {
		pisex::RemoveTimer(again);
	}
	pisex::Shutdown();

	// Leave the process in the "no s2sdk plugin" state the other checks rely on.
	ResetEngine();
}

// The dead-handle bookkeeping remembers freed *addresses*, and the allocator hands a freed
// CTimer's memory straight to the next one: a fresh timer must never be mistaken for a dead
// handle. (With the bug this test caught, the second cycle's RemoveTimer() silently did nothing -
// engine timer left running - and OnFire() freed the live object after its first callback, which
// is a use-after-free.)
void TestRecycledAddresses() {
	InstallEngine();

	// RemoveTimer() path - each cycle's allocation reuses the previous cycle's freed address.
	for (int i = 0; i < 64; ++i) {
		pisex::CTimer* timer = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [] { return -1.0f; });
		Check(timer != nullptr, "cycle timer created");
		const uint32_t id = timer != nullptr ? timer->Handle() : 0;
		pisex::RemoveTimer(timer);
		Check(KillCount(id) == 1, "RemoveTimer kills the engine timer in cycle " + std::to_string(i));
	}

	// Fire path - the object is freed by Poll() and its address is reused by the next timer.
	for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) {
		int runs = 0;
		pisex::CTimer* timer = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [&runs] {
			++runs;
			return -1.0f;
		});
		Check(timer != nullptr, "stop-cycle timer created");
		const uint32_t id = timer != nullptr ? timer->Handle() : 0;
		FireEngineTimer(id);
		Check(runs == 1, "stop-cycle callback ran (cycle " + std::to_string(i) + ")");
		Check(timer != nullptr && !timer->IsAlive(), "stop-cycle timer stopped (cycle " + std::to_string(i) + ")");
		pisex::Poll(); // frees the object; its address becomes the next allocation's
		Check(KillCount(id) == 1, "stopped timer was killed (cycle " + std::to_string(i) + ")");
	}

	ResetEngine();
}

// Timers survive a map change (Pisex semantics - the admin core's expiry timer relies on it), but
// their callbacks must not run while no map is up: s2sdk's client list is torn down in that window
// and a ported callback almost always touches players (a timer that renames a player reaches
// Player::SetName on a clientless slot, which crashes). The fire is postponed and the
// timer re-armed with one tick on the first ready frame. NextFrame behaves the same way.
void TestMapChangePostponement() {
	InstallEngine();

	// Normalise the lifecycle: end any map, then start a fresh one.
	pisex::OnMapEndNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "no map is ready after a map end");
	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "the map start alone does not grant readiness (no update yet)");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(pisex::IsGameReady(), "the first update after the map start is ready");

	int runs = 0;
	pisex::CTimer* timer = pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [&runs] {
		++runs;
		return 1.0f;
	});
	Check(timer != nullptr, "timer created on a ready map");
	const uint32_t id = timer != nullptr ? timer->Handle() : 0;
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	Check(runs == 1, "the callback runs while the map is up");
	pisex::Poll(); // applies the reschedule

	// The map ends. The engine keeps firing our Repeat timer; no callback may run.
	pisex::OnMapEndNotify();
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "the map end disables client/entity access");
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	Check(runs == 1, "a fire during the map change is postponed (the callback does not run)");
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "the fires did not make the library ready");
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(runs == 1, "a Poll during the map change does not run the callback");
	Check(!pisex::IsGameReady(), "a Poll during the map change does not re-enable readiness");
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	Check(runs == 1, "still postponed several frames into the map change");

	bool nextFrameRan = false;
	pisex::NextFrame([&nextFrameRan] { nextFrameRan = true; });
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(!nextFrameRan, "NextFrame waits for a ready frame");

	// The new map is up: the postponed timer is re-armed with one tick, then fires normally.
	pisex::OnMapStartNotify();
	pisex::Poll();
	Check(pisex::IsGameReady(), "ready again after the new map start");
	Check(RescheduledWith(id, pisex::kMinTimerDelay), "the postponed timer is re-armed with one tick");
	Check(nextFrameRan, "NextFrame runs on the first ready frame");
	FireEngineTimer(id);
	Check(runs == 2, "the postponed callback runs on the new map");
	pisex::Poll();
	pisex::RemoveTimer(timer);

	ResetEngine();
}

// Without the bindings nothing may be created, and every entry point stays a no-op.
void TestWithoutBindings() {
	ResetEngine();
	Check(pisex::CreateTimer(1.0f, [] { return -1.0f; }) == nullptr, "CreateTimer degrades to nullptr");
	pisex::NextFrame([] {});
	pisex::Poll();
	pisex::Shutdown();
	Check(true, "Poll/Shutdown without bindings are safe");
}

} // namespace

int main() {
	std::printf("pisexcompat timer engine tests (fake s2sdk timer bindings)\n");

	TestWithoutBindings();
	TestCreateAndRescheduleClamp();
	TestOneShotIsKilled();
	TestRecycledAddresses();
	TestRemoveFromInsideCallback();
	TestMapChangePostponement();
	TestShutdownFromInsideCallback();
	TestWithoutBindings();

	std::printf("%d checks, %d failures\n", g_checks, g_failures);
	return g_failures == 0 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

`libs/plgdb/include/plgdb/db.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once
// plgdb — async MySQL/SQLite access for Plugify C++ plugins (static library, linked into each plugin).
//
// Threading contract:
//   * Query()/Transaction() may be called from the game thread only; they never block.
//   * Each Database owns one worker thread that runs statements in FIFO order.
//   * Callbacks NEVER run on the worker thread: completed results are queued and executed
//     by Poll(), which the plugin calls from the game thread (e.g. OnPluginUpdate).
//   * QuerySync() blocks the caller; use it only for startup/migrations/tests.
//
// SQL contract:
//   * Parameters are bound with '?' placeholders for both drivers (real prepared statements,
//     no string interpolation). Never build SQL from user data.
//   * Value maps to SQL as: monostate -> NULL, int64_t -> BIGINT/INTEGER, double -> DOUBLE/REAL,
//     std::string -> TEXT/BLOB (binary-safe).

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <optional>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <utility>
#include <variant>
#include <vector>

namespace plgdb {

enum class Driver { MySQL, SQLite };

struct Config {
	Driver driver = Driver::SQLite;
	// MySQL
	std::string host = "127.0.0.1";
	uint16_t port = 3306;
	std::string user;
	std::string password;
	std::string database;
	std::string charset = "utf8mb4";
	unsigned connectTimeoutSec = 5;
	// SQLite
	std::string sqlitePath; // file path; ":memory:" allowed for tests
	// Both
	unsigned maxReconnectAttempts = 1; // per statement, on lost connection
};

using Value = std::variant<std::monostate, int64_t, double, std::string>;
using Params = std::vector<Value>;

class Result {
public:
	bool Ok() const noexcept { return error.empty(); }
	const std::string& Error() const noexcept { return error; }

	size_t RowCount() const noexcept { return rows.size(); }
	size_t ColumnCount() const noexcept { return columns.size(); }
	const std::vector<std::string>& Columns() const noexcept { return columns; }
	std::optional<size_t> ColumnIndex(std::string_view name) const noexcept;

	const Value& At(size_t row, size_t col) const; // throws std::out_of_range
	bool IsNull(size_t row, size_t col) const;
	int64_t GetInt(size_t row, size_t col, int64_t def = 0) const;
	double GetDouble(size_t row, size_t col, double def = 0.0) const;
	std::string GetString(size_t row, size_t col, std::string def = {}) const;

	uint64_t AffectedRows() const noexcept { return affectedRows; }
	uint64_t InsertId() const noexcept { return insertId; }

	// Filled by the implementation.
	std::string error;
	std::vector<std::string> columns;
	std::vector<std::vector<Value>> rows;
	uint64_t affectedRows = 0;
	uint64_t insertId = 0;
};

using Callback = std::function<void(const Result&)>;

struct Statement {
	std::string sql;
	Params params;
};

class Database {
public:
	// Connects lazily on the worker thread; returns nullptr only for an invalid config.
	static std::unique_ptr<Database> Create(const Config& config);
	virtual ~Database() = default; // flushes pending work, joins the worker

	virtual Driver GetDriver() const noexcept = 0;

	virtual void Query(std::string sql, Params params, Callback callback = {}) = 0;
	// All statements in one transaction; on the first error everything is rolled back and the
	// callback receives that error. On success the callback receives the LAST statement's result.
	// A lost connection never reconnects in the middle of a transaction (the new session would
	// be in autocommit mode and the caller would get a false success): the transaction is
	// redone from the start while nothing has completed, otherwise the callback gets the error.
	virtual void Transaction(std::vector<Statement> statements, Callback callback = {}) = 0;

	virtual Result QuerySync(std::string sql, Params params = {}) = 0;

	// Runs completed callbacks on the calling thread. Returns how many ran.
	virtual size_t Poll() = 0;

	// Number of statements queued or running on the worker.
	virtual size_t Pending() const noexcept = 0;
};

} // namespace plgdb

```

`libs/plgdb/src/database.cpp`:

```cpp
// plgdb: worker thread, FIFO queue, completion queue and the Database factory.

#include "internal.hpp"

#include <exception>
#include <utility>

namespace plgdb::detail {

namespace {

std::mutex g_loggerMutex;
std::function<void(std::string_view)> g_logger;

} // namespace

void SetLogger(std::function<void(std::string_view)> logger) {
	std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_loggerMutex);
	g_logger = std::move(logger);
}

void Log(std::string_view message) {
	std::function<void(std::string_view)> logger;
	{
		std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_loggerMutex);
		logger = g_logger;
	}
	if (logger) {
		try {
			logger(message);
		} catch (...) {
			// A logger must never take the database down.
		}
	}
}

DatabaseBase::~DatabaseBase() {
	StopWorker();
}

void DatabaseBase::StartWorker() {
	std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(queueMutex_);
	if (started_) return;
	started_ = true;
	worker_ = std::thread([this] { WorkerMain(); });
}

size_t DatabaseBase::Pending() const noexcept {
	return pending_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
}

void DatabaseBase::StopWorker() {
	{
		std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(queueMutex_);
		if (!worker_.joinable()) return; // already stopped (or never started)
		stopping_ = true;
	}
	queueCv_.notify_all();
	worker_.join();

	// Drop callbacks whose results arrived but were never polled. Per contract
	// they are discarded without being called.
	std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(completionMutex_);
	completions_.clear();
}

void DatabaseBase::Query(std::string sql, Params params, Callback callback) {
	Job job;
	job.sql = std::move(sql);
	job.params = std::move(params);
	job.callback = std::move(callback);
	{
		std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(queueMutex_);
		if (stopping_) return; // shutting down: silently drop the job
		queue_.push_back(std::move(job));
		pending_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
	}
	queueCv_.notify_one();
}

void DatabaseBase::Transaction(std::vector<Statement> statements, Callback callback) {
	Job job;
	job.isTransaction = true;
	job.statements = std::move(statements);
	job.callback = std::move(callback);
	{
		std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(queueMutex_);
		if (stopping_) return; // shutting down: silently drop the job
		queue_.push_back(std::move(job));
		pending_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
	}
	queueCv_.notify_one();
}

Result DatabaseBase::QuerySync(std::string sql, Params params) {
	auto slot = std::make_shared<SyncSlot>();
	{
		std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(queueMutex_);
		if (stopping_) {
			Result result;
			result.error = "plgdb: database is shutting down";
			return result;
		}
		Job job;
		job.sql = std::move(sql);
		job.params = std::move(params);
		job.sync = slot;
		queue_.push_back(std::move(job));
		pending_.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
	}
	queueCv_.notify_one();

	// Safe to wait here even if Poll() is never called: the worker completes the
	// job independently. Calling QuerySync from inside a Poll() callback cannot
	// deadlock either — callbacks run on the caller thread, not on the worker.
	std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(slot->mutex);
	slot->cv.wait(lock, [&slot] { return slot->done; });
	return slot->result;
}

size_t DatabaseBase::Poll() {
	std::deque<Completion> batch;
	{
		std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(completionMutex_);
		batch.swap(completions_);
	}

	size_t ran = 0;
	for (Completion& completion : batch) {
		if (!completion.callback) continue;
		try {
			completion.callback(completion.result);
		} catch (const std::exception& e) {
			Log(std::string("plgdb: exception thrown by callback: ") + e.what());
		} catch (...) {
			Log("plgdb: unknown exception thrown by callback");
		}
		++ran;
	}
	return ran;
}

void DatabaseBase::WorkerMain() {
	for (;;) {
		Job job;
		{
			std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(queueMutex_);
			queueCv_.wait(lock, [this] { return stopping_ || !queue_.empty(); });
			if (queue_.empty()) break; // stopping_ && nothing left to flush
			job = std::move(queue_.front());
			queue_.pop_front();
		}

		Result result = RunJob(job);
		pending_.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);

		if (job.sync) {
			{
				std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(job.sync->mutex);
				job.sync->result = std::move(result);
				job.sync->done = true;
			}
			job.sync->cv.notify_all();
		} else if (job.callback) {
			std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(completionMutex_);
			completions_.push_back(Completion{std::move(job.callback), std::move(result)});
		}
	}
}

Result DatabaseBase::RunJob(const Job& job) noexcept {
	try {
		if (job.isTransaction) return OnTransaction(job.statements);
		return OnQuery(job.sql, job.params);
	} catch (const std::exception& e) {
		Result result;
		result.error = std::string("plgdb: unhandled exception on worker thread: ") + e.what();
		Log(result.error);
		return result;
	} catch (...) {
		Result result;
		result.error = "plgdb: unhandled unknown exception on worker thread";
		Log(result.error);
		return result;
	}
}

} // namespace plgdb::detail

namespace plgdb {

std::unique_ptr<Database> Database::Create(const Config& config) {
	try {
		switch (config.driver) {
		case Driver::MySQL:
			if (config.host.empty() || config.database.empty()) return nullptr;
			return detail::MakeMySQLDatabase(config);
		case Driver::SQLite:
			if (config.sqlitePath.empty()) return nullptr;
			return detail::MakeSQLiteDatabase(config);
		}
	} catch (const std::exception& e) {
		// Never let construction (e.g. a failed thread spawn) throw into plugin code.
		detail::Log(std::string("plgdb: Database::Create failed: ") + e.what());
	} catch (...) {
		detail::Log("plgdb: Database::Create failed with an unknown exception");
	}
	return nullptr;
}

} // namespace plgdb
```

`libs/plgdb/src/internal.hpp`:

```hpp
#pragma once
// plgdb internals: shared worker/queue base class and driver factories.
// NOT a public header — the public API is <plgdb/db.hpp> only.

#include <plgdb/db.hpp>

#include <atomic>
#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstddef>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace plgdb::detail {

// Optional logging hook for internal diagnostics (worker-side exceptions,
// exceptions thrown by user callbacks, reconnects). Thread-safe; pass an empty
// std::function to clear it. Never called with the completion lock held.
void SetLogger(std::function<void(std::string_view)> logger);
void Log(std::string_view message);

// Common plumbing for both drivers:
//   * one worker thread started by StartWorker() (called from the concrete
//     driver's constructor, after its own members exist),
//   * FIFO job queue (mutex + condvar),
//   * completion queue drained by Poll() on the caller thread,
//   * StopWorker(): stop accepting work, drain the queue (flush), join, then
//     discard completions that were never polled (those callbacks are dropped
//     without being called).
class DatabaseBase : public Database {
public:
	explicit DatabaseBase(Config config) : config_(std::move(config)) {}
	~DatabaseBase() override;

	void Query(std::string sql, Params params, Callback callback) override;
	void Transaction(std::vector<Statement> statements, Callback callback) override;
	Result QuerySync(std::string sql, Params params) override;
	size_t Poll() override;
	size_t Pending() const noexcept override;

protected:
	const Config& config() const noexcept { return config_; }

	// Idempotent. Starting with no jobs queued and stopping with an empty queue
	// are both no-ops.
	void StartWorker();
	void StopWorker();

	// Called on the worker thread only. Implementations must not let exceptions
	// escape (DatabaseBase catches anyway, but Result.error is the contract).
	virtual Result OnQuery(const std::string& sql, const Params& params) = 0;
	virtual Result OnTransaction(const std::vector<Statement>& statements) = 0;

private:
	struct SyncSlot {
		std::mutex mutex;
		std::condition_variable cv;
		bool done = false;
		Result result;
	};

	struct Job {
		bool isTransaction = false;
		std::string sql;
		Params params;
		std::vector<Statement> statements;
		Callback callback;
		std::shared_ptr<SyncSlot> sync; // QuerySync: result goes here, no callback
	};

	struct Completion {
		Callback callback;
		Result result;
	};

	void WorkerMain();
	Result RunJob(const Job& job) noexcept;

	Config config_;
	std::thread worker_;
	std::mutex queueMutex_;
	std::condition_variable queueCv_;
	std::deque<Job> queue_;
	bool stopping_ = false; // guarded by queueMutex_
	bool started_ = false;  // guarded by queueMutex_
	std::mutex completionMutex_;
	std::deque<Completion> completions_;
	std::atomic<size_t> pending_{0};
};

std::unique_ptr<Database> MakeMySQLDatabase(const Config& config);
std::unique_ptr<Database> MakeSQLiteDatabase(const Config& config);

} // namespace plgdb::detail

```

`libs/plgdb/src/mysql_db.cpp`:

```cpp
// plgdb MySQL driver: MariaDB Connector/C, real prepared statements on a worker thread.

#include "internal.hpp"

#include <mariadb/errmsg.h>
#include <mariadb/mysql.h>

#include <charconv>
#include <cstring>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

#ifndef MYSQL_DATA_TRUNCATED
#define MYSQL_DATA_TRUNCATED 101
#endif

namespace plgdb::detail {

namespace {

using StmtPtr = std::unique_ptr<MYSQL_STMT, decltype(&mysql_stmt_close)>;

std::string ConnErrorString(MYSQL* conn) {
	const unsigned int code = mysql_errno(conn);
	const char* msg = mysql_error(conn);
	return "plgdb(mysql): error " + std::to_string(code) + ": " + (msg && *msg ? msg : "unknown error");
}

std::string StmtErrorString(MYSQL_STMT* stmt) {
	const unsigned int code = mysql_stmt_errno(stmt);
	const char* state = mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt);
	const char* msg = mysql_stmt_error(stmt);
	std::string out = "plgdb(mysql): error " + std::to_string(code);
	if (state && *state && std::strcmp(state, "00000") != 0) {
		out += " (";
		out += state;
		out += ")";
	}
	out += ": ";
	out += (msg && *msg) ? msg : "unknown error";
	return out;
}

// Client-side codes >= 2000 plus SQLSTATE class 08 (connection exception).
bool IsConnectionError(unsigned int code, const char* sqlstate) {
	switch (code) {
	case CR_SERVER_GONE_ERROR: // 2006
	case CR_SERVER_LOST:       // 2013
	case CR_CONNECTION_ERROR:  // 2002
	case CR_CONN_HOST_ERROR:   // 2003
	case CR_UNKNOWN_HOST:      // 2005
	case 2055:                 // CR_SERVER_LOST_EXTENDED
		return true;
	default:
		break;
	}
	return sqlstate != nullptr && sqlstate[0] == '0' && sqlstate[1] == '8';
}

// Result columns are fetched as text (binary protocol + MYSQL_TYPE_STRING
// conversion, buffers sized from STMT_ATTR_UPDATE_MAX_LENGTH / fetch_column).
// Integers become int64_t, floating point and DECIMAL become double (DECIMAL is
// lossy for values that need more than double precision), everything else stays
// binary-safe text with embedded NULs preserved.
Value ConvertValue(const MYSQL_FIELD& field, std::string&& text) {
	const char* begin = text.data();
	const char* end = begin + text.size();
	switch (field.type) {
	case MYSQL_TYPE_TINY:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_SHORT:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_LONG:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_LONGLONG:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_INT24:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_YEAR: {
		int64_t out = 0;
		auto [ptr, ec] = std::from_chars(begin, end, out);
		if (ec == std::errc() && ptr == end) return out;
		if ((field.flags & UNSIGNED_FLAG) != 0) {
			uint64_t uout = 0;
			auto [uptr, uec] = std::from_chars(begin, end, uout);
			if (uec == std::errc() && uptr == end && uout <= static_cast<uint64_t>(std::numeric_limits<int64_t>::max())) {
				return static_cast<int64_t>(uout);
			}
		}
		return text; // out of int64 range: expose the value as text
	}
	case MYSQL_TYPE_FLOAT:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_DOUBLE:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_DECIMAL:
	case MYSQL_TYPE_NEWDECIMAL: {
		double out = 0.0;
		auto [ptr, ec] = std::from_chars(begin, end, out);
		if (ec == std::errc() && ptr == end) return out;
		return text;
	}
	default:
		return text;
	}
}

class MySQLDatabase final : public DatabaseBase {
public:
	explicit MySQLDatabase(const Config& config) : DatabaseBase(config) { StartWorker(); }
	~MySQLDatabase() override {
		StopWorker();
		CloseConnection();
	}

	Driver GetDriver() const noexcept override { return Driver::MySQL; }

protected:
	Result OnQuery(const std::string& sql, const Params& params) override {
		return RunStatement(sql, params, /*allowReconnect=*/true, nullptr);
	}

	Result OnTransaction(const std::vector<Statement>& statements) override {
		unsigned restarts = 0;
		for (;;) {
			Result begin = RunStatement("START TRANSACTION", {}, /*allowReconnect=*/true, nullptr);
			if (!begin.Ok()) return begin;

			bool restart = false;
			bool partial = false; // a data statement already ran: never retry after this
			Result last;
			for (const Statement& statement : statements) {
				bool lost = false;
				// Never reconnect inside the transaction: the fresh connection would be in
				// autocommit mode, so the statements after it would commit on their own while
				// the caller still sees one atomic unit. A lost connection is handled by the
				// restart path below, which redoes BEGIN plus the statements (only possible
				// while nothing has completed).
				Result result = RunStatement(statement.sql, statement.params, /*allowReconnect=*/false, &lost);
				if (!result.Ok()) {
					// The transaction is dead either way; the rollback is best effort
					// (it fails too if the connection dropped).
					RunStatement("ROLLBACK", {}, /*allowReconnect=*/false, nullptr);
					if (lost && !partial && restarts < config().maxReconnectAttempts) {
						++restarts;
						restart = true; // nothing was done yet: safe to redo from BEGIN
					}
					last = std::move(result);
					break;
				}
				partial = true;
				last = std::move(result);
			}
			if (restart) {
				Log("plgdb(mysql): connection lost before any work, restarting transaction");
				continue;
			}
			if (!last.Ok()) return last;

			Result commit = RunStatement("COMMIT", {}, /*allowReconnect=*/false, nullptr);
			if (!commit.Ok()) {
				RunStatement("ROLLBACK", {}, /*allowReconnect=*/false, nullptr);
				return commit;
			}
			return last;
		}
	}

private:
	// Retries the statement after reconnecting up to config().maxReconnectAttempts
	// times when the failure is a lost/unavailable connection.
	Result RunStatement(const std::string& sql, const Params& params, bool allowReconnect, bool* connLostOut) {
		unsigned attempts = 0;
		for (;;) {
			if (conn_ == nullptr) {
				std::string err;
				if (!EnsureConnected(err)) {
					if (connLostOut) *connLostOut = true;
					if (!allowReconnect || attempts >= config().maxReconnectAttempts) {
						Result result;
						result.error = err;
						return result;
					}
					++attempts;
					continue;
				}
			}

			bool lost = false;
			Result result = RunStatementOnce(sql, params, lost);
			if (connLostOut) *connLostOut = lost;
			if (result.Ok() || !lost) return result;

			Log("plgdb(mysql): lost connection, reconnecting");
			CloseConnection();
			if (!allowReconnect || attempts >= config().maxReconnectAttempts) return result;
			++attempts;
		}
	}

	Result RunStatementOnce(const std::string& sql, const Params& params, bool& connLost) {
		Result result;
		connLost = false;

		if (sql.empty()) {
			result.error = "plgdb(mysql): empty statement";
			return result;
		}

		MYSQL_STMT* raw = mysql_stmt_init(conn_);
		if (raw == nullptr) {
			result.error = ConnErrorString(conn_);
			connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_errno(conn_), mysql_sqlstate(conn_));
			return result;
		}
		StmtPtr stmt(raw, mysql_stmt_close);

		// Ask the connector to keep MYSQL_FIELD::max_length up to date so result
		// buffers can be sized exactly after mysql_stmt_store_result().
		my_bool updateMaxLength = 1;
		mysql_stmt_attr_set(stmt.get(), STMT_ATTR_UPDATE_MAX_LENGTH, &updateMaxLength);

		if (mysql_stmt_prepare(stmt.get(), sql.data(), static_cast<unsigned long>(sql.size())) != 0) {
			result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
			connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
			return result;
		}

		const unsigned long paramCount = mysql_stmt_param_count(stmt.get());
		if (paramCount != params.size()) {
			result.error = "plgdb(mysql): statement expects " + std::to_string(paramCount) +
			               " parameters, " + std::to_string(params.size()) + " given";
			return result;
		}

		// The connector keeps a reference to the parameter bind array and to every
		// buffer it points at, so all of these must outlive mysql_stmt_execute().
		std::vector<MYSQL_BIND> paramBinds;
		std::vector<my_bool> paramNulls;
		std::vector<unsigned long> paramLengths;
		std::vector<int64_t> paramInts;
		std::vector<double> paramDoubles;
		std::vector<std::string> paramStrings;

		if (paramCount > 0) {
			paramBinds.resize(paramCount);
			paramNulls.assign(paramCount, 0);
			paramLengths.assign(paramCount, 0);
			paramInts.assign(paramCount, 0);
			paramDoubles.assign(paramCount, 0.0);
			paramStrings.reserve(paramCount); // keeps element addresses stable below

			for (size_t i = 0; i < params.size(); ++i) {
				MYSQL_BIND& bind = paramBinds[i];
				std::memset(&bind, 0, sizeof(bind));
				bind.is_null = &paramNulls[i];

				const Value& value = params[i];
				if (std::holds_alternative<std::monostate>(value)) {
					bind.buffer_type = MYSQL_TYPE_NULL;
				} else if (const auto* asInt = std::get_if<int64_t>(&value)) {
					paramInts[i] = *asInt;
					bind.buffer_type = MYSQL_TYPE_LONGLONG;
					bind.buffer = &paramInts[i];
					bind.buffer_length = sizeof(int64_t);
					bind.is_unsigned = 0;
				} else if (const auto* asDouble = std::get_if<double>(&value)) {
					paramDoubles[i] = *asDouble;
					bind.buffer_type = MYSQL_TYPE_DOUBLE;
					bind.buffer = &paramDoubles[i];
					bind.buffer_length = sizeof(double);
				} else {
					paramStrings.push_back(std::get<std::string>(value));
					const std::string& text = paramStrings.back();
					// Binary-safe: the length is always explicit, never strlen.
					// Strings are sent with the connection charset (so utf8mb4 text
					// into utf8mb4 columns needs no conversion); very large values
					// go as BLOB to avoid the 16-bit VARCHAR length class.
					bind.buffer_type = text.size() > 65535 ? MYSQL_TYPE_LONG_BLOB : MYSQL_TYPE_STRING;
					bind.buffer = const_cast<char*>(text.data());
					bind.buffer_length = static_cast<unsigned long>(text.size());
					bind.length = &paramLengths[i];
					paramLengths[i] = static_cast<unsigned long>(text.size());
				}
			}

			if (mysql_stmt_bind_param(stmt.get(), paramBinds.data()) != 0) {
				result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
				connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
				return result;
			}
		}

		if (mysql_stmt_execute(stmt.get()) != 0) {
			result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
			connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
			return result;
		}

		MYSQL_RES* rawMeta = mysql_stmt_result_metadata(stmt.get());
		if (rawMeta == nullptr) {
			if (mysql_stmt_field_count(stmt.get()) != 0) {
				result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
				connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
				return result;
			}
			const my_ulonglong affected = mysql_stmt_affected_rows(stmt.get());
			result.affectedRows = (affected == static_cast<my_ulonglong>(-1)) ? 0 : static_cast<uint64_t>(affected);
			result.insertId = mysql_stmt_insert_id(stmt.get());
			return result;
		}
		std::unique_ptr<MYSQL_RES, decltype(&mysql_free_result)> meta(rawMeta, mysql_free_result);

		// store_result guarantees every row is available and makes
		// mysql_stmt_fetch_column for oversized values cheap and reliable.
		if (mysql_stmt_store_result(stmt.get()) != 0) {
			result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
			connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
			return result;
		}

		const unsigned int fieldCount = mysql_num_fields(meta.get());
		MYSQL_FIELD* fields = mysql_fetch_fields(meta.get());

		result.columns.reserve(fieldCount);
		for (unsigned int i = 0; i < fieldCount; ++i) {
			result.columns.emplace_back(fields[i].name, fields[i].name_length);
		}

		struct ColumnBuffer {
			std::vector<char> text;
			unsigned long length = 0;
			my_bool isNull = 0;
			my_bool truncated = 0;
		};
		std::vector<ColumnBuffer> colBuffers(fieldCount);
		std::vector<MYSQL_BIND> resultBinds(fieldCount);
		for (unsigned int i = 0; i < fieldCount; ++i) {
			// max_length is filled in by store_result(); fall back to a modest
			// buffer and let the fetch_column path handle anything longer.
			const unsigned long maxLength = fields[i].max_length;
			const size_t size = maxLength > 0 ? maxLength : 256;
			colBuffers[i].text.resize(size);
			MYSQL_BIND& bind = resultBinds[i];
			std::memset(&bind, 0, sizeof(bind));
			bind.buffer_type = MYSQL_TYPE_STRING; // convert everything to text
			bind.buffer = colBuffers[i].text.data();
			bind.buffer_length = size;
			bind.length = &colBuffers[i].length;
			bind.is_null = &colBuffers[i].isNull;
			bind.error = &colBuffers[i].truncated;
		}
		if (mysql_stmt_bind_result(stmt.get(), resultBinds.data()) != 0) {
			result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
			connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
			return result;
		}

		for (;;) {
			const int rc = mysql_stmt_fetch(stmt.get());
			if (rc == MYSQL_NO_DATA) break;
			if (rc != 0 && rc != MYSQL_DATA_TRUNCATED) {
				result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
				connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
				result.rows.clear();
				return result;
			}

			std::vector<Value> row;
			row.reserve(fieldCount);
			for (unsigned int i = 0; i < fieldCount; ++i) {
				ColumnBuffer& buffer = colBuffers[i];
				if (buffer.isNull) {
					row.emplace_back(std::monostate{});
					continue;
				}
				if (buffer.truncated || buffer.length > buffer.text.size()) {
					// Long data: pull the full column value.
					std::string full;
					full.resize(buffer.length);
					MYSQL_BIND fetchBind;
					std::memset(&fetchBind, 0, sizeof(fetchBind));
					unsigned long fetched = buffer.length;
					my_bool fetchNull = 0;
					my_bool fetchError = 0;
					fetchBind.buffer_type = MYSQL_TYPE_STRING;
					fetchBind.buffer = full.data();
					fetchBind.buffer_length = buffer.length;
					fetchBind.length = &fetched;
					fetchBind.is_null = &fetchNull;
					fetchBind.error = &fetchError;
					if (mysql_stmt_fetch_column(stmt.get(), &fetchBind, i, 0) != 0 || fetchNull) {
						result.error = StmtErrorString(stmt.get());
						connLost = IsConnectionError(mysql_stmt_errno(stmt.get()), mysql_stmt_sqlstate(stmt.get()));
						result.rows.clear();
						return result;
					}
					full.resize(fetched);
					row.push_back(ConvertValue(fields[i], std::move(full)));
				} else {
					std::string text(buffer.text.data(), buffer.length);
					row.push_back(ConvertValue(fields[i], std::move(text)));
				}
			}
			result.rows.push_back(std::move(row));
		}

		const my_ulonglong affected = mysql_stmt_affected_rows(stmt.get());
		result.affectedRows = (affected == static_cast<my_ulonglong>(-1)) ? 0 : static_cast<uint64_t>(affected);
		result.insertId = mysql_stmt_insert_id(stmt.get());
		return result;
	}

	bool EnsureConnected(std::string& errOut) {
		if (conn_ != nullptr) return true;

		MYSQL* handle = mysql_init(nullptr);
		if (handle == nullptr) {
			errOut = "plgdb(mysql): mysql_init failed (out of memory)";
			return false;
		}

		unsigned int timeout = config().connectTimeoutSec;
		if (timeout == 0) timeout = 5;
		mysql_options(handle, MYSQL_OPT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, &timeout);
		mysql_options(handle, MYSQL_OPT_READ_TIMEOUT, &timeout);
		mysql_options(handle, MYSQL_OPT_WRITE_TIMEOUT, &timeout);
		if (!config().charset.empty()) {
			mysql_options(handle, MYSQL_SET_CHARSET_NAME, config().charset.c_str());
		}

		if (mysql_real_connect(handle, config().host.c_str(), config().user.c_str(), config().password.c_str(),
		                       config().database.c_str(), config().port, nullptr, 0) == nullptr) {
			errOut = ConnErrorString(handle);
			mysql_close(handle);
			return false;
		}

		conn_ = handle;
		Log("plgdb(mysql): connected to " + config().host + ":" + std::to_string(config().port) + "/" + config().database);
		return true;
	}

	void CloseConnection() {
		if (conn_ == nullptr) return;
		mysql_close(conn_);
		conn_ = nullptr;
	}

	MYSQL* conn_ = nullptr; // owned by the worker thread
};

} // namespace

std::unique_ptr<Database> MakeMySQLDatabase(const Config& config) {
	return std::make_unique<MySQLDatabase>(config);
}

} // namespace plgdb::detail
```

```cpp
#include <plgdb/db.hpp>

#include <stdexcept>

namespace plgdb {

std::optional<size_t> Result::ColumnIndex(std::string_view name) const noexcept {
	for (size_t i = 0; i < columns.size(); ++i) {
		if (columns[i] == name) return i;
	}
	return std::nullopt;
}

const Value& Result::At(size_t row, size_t col) const {
	if (row >= rows.size() || col >= rows[row].size()) throw std::out_of_range("plgdb::Result::At");
	return rows[row][col];
}

bool Result::IsNull(size_t row, size_t col) const {
	return std::holds_alternative<std::monostate>(At(row, col));
}

int64_t Result::GetInt(size_t row, size_t col, int64_t def) const {
	const Value& v = At(row, col);
	if (auto p = std::get_if<int64_t>(&v)) return *p;
	if (auto p = std::get_if<double>(&v)) return static_cast<int64_t>(*p);
	if (auto p = std::get_if<std::string>(&v)) {
		try { return std::stoll(*p); } catch (...) { return def; }
	}
	return def;
}

double Result::GetDouble(size_t row, size_t col, double def) const {
	const Value& v = At(row, col);
	if (auto p = std::get_if<double>(&v)) return *p;
	if (auto p = std::get_if<int64_t>(&v)) return static_cast<double>(*p);
	if (auto p = std::get_if<std::string>(&v)) {
		try { return std::stod(*p); } catch (...) { return def; }
	}
	return def;
}

std::string Result::GetString(size_t row, size_t col, std::string def) const {
	const Value& v = At(row, col);
	if (auto p = std::get_if<std::string>(&v)) return *p;
	if (auto p = std::get_if<int64_t>(&v)) return std::to_string(*p);
	if (auto p = std::get_if<double>(&v)) return std::to_string(*p);
	return def;
}

} // namespace plgdb
```

`libs/plgdb/src/sqlite_db.cpp`:

```cpp
// plgdb SQLite driver: sqlite3, prepared statements on a worker thread.

#include "internal.hpp"

#include <sqlite3.h>

#include <cctype>
#include <cstring>
#include <filesystem>
#include <system_error>
#include <memory>
#include <string>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

namespace plgdb::detail {

namespace {

using StmtPtr = std::unique_ptr<sqlite3_stmt, decltype(&sqlite3_finalize)>;

bool IsMemoryPath(const std::string& path) {
	return path == ":memory:" || path.rfind("file::memory:", 0) == 0;
}

class SQLiteDatabase final : public DatabaseBase {
public:
	explicit SQLiteDatabase(const Config& config) : DatabaseBase(config) { StartWorker(); }
	~SQLiteDatabase() override {
		StopWorker();
		Close();
	}

	Driver GetDriver() const noexcept override { return Driver::SQLite; }

protected:
	Result OnQuery(const std::string& sql, const Params& params) override {
		Result result;
		std::string err;
		if (!EnsureOpen(err)) {
			result.error = err;
			return result;
		}
		return Exec(sql, params);
	}

	Result OnTransaction(const std::vector<Statement>& statements) override {
		Result result;
		std::string err;
		if (!EnsureOpen(err)) {
			result.error = err;
			return result;
		}

		Result begun = Exec("BEGIN", {});
		if (!begun.Ok()) return begun;

		Result last;
		for (const Statement& statement : statements) {
			Result current = Exec(statement.sql, statement.params);
			if (!current.Ok()) {
				Rollback();
				return current;
			}
			last = std::move(current);
		}

		Result committed = Exec("COMMIT", {});
		if (!committed.Ok()) {
			Rollback();
			return committed;
		}
		return last;
	}

private:
	bool EnsureOpen(std::string& errOut) {
		if (db_ != nullptr) return true;

		const std::string& path = config().sqlitePath;
		sqlite3* handle = nullptr;
		if (path != ":memory:" && path.rfind("file:", 0) != 0) {
			// Create the parent directory of a file database (plugin data dirs may not exist yet).
			std::error_code ec;
			const std::filesystem::path parent = std::filesystem::path(path).parent_path();
			if (!parent.empty()) {
				std::filesystem::create_directories(parent, ec);
			}
		}
		const int rc = sqlite3_open_v2(path.c_str(), &handle, SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE | SQLITE_OPEN_FULLMUTEX, nullptr);
		if (rc != SQLITE_OK) {
			errOut = std::string("plgdb(sqlite): cannot open ") + path + ": " + (handle ? sqlite3_errmsg(handle) : sqlite3_errstr(rc));
			if (handle != nullptr) sqlite3_close(handle);
			return false;
		}

		sqlite3_busy_timeout(handle, 5000);
		if (!IsMemoryPath(path)) {
			// WAL is persistent per database file; ignore failures (e.g. read-only
			// filesystems keep the rollback journal, which still works).
			char* message = nullptr;
			if (sqlite3_exec(handle, "PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;", nullptr, nullptr, &message) != SQLITE_OK) {
				Log(std::string("plgdb(sqlite): PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL failed: ") + (message ? message : "unknown error"));
			}
			sqlite3_free(message);
		}

		db_ = handle;
		return true;
	}

	void Close() {
		if (db_ == nullptr) return;
		sqlite3_close(db_);
		db_ = nullptr;
	}

	void Rollback() {
		if (db_ == nullptr) return;
		sqlite3_exec(db_, "ROLLBACK", nullptr, nullptr, nullptr);
	}

	Result Exec(const std::string& sql, const Params& params) {
		Result result;
		if (sql.empty()) {
			result.error = "plgdb(sqlite): empty statement";
			return result;
		}

		sqlite3_stmt* raw = nullptr;
		const char* tail = nullptr;
		const int prepareRc = sqlite3_prepare_v2(db_, sql.c_str(), static_cast<int>(sql.size()), &raw, &tail);
		if (prepareRc != SQLITE_OK) {
			result.error = std::string("plgdb(sqlite): prepare failed: ") + sqlite3_errmsg(db_);
			return result;
		}
		if (raw == nullptr) {
			result.error = "plgdb(sqlite): statement contains no SQL";
			return result;
		}
		StmtPtr stmt(raw, sqlite3_finalize);

		if (tail != nullptr) {
			for (const char* p = tail; *p != '\0'; ++p) {
				if (*p != ';' && !std::isspace(static_cast<unsigned char>(*p))) {
					result.error = "plgdb(sqlite): multiple statements in one call are not supported";
					return result;
				}
			}
		}

		const int paramCount = sqlite3_bind_parameter_count(stmt.get());
		if (paramCount != static_cast<int>(params.size())) {
			result.error = "plgdb(sqlite): statement expects " + std::to_string(paramCount) + " parameters, " +
			               std::to_string(params.size()) + " given";
			return result;
		}

		for (int i = 0; i < paramCount; ++i) {
			const Value& value = params[static_cast<size_t>(i)];
			int rc = SQLITE_OK;
			if (std::holds_alternative<std::monostate>(value)) {
				rc = sqlite3_bind_null(stmt.get(), i + 1);
			} else if (const auto* asInt = std::get_if<int64_t>(&value)) {
				rc = sqlite3_bind_int64(stmt.get(), i + 1, *asInt);
			} else if (const auto* asDouble = std::get_if<double>(&value)) {
				rc = sqlite3_bind_double(stmt.get(), i + 1, *asDouble);
			} else {
				const std::string& text = std::get<std::string>(value);
				// Explicit byte length keeps embedded NULs (binary-safe).
				rc = sqlite3_bind_text(stmt.get(), i + 1, text.data(), static_cast<int>(text.size()), SQLITE_TRANSIENT);
			}
			if (rc != SQLITE_OK) {
				result.error = std::string("plgdb(sqlite): bind failed: ") + sqlite3_errmsg(db_);
				return result;
			}
		}

		const int columnCount = sqlite3_column_count(stmt.get());
		if (columnCount > 0) {
			result.columns.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(columnCount));
			for (int i = 0; i < columnCount; ++i) {
				const char* name = sqlite3_column_name(stmt.get(), i);
				result.columns.emplace_back(name ? name : "");
			}

			for (;;) {
				const int stepRc = sqlite3_step(stmt.get());
				if (stepRc == SQLITE_DONE) break;
				if (stepRc != SQLITE_ROW) {
					result.error = std::string("plgdb(sqlite): step failed: ") + sqlite3_errmsg(db_);
					result.rows.clear();
					return result;
				}

				std::vector<Value> row;
				row.reserve(static_cast<size_t>(columnCount));
				for (int i = 0; i < columnCount; ++i) {
					switch (sqlite3_column_type(stmt.get(), i)) {
					case SQLITE_INTEGER:
						row.emplace_back(static_cast<int64_t>(sqlite3_column_int64(stmt.get(), i)));
						break;
					case SQLITE_FLOAT:
						row.emplace_back(sqlite3_column_double(stmt.get(), i));
						break;
					case SQLITE_TEXT: {
						const unsigned char* text = sqlite3_column_text(stmt.get(), i);
						const int bytes = sqlite3_column_bytes(stmt.get(), i);
						row.emplace_back(text != nullptr
						                     ? std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char*>(text), bytes > 0 ? static_cast<size_t>(bytes) : 0)
						                     : std::string());
						break;
					}
					case SQLITE_BLOB: {
						const void* blob = sqlite3_column_blob(stmt.get(), i);
						const int bytes = sqlite3_column_bytes(stmt.get(), i);
						if (blob != nullptr && bytes > 0) {
							row.emplace_back(std::string(static_cast<const char*>(blob), static_cast<size_t>(bytes)));
						} else {
							row.emplace_back(std::string());
						}
						break;
					}
					default: // SQLITE_NULL
						row.emplace_back(std::monostate{});
						break;
					}
				}
				result.rows.push_back(std::move(row));
			}
		} else {
			const int stepRc = sqlite3_step(stmt.get());
			if (stepRc != SQLITE_DONE) {
				result.error = std::string("plgdb(sqlite): step failed: ") + sqlite3_errmsg(db_);
				return result;
			}
			result.affectedRows = static_cast<uint64_t>(sqlite3_changes(db_));
			result.insertId = static_cast<uint64_t>(sqlite3_last_insert_rowid(db_));
		}
		return result;
	}

	sqlite3* db_ = nullptr; // owned by the worker thread
};

} // namespace

std::unique_ptr<Database> MakeSQLiteDatabase(const Config& config) {
	return std::make_unique<SQLiteDatabase>(config);
}

} // namespace plgdb::detail
```
